name: dsh-baton
description: Hand tasks from Claude Code, Codex or any MCP client to a local DeepSeek Harness.

readme.markdown:
English | 中文

  macOS · Windows (guide) · no Node.js needed · zero dependencies · MIT

Claude Code and Codex each hand a task to DeepSeek Harness, and its subagents build this rainy-night street in 1 h 41 min (40 s, sound on):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/72e2fdff-275e-48bc-8e5a-39ffb025a0a8

  

  

## See it run

One Codex chat starts a task, queues a follow-up, steers the running turn, and waits for all three:

  

Codex and Claude take turns in the same Harness session, and every message is labelled with who sent it:

  

More demos →

## Quick start

  

Requires DeepSeek Harness ≥ 0.2.1-rc.2 (signed in) and Claude Code or Codex. Nothing else: no Node.js, no terminal. The steps are the same on macOS and Windows.

**1. Add the plugin in Harness:** **Plugins** (插件) → **Add plugin** (添加插件) → type `dsh-baton-host` → **Install** (安装) → **Enable now** (立即启用).

Switched on, the plugin registers dsh-baton for Claude Code and Codex, for every folder, and Harness says so.

**2. Codex only, once:** Codex **Settings → Hooks** → **Trust** **dsh-baton: waiting for the Harness run**. Codex is then woken when a run ends instead of checking every 270 s. You trust it once: updates and Harness restarts do not ask again. Skip it and Codex waits with `dsh_wait` as before; the first hand-over reminds you.

**3. Check:** in a **new** Claude Code or Codex conversation, ask it to call `dsh_list_workspaces`. It lists your Harness workspaces.

That is all. If Harness says it could not register, run `npx -y dsh-baton-mcp setup` in a terminal (this needs Node.js ≥ 22.15); it does the same registration. Updating, removing and Windows details are [further down](#install-details).

## How it works

  

  

**How each client waits** (nothing to configure):
- **Claude Code** waits for a run in the background (the `wait_command` that `dsh_send` returns) and is woken once, when the run ends.
- **Codex** with the dsh-baton Stop hook trusted (from 0.6.1): after `dsh_send` it ends its turn; the hook waits for the run outside the model and, when the run ends or asks something, continues the same conversation with the result. One model request per run instead of one every 270 s.
- **Codex** without the hook waits inside `dsh_wait`, up to 270 s per call, just under its 300 s tool timeout. An unfinished wait returns only the state, so Codex calls again without summarising. Codex gets no `wait_command`: its terminal cannot wake it, so it would poll.
- Codex asks you to approve MCP tool calls: approve the `dsh-baton` tools. For unattended `codex exec` runs, add `--approve-for-me`.

**Pick a model** (from 0.6.1): just say which one, for example "hand it to DeepSeek, V4 Pro". `dsh_send` passes it as `model` (and `reasoning_effort`), matched against the models Harness lists, so a model Harness adds later works as soon as it shows up. It applies to that session only; Harness's default model stays as it was. `dsh_list_models` shows what is available.

**How a hand-over is checked** (from 0.6.0)

You don't have to take DeepSeek's word for it. Before the run, dsh-baton notes what is in the folder. When the run ends it shows exactly which files were created, changed or deleted, and runs your project's own tests itself (`npm test`, or whatever the client passes as `checks`). A second, read-only DeepSeek agent then goes through the request point by point and ends with a table: requirement, met or not, and where (file:line). Claude or GPT reads just that, sends anything missing back in one message, and opens code only where a row says "not met". Unless `cwd` names another folder, the new Harness session starts in the folder you're already working in.

  

## Token usage

**In short: hand over the big, long jobs.** A feature that spans many files, a large refactor, a whole small app: that is where it saves the most. Claude Code's own bill drops by 65–81%, and Codex gets 2 to 5 times as many tasks out of a ChatGPT Plus 5-hour window (5 times on a medium task with GPT-6 Astra).

**The honest part:** for small tasks, Codex on GPT-6.1 Sol is cheap enough that doing it alone costs less in total than handing it over, and at medium size it comes out about even. The hand-over pays off when you want Claude or GPT to plan and review, a cheaper model to do the typing, and you'd rather not keep hitting the 5-hour limit.

**Who this is for:** most of us pay for Claude or ChatGPT with a plan (Plus, Pro, Max 5x…), while DeepSeek is pay-as-you-go from a balance you top up, so every hand-over is money spent outside your plan. If your plan's limits already cover how you work, you don't need this: keep it simple and keep the money. If you're like me and keep running long, messy jobs with round after round of changes, and keep hitting the limit, a little DeepSeek spend gets you a lot more out of the plan you already pay for.

  

Cost per task at list price, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 at its peak price:

| Client · model | Task | Alone | Handed over, client only | Handed over, with DeepSeek |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code · Opus 5.5 high | Small | $1.07 | $0.37 (−65%) | $0.55 (−49%) |
| Claude Code · Opus 5.5 high | Medium | $2.13 | $0.41 (−81%) | $0.70 (−67%) |

| Codex · GPT-6 Astra high | Medium | $2.27 | $0.48 (−79%) | $0.78 (−65%) |

readme.markdown: @vibgrate/cli Local codebase intelligence for AI coding agents — graph, drift, and version-correct docs on your machine Want to help? See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) and [good first issues](https://github.com/vibgrate/cli/labels/good%20first%20issue). ```bash npx @vibgrate/cli scan # drift score + upgrade priorities npm install -D @vibgrate/cli # install for repeat runs ``` `vg` answers three questions for any repo: 1. **What is this codebase?** — A deterministic [code graph](https://vibgrate.com/graph): call trees, import paths, impact surfaces, dependency facts. 2. **How far behind is it?** — A ranked **[DriftScore](https://vibgrate.com/driftscore)** (0–100) with runtime/framework lag, dependency age and EOL proximity, and a prioritized fix list. Exposure is scored separately as a **[RiskScore](https://vibgrate.com/riskscore)**; the two together are the **[DriftRisk Index](https://vibgrate.com/driftrisk)**. The full methodology — formulas, sources, and limitations — is published as a [whitepaper](https://vibgrate.com/whitepapers/software-risk-and-drift-scoring-methodology) under CC BY 4.0 (DOI [10.5281/zenodo.21336304](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21336304)). 3. **Can we fix it here?** — [**VG Code**](#vg-code--write-the-change-not-just-the-report), a coding agent whose search tool is the code graph, not a grep — in your terminal as `vg code` and as the VG Code panel in [Vibgrate for VS Code](https://vibgrate.com/vscode) — plus `vg fix`, ranked upgrade plans it can apply. Everything runs **on your machine**. No API key, no network call, no data leaving your repo unless you explicitly push. The `vibgrate` command is an alias for `vg` — they are interchangeable. --- ## See it run A real vg scan replay — drift score, breakdown, and ranked priorities in one command. Animation plays right here on GitHub; nothing runs in your browser. ▶ Try the live, interactive CLI simulator → Step through every command (scan, build, ask, why, …) against real sample repos. --- ## Try it in 10 seconds No install, no signup: ```bash npx @vibgrate/cli scan # drift score + upgrade priorities npx @vibgrate/cli build # build the code graph npx @vibgrate/cli ask "what does AuthService do?" npx @vibgrate/cli code # a coding agent — it asks before every edit ``` Install for repeat runs: ```bash npm install -D @vibgrate/cli npx vg scan # vg is the primary command; vibgrate is an alias ``` > Local binaries live in `node_modules/.bin` — use `npx vg` (or an npm script) unless you install globally. --- ## Windows installation Windows is supported with Node.js 22 or newer. PowerShell is the preferred shell for the Windows installer: ```powershell irm https://vibgrate.com/install.ps1 | iex ``` If you prefer npm, install the CLI globally: ```powershell npm install -g @vibgrate/cli ``` For a one-off run without changing PATH, use: ```powershell npx @vibgrate/cli scan ``` A global npm install places the `vg.cmd` and `vibgrate.cmd` shims in npm's global prefix. Check the exact location with `npm config get prefix`; if `vg` is not found, add that directory to your user `PATH`, then open a new PowerShell window. Verify the installation with: ```powershell vg --help vg doctor ``` `vg doctor` is a read-only diagnostic command. If `vg` conflicts with another command on your system, use the identical `vibgrate` command instead. Command examples elsewhere in this README use POSIX path syntax; adapt paths to PowerShell on Windows. --- ## Use it with your AI assistant `vg serve` starts **[Vibgrate AI Context](https://vibgrate.com/library)** — a local-first [MCP](https://vibgrate.com/glossary/model-context-protocol) server that gives any MCP-compatible assistant (Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, Gemini CLI, …) your code map, **offline drift**, local models, and **version-correct library docs**, all from your machine (no account, nothing uploaded; thin local docs fall through to the hosted catalog unless you pass `--local`). No context-window stuffing, no hallucinated APIs. The map **keeps itself fresh**: when files change — including edits the assistant itself just made — the next tool call rebuilds it incrementally before answering, with no watcher or daemon involved. node-turborepo/serve — vg serve --http starts Vibgrate AI Context. Live simulator. Wire it up in one command: ```bash vg install # interactive: pick your assistant(s) and done vg install --all # install for every detected assistant at once ``` This writes the MCP config for your chosen tool(s) and installs a skill that teaches the assistant how to query the graph. After reloading your assistant you get graph-aware answers: call trees, impact analysis, drift findings, version-correct library docs — all from local data. The token savings are measured and published, methodology included, at [vibgrate.com/cli/benchmarks/token-savings](https://vibgrate.com/cli/benchmarks/token-savings). Browse all 21+ supported assistants and their skill descriptions at **[vibgrate.com/skills](https://vibgrate.com/skills)**. ## Cut what your assistant re-reads: context compression Every turn, your AI assistant re-sends the whole conversation — including the 20,000-line test log, the 400-row JSON payload, and the grep output it has already acted on. You pay for that context again on every step. Vibgrate CLI compresses tool output and older turns **before** they reach the model, keeps the originals retrievable on your machine, and reports what it saved. ```bash vg install claude --compress # point Claude Code at the listener and start it (undo with `vg uninstall claude`) vg savings # tokens and estimated dollars saved, …

readme.markdown:
# regintel-mcp

**Regulatory intelligence from FDA regulations.gov dockets:** who commented, what they asked for, and what changed between the draft and final guidance.

Black Swan Causal Labs · [blackswancausallabs.com](https://blackswancausallabs.com)

> **Retrieval lives in the MCP server. Judgment lives in skills. Humans sit at the checkpoints.**

| Layer | Component | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Data | `regintel-mcp` server (this repo, MIT) | **Phase 1 built.** Fetch, cache, extract, diff. No interpretation. |
| Method | skills: `submitter-taxonomy`, `comment-theming`, `draft-final-concordance` | Built |
| Orchestration | `/docket-analysis <docketId>` with 4 human checkpoints | Built; first run on FDA-2020-D-2307 |
| Output | Docket Lens explorer (reads one `analysis.json`; PolyForm Noncommercial) | **Built** for FDA-2020-D-2307 |

## Install

Python 3.11 or later.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Black-Swan-Causal-Labs/regintel-mcp.git
cd regintel-mcp
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e .
cp .env.example .env    # then paste your key into .env
```

**API key:** get a free key at <https://open.gsa.gov/api/regulationsgov/> and put it in `.env` as `REGULATIONS_GOV_API_KEY=...`. `.env` is gitignored. The key is sent only as the `X-Api-Key` header and never appears in logs, the cache or any output. `DEMO_KEY` is fine for single lookups but too rate-limited for a full corpus pull. Personal keys allow 1,000 requests/hour.

**Register with an MCP client.** MCP is an open standard, so the server works with any compatible assistant (Claude, OpenAI Codex, others). For Claude Code, from the repo directory:

```bash
claude mcp add regintel-mcp -- "$(pwd)/.venv/bin/python" -m regintel_mcp
```

When installed as a Claude plugin, `.mcp.json` starts the server from the plugin root.

## Tools

Every tool reads the local SQLite cache (`data/cache.sqlite`) first. It only touches the network on a cache miss or when called with `refresh=true`.

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `search_dockets(query, agency="FDA", docket_type?, limit=25)` | Keyword search over dockets |
| `get_docket(docket_id)` | Docket metadata and total comment count |
| `list_documents(docket_id)` | Notices, draft and final guidance, meeting material, with every file URL |
| `list_comments(docket_id, include_withdrawn=false)` | All comments, paginated internally. Flags `is_stub`, `duplicate_of` and `agency_duplicate_count` (flags only; nothing is dropped) |
| `get_comment(comment_id)` | Body, submitter fields, attachments and **extracted attachment text** |
| `build_corpus(docket_id, with_attachments=true)` | Pulls every comment and attachment into the cache. Resumable. Reports stubs, duplicates, OCR needs and failures |
| `get_guidance_text(ref)` | A guidance document (doc ID or URL) split into numbered sections |
| `diff_guidance(draft_ref, final_ref)` | Section-aligned draft-vs-final diff with paragraph changes and moved-paragraph detection |
| `export_corpus(docket_id)` | Writes `output/<docket>/corpus.jsonl` for skills and subagents |

For long pulls outside a chat: `.venv/bin/python -m regintel_mcp build-corpus FDA-2020-D-2307`.

**How the diff works:** the text layer is extracted with pdfplumber. Running headers, draft line numbers, footnotes and the table of contents are removed. Sections are split on the guidance's own Roman, letter and number headings, then matched draft→final by heading (parent-qualified first) and then by heading plus text similarity. Paragraphs are diffed within each matched section, and paragraphs that moved to a different section are labelled. Everything is deterministic: there are no model calls in the server.

API behaviour verified against the live service is recorded in [`docs/api-notes.md`](docs/api-notes.md).

## Docket Lens (the explorer)

**Docket Lens** (`explorer/template.html`) is a single page that reads one `analysis.json` and shows three linked views: who spoke, what they asked for (a themes × submitter-type heatmap that opens the verbatim requests), and what changed (draft vs final by section, with each request's call). Build a docket's copy with:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/build_analysis.py FDA-2020-D-2307
.venv/bin/python scripts/build_explorer.py FDA-2020-D-2307
```

Then open `explorer/FDA-2020-D-2307/index.html` through any static server, e.g. `python3 -m http.server --directory explorer/FDA-2020-D-2307`. The explorer is licensed separately under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (`explorer/LICENSE`, `explorer/NOTICE`).

### Hosting a Docket Lens demo (Cloudflare Pages, password-protected)

```bash
sh scripts/build_site.sh FDA-2020-D-2307
cd site && npx wrangler pages deploy public --project-name docket-lens
```

`site/functions/_middleware.js` puts HTTP Basic Auth in front of every request, including `analysis.json`. Credentials are Pages secrets, never files: `npx wrangler pages secret put DEMO_USER --project-name docket-lens`, and the same for `DEMO_PASS`. If either secret is missing, the site serves nothing (it fails closed). It is a demo gate, not access control for sensitive data.

## Status (3 Oct 2026)

- First full run: FDA-2020-D-2307 (60 comments, 1,211 requests, 4 checkpoints, human spot-check agreement 91% on 55 calls). Outputs in `output/FDA-2020-D-2307/`, decisions in `decisions/`.
- Second-docket smoke test: FDA-2021-D-0548. Retrieval and the draft/final comparison passed without changes; see `docs/smoke-test-FDA-2021-D-0548.md`.

## The concordance caveat

This tool measures **concordance, not impact.** Changes between draft and final guidance also come from FDA's internal review, ICH M14, other guidances and the evolving science. When the final text moves in the direction a commenter asked for, that does **not** show the comment caused the change. Every output from this project carries that caveat.

## License

Server: MIT (see `LICENSE`). The Explorer template is licensed separately under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0.

© 2026 Black Swan Causal Labs ·

readme.markdown:
# ScalpStream MCP server

Pay-per-call MCP server for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and any MCP client: US product recalls, US border wait times, cheapest fuel prices, air quality and a wash-sale check on your own trades, settled in USDC over x402 on Base.

An MCP server that buys small, factual datasets at call time with your own
wallet, over [x402](https://x402.org) — roughly **$0.01 a call**, no account, no
subscription, no API key anywhere in the flow.

Most MCP servers wrap an API you already hold a key for. This one pays as it
goes. The seller holds no keys either: settlement runs through a facilitator that
sponsors gas, so the only key in the system is yours, held in memory for the
lifetime of the process and never written anywhere.

**It is useful before you fund anything.** With no key configured, every paid
tool returns the free preview *and the exact quoted price*, so you can see what
you would be buying before deciding to buy it.

## Tools

| Tool | What you get |
|---|---|
| `product_recalls` | Active US recalls for a product, brand, ingredient or vehicle across FDA, NHTSA and CPSC in one query, with severity normalised onto one scale, the hazard, the remedy, and the lot numbers that tell whether a specific unit is affected. |
| `border_crossings` | US ports of entry ranked by **all-in** time — drive plus current CBP wait — per lane type. The nearest crossing is often not the fastest. |
| `cheapest_fuel` | Cheapest fuel by location and grade. Station-level for Spain, France, Italy; official regional averages for the US. |
| `air_quality` | Current AQI and pollutants anywhere in the world, an EPA-based verdict on exercising outdoors, and the cleanest window ahead. |
| `wash_sale_check` | The US wash-sale rule (IRC 1091) applied to the user's **own** trades across taxable, IRA and spouse accounts: would buying or selling a ticker on a date wash a loss, by how much, and the first safe rebuy date; or the whole ledger with adjusted basis and the year's totals. A rule calculation, not tax advice; the service keeps nothing. |
| `payment_status` | What's configured, what's been spent. Makes no network call and costs nothing. |

Withdrawn tools are listed under
[Versions](#versions).

## Install

### Docker (no toolchain needed)

The published image is `ghcr.io/dv1-321/scalpstream-mcp`. It runs as a
non-root user on a shell-less base and speaks MCP over stdin/stdout, so it needs
`-i` and nothing else:

```bash
docker run -i --rm ghcr.io/dv1-321/scalpstream-mcp:latest
```

Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) or any MCP client that takes a
command, preview-only:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "scalpstream": {
      "command": "docker",
      "args": ["run", "-i", "--rm", "ghcr.io/dv1-321/scalpstream-mcp:latest"]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add scalpstream -- docker run -i --rm ghcr.io/dv1-321/scalpstream-mcp:latest
```

To enable paid calls, put the key in the client's `env` block and forward it
with a bare `-e NAME` — the name only, so the value never appears in the
command line:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "scalpstream": {
      "command": "docker",
      "args": ["run", "-i", "--rm", "-e", "EVM_BASE_PRIVATE_KEY", "-e", "SCALPMCP_BUDGET_USD",
               "ghcr.io/dv1-321/scalpstream-mcp:latest"],
      "env": {
        "EVM_BASE_PRIVATE_KEY": "0x...",
        "SCALPMCP_BUDGET_USD": "2.00"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Each release is also tagged (`:v0.1.9` and so on) for installs that want to pin
one; the MCP registry entry pins the exact tag.

Claude Code can also take it as a plugin, which installs the same Docker
command with no secrets and bundles the `scalpstream-data` skill:

```text
/plugin marketplace add DV1-321/scalpstream-mcp
/plugin install scalpstream@scalpstream-mcp
```

Gemini CLI reads the `gemini-extension.json` at the root of this repository:

```bash
gemini extensions install https://github.com/DV1-321/scalpstream-mcp
```

Both pin the release tag and start preview-only. To pay, add the key to the
installed server's `env` as described above; never to the manifest.

### Go

```bash
go install github.com/DV1-321/scalpstream-mcp/cmd/scalpmcp@latest
```

This puts `scalpmcp` in `$(go env GOPATH)/bin`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "scalpstream": {
      "command": "scalpmcp",
      "env": {
        "EVM_BASE_PRIVATE_KEY": "0x...",
        "SCALPMCP_MAX_PRICE_USD": "0.10",
        "SCALPMCP_BUDGET_USD": "2.00"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Omit `env` entirely to run in preview-only mode.

## Configure

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `EVM_BASE_PRIVATE_KEY` | *(unset)* | Base-mainnet key holding a little USDC. Unset = preview-only. |
| `SCALPMCP_MAX_PRICE_USD` | `0.10` | Refuse any single call quoted above this. |
| `SCALPMCP_BUDGET_USD` | `2.00` | Refuse once the process has spent this much in total. |
| `SCALPMCP_FUEL_URL`, `_AIR_URL`, `_BORDER_URL`, `_RECALL_URL`, `_BASIS_URL` | the live services | Override a service origin, for testing against a stub. |

## Paying without a crypto wallet

The same data runs as Apify Actors, billed to your Apify plan instead of a
wallet. Apify's hosted MCP server exposes any Actor as a tool, so an MCP client
that cannot hold a key can reach the same lookups through it with an Apify
account:

| Data | Apify MCP link |
|---|---|
| Fuel prices | <https://mcp.apify.com?tools=rolescout/fuelscout-cheapest-fuel-prices> |
| US border waits | <https://mcp.apify.com?tools=rolescout/borderscout-us-border-wait-times> |
| US product recalls | <https://mcp.apify.com?tools=rolescout/recallscout-us-product-recalls> |

Those links authenticate with your Apify account; this server has no part in
them and never needs your Apify token.

readme.markdown:
# Apify document tools

Open-source [Apify](https://apify.com) Actors for working with business documents, audio, video, websites and domains. Run them in the cloud with no setup
from Apify Store, call them from your code, or plug them into AI agents through the Apify MCP server.

| Actor | What it does | Run it |
|---|---|---|
| [Document to Markdown for AI](document-to-markdown/) | PDF, scanned PDF and images (OCR in 11 languages incl. Ukrainian and Russian), DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, legacy Office and HTML → Markdown, JSON tables and RAG chunks | [apify.com/ai_admin/document-to-markdown](https://apify.com/ai_admin/document-to-markdown) |
| [Office to PDF & PDF/A](office-to-pdf/) | Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OpenDocument, RTF, HTML and images → PDF or archival PDF/A-2b, optional merge into one PDF | [apify.com/ai_admin/office-to-pdf](https://apify.com/ai_admin/office-to-pdf) |
| [Audio & Video Transcriber](audio-transcriber/) | Audio and video → text, timestamped segments and SRT/VTT subtitles with Whisper large-v3 (via Groq), 99 languages | [apify.com/ai_admin/audio-transcriber](https://apify.com/ai_admin/audio-transcriber) |
| [PDF to Image & Image Converter](pdf-image-converter/) | PDF pages → PNG/JPG/WebP/TIFF, images → PDF, image formats incl. iPhone HEIC, resize, ZIP | [apify.com/ai_admin/pdf-image-converter](https://apify.com/ai_admin/pdf-image-converter) |
| [Image to Text OCR](image-to-text-ocr/) | Images and scanned PDFs → text, lines and words with confidence and boxes, 38 languages incl. Ukrainian, auto-rotate | [apify.com/ai_admin/image-to-text-ocr](https://apify.com/ai_admin/image-to-text-ocr) |
| [Text to Speech](text-to-speech/) | Text, PDF and Word → MP3/WAV/OGG with SRT/VTT subtitles, 37 neural voices in 23 languages incl. 3 Ukrainian, no API key | [apify.com/ai_admin/text-to-speech](https://apify.com/ai_admin/text-to-speech) |
| [Website Screenshot & URL/HTML to PDF](website-screenshot/) | Full-page or viewport screenshots (PNG/JPEG/WebP), web pages and raw HTML → PDF, device presets, dark mode, element shots | [apify.com/ai_admin/website-screenshot](https://apify.com/ai_admin/website-screenshot) |
| [Domain WHOIS, DNS & SSL Checker](domain-whois-dns-ssl/) | Bulk RDAP/WHOIS (registrar, expiry, availability), DNS incl. MX/SPF/DMARC/CAA, SSL issuer and days left | [apify.com/ai_admin/domain-whois-dns-ssl](https://apify.com/ai_admin/domain-whois-dns-ssl) |
| [Video Frame Extractor](video-frame-extractor/) | Video → still frames: evenly spaced, every N seconds, exact timestamps, scene changes or keyframes, contact sheet | [apify.com/ai_admin/video-frame-extractor](https://apify.com/ai_admin/video-frame-extractor) |

Ready-made examples (Apify tasks): [document-to-markdown examples](https://apify.com/ai_admin/document-to-markdown/examples),
[office-to-pdf examples](https://apify.com/ai_admin/office-to-pdf/examples),
[OCR examples](https://apify.com/ai_admin/image-to-text-ocr/examples) — every Actor page has an Examples tab.

## Use from AI agents (MCP)

All Actors are available as MCP tools — hosted (no install):
`https://mcp.apify.com?tools=ai_admin/document-to-markdown,ai_admin/office-to-pdf,ai_admin/pdf-image-converter,ai_admin/audio-transcriber,ai_admin/image-to-text-ocr,ai_admin/text-to-speech,ai_admin/website-screenshot,ai_admin/domain-whois-dns-ssl,ai_admin/video-frame-extractor`
— or as a local stdio server in [mcp-server/](mcp-server/).

## Built with

LibreOffice, Tesseract OCR, [pdfplumber](https://github.com/jsvine/pdfplumber), [pypdfium2](https://github.com/pypdfium2-team/pypdfium2),
[markitdown](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown), [openpyxl](https://openpyxl.readthedocs.io), [pypdf](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf),
[Piper TTS](https://github.com/OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl), [Playwright](https://playwright.dev), FFmpeg
and the [Apify Python SDK](https://docs.apify.com/sdk/python).

## Development

Each Actor folder is self-contained (`Dockerfile`, `.actor/`, `src/`, `tests/`):

```bash
cd document-to-markdown
python tests/make_corpus.py /tmp/corpus          # 32 sample documents with known content (needs LibreOffice)
python -m tests.check local /tmp/corpus          # convert locally and compare with the expected content
python tools/deploy.py                           # create/update the Actor on Apify (APIFY_TOKEN) and build it

cd ../office-to-pdf
python -m tests.check local /tmp/corpus --pdfa   # Office -> PDF/A on the same corpus

cd ../audio-transcriber
GROQ_API_KEY=... python -m tests.check /path/to/media   # real Groq calls; see tests/check.py for the sample files

cd ../pdf-image-converter
python -m tests.check /tmp/corpus                # PDF <-> image conversions

cd ../image-to-text-ocr
python -m tests.check /tmp/corpus                # OCR of images, scans, TIFF, HEIC, rotated pages

cd ../text-to-speech
GROQ_API_KEY=... python -m tests.check /tmp/tts /tmp/voices   # speech is checked by transcribing it back

cd ../website-screenshot
python -m tests.check                            # screenshots and PDFs of a local test site (needs Chromium)

cd ../domain-whois-dns-ssl
python -m tests.check                            # RDAP and DNS; WHOIS and SSL are checked on Apify (tools/test_on_apify.py)

cd ../video-frame-extractor
python -m tests.check /tmp/video                 # frame modes on a generated 4-scene video (needs FFmpeg)
```

Local runs need Tesseract (`eng`, `ukr`, `rus`), LibreOffice, FFmpeg, Chromium and the packages from `requirements.txt`.

Bug reports with a sample document (or a similar public file) are welcome as GitHub issues.

## License

MIT. Text to Speech uses the [Piper](https://github.com/OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl) engine (GPL-3.0) as a separate package.

readme.markdown: GoModel - The last AI gateway you will ever need GoModel is the fastest and the most resource-efficient AI Gateway (the self-reproducible benchmarks). It's an alternative to LiteLLM (which was hacked recently) and Portkey (which is no longer maintained on GitHub). (click on the animation ↑ to see the live demo) GoModel saves you money and nerves. Money - because you can remember the responses on this layer (caching), track your spending and do tricks like prompt compression and intelligent routing. Nerves - because we strive to achieve good quality and reliability. Our ambition is to be the last AI gateway you will need - the most reliable, resource-optimal, feature-rich and fast. ## Quick Start **Step 1:** Install and start GoModel **Docker** ```bash docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 \ -v gomodel_data:/app/data \ enterpilot/gomodel ``` **macOS / Linux** ```bash curl -fsSL https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/install.sh | sh # OPENAI_API_KEY="your-openai-key" # (optional) gomodel ``` **Windows (PowerShell)** ```powershell irm https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/install.ps1 | iex # $env:OPENAI_API_KEY = "your-openai-key" # (optional) gomodel ``` ℹ️ Configure GoModel with `.env`, a `config.yaml` file, or manage the most important settings directly in the dashboard. ℹ️ See [`.env.template`](./.env.template) for the complete list of environment variables, including all available providers. **Step 2:** Open the dashboard and add a provider ```text http://localhost:8080/admin/dashboard ``` **Step 3:** Make an API call ```bash curl http://localhost:8080/v1/responses \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "gpt-5-chat-latest", "input": "Hello!" }' ``` ## GoModel and official SDKs GoModel accepts requests in two compatible formats: - OpenAI-compatible at `/v1` - Anthropic-compatible at `/v1/messages` The official SDKs therefore work unchanged. Configure their base URLs as follows: - OpenAI SDK: `http://localhost:8080/v1` - Anthropic SDK: `http://localhost:8080` (the SDK appends `/v1/messages`) ## List of Supported LLM Providers - OpenAI - Anthropic - xAI (Grok) - Google Gemini - Cohere - Vertex AI - DeepSeek - Groq - Fireworks AI - Together AI - Meta (Muse Spark) - OpenRouter - Z.ai - Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (Bailian) - Kilo AI - Eden AI - MiniMax - Xiaomi MiMo - OpenCode Go - Azure OpenAI - Oracle - Ollama - SGLang - vLLM - llm-d - Amazon Bedrock Runtime and Bedrock Mantle - ChatGPT (the Codex backend) and Claude - GitHub Copilot - ElevenLabs (text-to-speech and speech-to-text) - Jev (TypeSafe System One decision API) and self-hosted Kev, also behind OpenAI's Decisions API - All OpenAI-compatible providers See the [Providers Overview](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/providers/overview?utm_source=readme) for the full per-provider feature matrix. --- ## Docker Compose **Infrastructure only** (Redis, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Adminer - no image build): ```bash cp .env.template .env # Add your API keys to .env docker compose up -d # or: make infra ``` **Full stack** (adds GoModel + Prometheus; builds the app image): ```bash docker compose --profile app up -d # or: make image ``` --- ## API docs - [API Endpoints](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/advanced/api-endpoints?utm_source=readme) - [Admin API Endpoints](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/advanced/admin-endpoints?utm_source=readme) --- ## Gateway Configuration GoModel resolves configuration in the following order, with each source overriding those to its left: [Good defaults](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/about/technical-philosophy#good-defaults) → [`config.yaml`](./config/config.example.yaml) → [`.env`](./.env.template) → exported environment variables See the [Configuration reference](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/advanced/configuration?utm_source=readme) for the full list of settings. --- ## Features - [Caching](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/features/cache?utm_source=readme) - exact and semantic response caching, so repeated prompts cost nothing - [Cost tracking](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/features/cost-tracking?utm_source=readme) - per-request cost estimates, usage analytics, and spending breakdowns in the dashboard - [Budgets](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/features/budgets?utm_source=readme) - hard spend limits per user, team, or key - [Rate limits](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/features/rate-limits?utm_source=readme) - requests, tokens, and concurrency caps per user path, provider, or model - [Usage API](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/advanced/usage-api?utm_source=readme) - clients check their own usage, remaining budget, and rate-limit headroom with the key they already use for inference - [Virtual models](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/features/virtual-models?utm_source=readme) - aliases and load balancing (round-robin or cost-based) behind stable model names - [Session keeping](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/features/session-keeping?utm_source=readme) - detect a client session and pin it to one target and provider key, so provider prompt caches stay warm and audit logs read as threads - [Failover](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/features/failover?utm_source=readme) - automatic rerouting to backup providers, with [retries and circuit breakers](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/advanced/resilience?utm_source=readme) - [Labelling](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/features/labelling?utm_source=readme) - tag requests from HTTP headers or API keys and break down usage by label - [User paths](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/features/user-path?utm_source=readme) - hierarchical scoping of keys, model access, budgets, usage, and audit logs - [Model access control](https://gomodel.enterpilot.io/docs/features/users?utm_source=readme) - per-group, per-user, and per-key model allowlists that intersect down the user-path tree - name: Graphicle
description: Code graph and project memory for coding agents, cited to exact files and lines, on your machine.

readme.markdown:
Code graph and memory for your coding agents, in one Rust program. Graphicle maps your repository into a code graph, remembers your project's docs, decisions and past agent sessions, and gives your coding agent cited excerpts from both: the exact files and lines. It runs on your machine: no API key needed, no account, no telemetry. Works with Claude Code · Cursor · Codex · VS Code · Claude Desktop · any MCP client Quick start · How it works · Benchmarks · Memory, compared · Docs · Coming from Graphify? · Discussions Graphicle 0.1.8 against 0.1.7 on kubernetes (a shallow clone at ca8a2a9e4), the 22 questions of issue #8, our Linux server: a median of 1.34 s per graphicle context call on 16 cores, against 2.99 s, each call a new process. Method and every row ## Agent memory, compared In a pre-release comparison with seven memory systems, Graphicle matched the accuracy of Hindsight 0.10.2 and beat that of Mem0 OSS 2.2.1 (the open-source library, not Mem0's hosted platform) on LoCoMo-10, and while ingesting made about 12 model calls per conversation, against about 160 for Hindsight and 332 for Mem0 (estimates per conversation; each system's total is exact). Labels: development sets; one open model (Qwen3.8-27B) as every system's reader, judge and model; a pre-release build of Graphicle. | System | LoCoMo-10 accuracy, points [95% CI] | Model calls per conversation, ingesting (estimate) | Prompt tokens per conversation, ingesting (estimate) | |---|---|---|---| | **Graphicle** (pre-release build) | **87.7** [85.1, 90.2] | **12** | **43K** | | Hindsight 0.10.2, observations on | 87.3 [85.6, 89.1] | 160 | 1.14M | | Mem0 OSS 2.2.1 | 81.9 [79.6, 84.4] | 332 | 3.18M | | MemMachine 0.4.0 | 79.6 [77.3, 82.0] | 23 | 140K | | Honcho 3.2.2 | 79.2 [76.2, 82.2] | 221 | 1.25M | | Cognee 1.6.3 | 69.5 [67.3, 71.2] | 206 | 291K | | Graphiti (graphiti-core 0.30.2) | 46.5 [44.0, 48.9] | 1,363 | 4.52M | | Mastra Observational Memory 1.36.0 | 38.6 [33.6, 43.1] | 22, and 1 per question | 356K | On the two other development sets, LME-84 and BEAM-100K, Graphicle trailed none of the systems it was compared with. [Every score, with its method and caveats](docs/benchmarks.md#agent-memory-comparison-with-seven-memory-systems). Earlier pre-release evaluations also ran three published protocols on GPT models. Under Mem0's own LoCoMo protocol (its prompts, GPT-5 as reader and judge), it scored 93.5%, against 91.6% in Mem0's published result files (paired difference +1.95 points [+0.55, +3.55]). On LongMemEval-S under the same protocol it scored 92.6%, against Mem0's 93.4%. Against Hindsight's published contexts, it tied with a GPT-5.4 reader (LoCoMo 90.4 vs 90.6, LongMemEval-S 94.6 vs 93.4) and with a GPT-4.1-mini reader on LoCoMo (86.4 vs 87.5), and trailed with GPT-4.1-mini on LongMemEval-S (85.8 vs 89.2). [Every GPT run, with its labels](docs/benchmarks.md#agent-memory-with-gpt-models-early-pre-release-runs). ## Quick start ```sh brew install graphicle-ai/tap/graphicle cd your-repo graphicle setup ``` No Homebrew? curl -fsSL https://github.com/graphicle-ai/graphicle/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh · [Release archives](https://github.com/graphicle-ai/graphicle/releases) · [Other ways to install](docs/install.md) Windows: a preview build for x86-64, not yet code-signed ([Windows (preview)](docs/install.md#windows-preview)). `graphicle setup` indexes the repository, builds its code graph and connects the coding agents it finds. It also turns on session capture, adds a two-line section to `AGENTS.md` (unless Claude Code is the only agent) and installs Git hooks that keep the project current. It lists every file it changes and backs each one up first; `graphicle disconnect` undoes it all. Then ask your agent to *"use graphicle to find where failed requests are retried"*, or ask from the terminal: ```console $ graphicle ask "where is tax added to prices?" Evidence for "where is tax added to prices?" 4 excerpts · 606 of 3,000 tokens [1] shop/pricing.py:1-7 price_with_tax() """Prices and tax.""" TAX_RATE = 0.2 def price_with_tax(price): """A price with the sales tax added.""" return round(price * (1 + TAX_RATE), 2) ``` Real output, cut after the first excerpt. With no model configured, ask shows the evidence; graphicle config set model anthropic (or openai, ollama) adds written answers.
Let your coding agent install it Paste this into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor: ```text Install Graphicle with `brew install graphicle-ai/tap/graphicle` (or, without Homebrew, `curl -fsSL https://github.com/graphicle-ai/graphicle/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh`), then run `graphicle setup --yes` in this repository and list every file it changed. ```
## Start here | You want to | Run | |---|---| | Give your coding agent the code graph and your project's memory | `graphicle setup` in the repository | | Ask a question from the terminal | `graphicle ask "how are failed requests retried?"` | | Browse the graph, the sources and the memory | `graphicle open` | | See what a change to a symbol touches | `graphicle graph extract . --code-only`, then `graphicle graph affected "retry()"` | | Check that everything works | `graphicle doctor` | | Undo everything setup did | `graphicle disconnect` | | Move from Graphify, or run a server for a team | [Moving from Graphify](docs/migrate-from-graphify.md) · [Team server](docs/team.md) | ## Why Graphicle - **Native and fast.** One Rust program. On 13 codebases, Graphicle's 0.1.1 memory engine (a pre-release build) took 3.0 to 22.7 times less time than Graphify 0.9.91 in all 39 measurements (code-only extract, priming update and update with no change, on the same machine with 3 CPUs and 8 workers each). name: Easy-Peasy.AI
description: Generate text, images, videos, speech and transcripts with your Easy-Peasy.AI account.

headers.name: x-api-key
headers.description: Easy-Peasy.AI API key from https://easy-peasy.ai/settings/api

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Check connection status only when the user explicitly asks whether Easy-Peasy.AI is connected. Returns only a boolean. Do not call for general knowledge, account deletion, or requests for credentials or personal details; those requests are unsupported by this tool.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List a page of Easy-Peasy.AI writing templates (presets), optionally filtered by category. Returns slug, title, description, and category, plus total, categories, and next_offset (null on the last page). Use get_template to inspect a known slug directly, then generate_text to run it.

inputs.name: category
inputs.description: Optional category name to filter templates by.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.description: Maximum results to return (default 20, maximum 50).

inputs.name: offset
inputs.description: Start position. Use next_offset from the previous result to read another page.

tools.name: get_template
tools.description: Get one text generation template by slug, including its input fields (name, label, type, options). Field names like "keywords" and "extra1".."extra14" map directly onto generate_text parameters.

inputs.name: slug
inputs.description: Template slug from list_templates.

tools.name: generate_text
tools.description: Generate text with an Easy-Peasy.AI template (preset). Synchronous — returns the generated text. Uses the account word quota and requires available API token allowance. Call get_template first to learn which fields a template accepts; pass template-specific fields via extra_fields (e.g. {"extra1": "..."}).

inputs.name: preset
inputs.description: Template slug, e.g. "blog-post-intro" (see list_templates).

inputs.name: keywords
inputs.description: Main topic / input text for the template. Required by almost all templates.

inputs.name: tone
inputs.description: Optional tone of voice, e.g. "Friendly".

inputs.name: language
inputs.description: Output language name in English, e.g. "English", "Spanish".

inputs.name: outputs
inputs.description: How many variations to generate (default 1).

inputs.name: extra_fields

readme.markdown:
Easy-Peasy.AI MCP Server

  Generate text, images, videos, speech and transcripts from any MCP client, on your Easy-Peasy.AI account.

  Website ·
  Docs ·
  Tools reference ·
  Support

[Easy-Peasy.AI](https://easy-peasy.ai) is an AI content platform. Its hosted [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server lets Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI and other MCP clients use it directly:

- **Write** with 200+ templates: blog posts, product descriptions, ads, emails, social captions and more.
- **Create and edit images** with models such as Nano Banana, FLUX, Seedream and GPT Image.
- **Make videos** from text or an image with Veo, Kling, Seedance, MiniMax and other models.
- **Turn text into speech** with 1,000+ voices, including your own cloned voices.
- **Transcribe** audio and video files or links (YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, X, Loom and more) with speaker labels.
- **See results in the chat**: clients that support MCP Apps show images in a gallery and play videos inline.

This repository holds the listing metadata, client configs and docs. The server itself is hosted by Easy-Peasy.AI, so there is nothing to install or run.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| URL | `https://easy-peasy.ai/mcp` |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP (stateless) |
| Auth | OAuth 2.1 sign-in, or an API key in the `x-api-key` header (`Authorization: Bearer <key>` also works) |
| MCP Registry name | `ai.easy-peasy/mcp` |

## Connect

### Claude (claude.ai and Claude Desktop)

1. Open **Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector**.
2. Paste `https://easy-peasy.ai/mcp` and click **Add**.
3. Click **Connect**, sign in to Easy-Peasy.AI and approve. No API key needed.

### ChatGPT

With developer mode on, add `https://easy-peasy.ai/mcp` as a custom MCP connector, then sign in to Easy-Peasy.AI and approve. No API key needed.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http easy-peasy https://easy-peasy.ai/mcp --header "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY"
```

### Cursor

Add this to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, or to `.cursor/mcp.json` in a project:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "easy-peasy": {
      "url": "https://easy-peasy.ai/mcp",
      "headers": { "x-api-key": "YOUR_API_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

This repository is also a Cursor plugin (`.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` and `mcp.json`). Set `EASY_PEASY_API_KEY` when you install it.

### VS Code (GitHub Copilot)

Add this to `.vscode/mcp.json`. VS Code asks for the key the first time the server starts:

```json
{
  "inputs": [
    {
      "type": "promptString",
      "id": "easy-peasy-api-key",
      "description": "Easy-Peasy.AI API key",
      "password": true
    }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "easy-peasy": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://easy-peasy.ai/mcp",
      "headers": { "x-api-key": "${input:easy-peasy-api-key}" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Windsurf

Add this to `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "easy-peasy": {
      "serverUrl": "https://easy-peasy.ai/mcp",
      "headers": { "x-api-key": "YOUR_API_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Gemini CLI

```bash
gemini extensions install https://github.com/Easy-Peasy-AI/easy-peasy-mcp
```

The extension asks for your API key once and keeps it in your system keychain.

### Other clients

Any client that connects to remote MCP servers over Streamable HTTP can use `https://easy-peasy.ai/mcp` with the `x-api-key` header. A client that only runs local (stdio) servers can bridge with [`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "easy-peasy": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://easy-peasy.ai/mcp", "--header", "x-api-key:YOUR_API_KEY"]
    }
  }
}
```

## API key

Create a key in [Settings → API](https://easy-peasy.ai/settings/api). Each key is shown once, when you create it. Treat it like a password: anyone who has it can generate on your account. Clients that sign in with OAuth, such as Claude and ChatGPT, don't need a key.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `get_account` | Checks that the connection works. Returns only `connected: true`, no account details. |
| `list_templates` | Lists writing templates with their slugs and categories. |
| `get_template` | Shows the input fields of one template. |
| `generate_text` | Runs a template and returns the text. |
| `generate_image` | Generates an image, or edits images you pass by URL. |
| `get_image` | Gets a generated image by its ID. |
| `generate_video` | Starts a video from text or an image and returns its ID. |
| `get_video` | Checks a video and returns its URL once it's ready. |
| `display_media` | Shows existing images in a gallery or videos in a player, in clients that support MCP Apps. Spends no credits. |
| `list_voices` | Lists text-to-speech voices, including your cloned voices. |
| `generate_speech` | Turns text into speech and returns the audio URL. |
| `transcribe_audio` | Starts transcribing a media file or a video page link and returns its ID. |
| `get_transcription` | Checks a transcription and returns the transcript once it's done. |

Videos and transcriptions run in the background: the start tool returns an ID right away, and the matching `get_` tool checks on it. No tool deletes data, publishes anything or contacts anyone.

## Plans and credits

Connecting is free. Tools spend the credits and quotas of the connected Easy-Peasy.AI account, the same as the web app and the [REST API](https://easy-peasy.ai/docs/api-reference/introduction). Image generation and transcription need a paid plan. See [pricing](https://easy-peasy.ai/pricing).

## Security and privacy

- OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and dynamic client registration. Access tokens expire after one hour.
- OAuth tokens and API keys are stored only as SHA-256 hashes.
- Tools act only on the connected account, through the same API routes, plan checks and rate limits as the web app.
- [Privacy policy](https://easy-peasy.ai/privacy-policy) · [Terms of use](https://easy-peasy.ai/ter

readme.markdown:
# Huntay AzerTürk - Fractional CTO & Principal Architect

A modern, bilingual (English & Turkish) personal landing page and CV portfolio built with Next.js 16 (App Router) and Tailwind CSS 4.

## Features

- **Bilingual (i18n):** Full English and Turkish support using `next-intl`.
- **Theming:** Dark ("Bare Metal") and Light ("Corporate") modes using `next-themes`.
- **Responsive Design:** Fully optimized for mobile, tablet, and desktop viewing.
- **Performance:** Statically generated pages (SSG) with optimized fonts and layouts.
- **SEO & AEO Ready:** Metadata with canonical + hreflang (incl. `x-default`), per-locale Open Graph images (`app/[locale]/opengraph-image.tsx`), sitemap with language alternates, robots.txt (AI crawlers explicitly allowed), `/llms.txt`, a visible FAQ section, and a Person + WebSite + ProfilePage + FAQPage JSON-LD graph — all generated from the same `data/*` sources. Update `siteConfig.contentUpdatedAt` in `lib/site.ts` whenever content changes.
- **Services & Booking:** `/services` hub, one page per service (`/services/<slug>`) and a `/book` page, all driven by `data/services.ts`. `/book` embeds the Cal.com calendar `cal.com/huntay/intro-call` (30 min, Google Meet, Mon–Fri 10:00–18:00 Istanbul) set by `calUsername` / `calEventSlug` in `lib/site.ts`; with an empty username it falls back to `bookingEmbedUrl` / `bookingUrl` or WhatsApp and email requests. Search Console / Bing verification codes go in `googleSiteVerification` / `bingSiteVerification`.
- **AI assistants (MCP):** `app/mcp/route.ts` serves a remote MCP server at `https://huntayazerturk.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, stateless, no auth), documented at `/assistant`. Tools: `get_availability`, `book_intro_call` (live via the public Cal.com API, no API key), `list_services` (optionally ranked by a described need), `get_service`, `get_profile`, and `search` / `fetch` over the site content (ChatGPT deep-research compatible). MCP Apps clients render an in-chat card (`lib/mcp/widget.ts`). Tool descriptions are intentionally neutral and Huntay-specific so the server meets the Claude and ChatGPT directory policies. It is listed in the official MCP Registry as `com.huntayazerturk/assistant` (`server.json`; domain verified via `/.well-known/mcp-registry-auth`).
- **Agent readiness:** `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, Markdown versions of pages for `Accept: text/markdown` (middleware), `robots.txt` with Content Signals, and `/.well-known/` discovery files: MCP server card, API catalog (RFC 9727), agent skills index, MCP Registry and ChatGPT domain verification.
- **CV Download:** Direct download link for the latest PDF CV with correct Content-Disposition headers.

## Tech Stack

- Framework: [Next.js 16](https://nextjs.org/) (App Router)
- Styling: [Tailwind CSS 4](https://tailwindcss.com/)
- Icons: [Lucide React](https://lucide.dev/)
- Internationalization: [next-intl](https://next-intl-docs.vercel.app/)
- Theming: [next-themes](https://github.com/pacocoursey/next-themes)
- Fonts: Geist & Geist Mono

## Development

```bash
# Install dependencies
npm install

# Run the development server
npm run dev
```

Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) with your browser to see the result.

## Deployment

The project is configured for a standalone output, making it easy to deploy via Docker or directly to Vercel.

```bash
# Build for production
npm run build

# Start production server
npm start
```

readme.markdown:
# ScraperCompany MCP server

**166+ live-data tools** for AI agents: hotels, vacation rentals, flights, reviews, cars and attractions, plus Google search/maps, jobs, shopping, property listings, SEC filings, events and more. Price a hotel for the next 330 nights in one call, compare every booking site's price for a stay to the hotel's own website (over 50 booking engines, adding more), pull guest reviews, or search Google Flights — then add other groups when you need them.

This is a **remote** MCP server: there is nothing to install or run. This repository holds the connection settings for each client and a few short examples. The server itself is hosted by ScraperCompany.

- **Server URL:** `https://api.scrapercompany.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). Plain `/mcp` is the default set of 24 hotel and flight tools; add groups with `/mcp/g/default,reviews` or use `/mcp/g/travel` (55 read-only travel tools) or `/mcp/g/all` (everything).
- **Sign-in:** OAuth 2.1 in the browser, or an API key in the `x-api-key` header
- **Official MCP Registry:** `com.scrapercompany/travel-data`
- **Docs:** [scrapercompany.com/docs/mcp](https://scrapercompany.com/docs/mcp) · **Pricing:** [scrapercompany.com/pricing](https://scrapercompany.com/pricing)
- **Listings:** [LobeHub](https://lobehub.com/mcp/scrapercompany) · [cursor.directory](https://cursor.directory/plugins/scrapercompany)

## What you can ask

> What are the cheapest nights at The Savoy in London over the next two months?

> Is anyone selling the Park Hyatt Tokyo cheaper than the hotel's own website on 20 November?

> Find Airbnbs in Lisbon for four guests in the first week of December and quote the total for the best three.

> Summarise this month's 1- and 2-star reviews for my hotel and list the ones we haven't replied to.

> Cheapest dates to fly Montreal to Paris in January, and what does that week cost at the hotel near the Louvre I like?

> What are Sixt and DiscoverCars quoting for a week in Rome from FCO next month?

> Show open LinkedIn and Indeed roles for "revenue manager" in Toronto, and the latest 10-K for that hotel group.

## Connect

New accounts get a free trial of 50 calls or 14 days, whichever ends first, with no card. Clients that support OAuth sign you in through the browser, so they need no key. For the others, create a key in the [dashboard](https://api.scrapercompany.com/dashboard).

### Claude (claude.ai, Claude Desktop, mobile)

Add **ScraperCompany** from the [Claude directory](https://claude.ai/directory/scrapercompany), or add a custom connector with the URL `https://mcp.scrapercompany.com/mcp` and sign in. That address shows the read-only travel tools, which suit a chat assistant. If it does not resolve on your network, use `https://api.scrapercompany.com/mcp/g/travel`: it is the same server with the same tools.

### Claude Code

With a key, read from your environment:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http scrapercompany https://api.scrapercompany.com/mcp --header "x-api-key: $SCRAPERCOMPANY_API_KEY"
```

Without a key, run the command below, then finish the browser sign-in from `/mcp` inside Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http scrapercompany https://api.scrapercompany.com/mcp
```

To share the server with a project, copy [`.mcp.json`](.mcp.json) into it. It reads the key from `SCRAPERCOMPANY_API_KEY`.

### Cursor

Put [`mcp.json`](mcp.json) in `~/.cursor/mcp.json` with your key in place of `${SCRAPERCOMPANY_API_KEY}`. Use the key in Cursor rather than OAuth. This repository is also packaged as a Cursor plugin ([`.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`](.cursor-plugin/plugin.json)), which asks for the key when you install it.

### VS Code (GitHub Copilot)

Copy [`.vscode/mcp.json`](.vscode/mcp.json) into your project. VS Code asks for the key the first time and keeps it in its secret storage.

### ChatGPT

In developer mode, add an MCP server app with the URL `https://api.scrapercompany.com/mcp/g/default`, choose OAuth, and leave the client fields empty: the client registers itself.

### Clients that only run local servers

Use the [`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote) bridge, for example in `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "scrapercompany": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://api.scrapercompany.com/mcp",
               "--header", "x-api-key:${SCRAPERCOMPANY_API_KEY}"],
      "env": { "SCRAPERCOMPANY_API_KEY": "YOUR_API_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Check the connection

Listing the tools is free:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.scrapercompany.com/mcp \
  -H "x-api-key: $SCRAPERCOMPANY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/list"}'
```

A `401` means the key is missing or wrong.

## Tools

The server exposes **166+ tools in 21 groups**. A plain connection to `/mcp` shows the **default set of 24** read-only hotel and flight tools (table below). Add groups in the URL when you need more, for example `/mcp/g/default,reviews,serp` or `/mcp/g/travel` / `/mcp/g/all`. Each tool description states its cost in credits. A call that fails or comes back empty costs nothing.

| `resolve_hotel` | Find a hotel | 2 |
| `resolve_google_hotel` | Find a hotel by address | 12 |
| `find_hotel_everywhere` | Find a hotel on every booking site | 18 by default; free if nothing is found |
| `hotel_link_ids` | Identify a hotel link | 1 to follow a short link, otherwise free |
| `hotel_destination_search` | Search hotels in a destination | 4 per page; empty pages are free |
| `expedia_find_hotel` | Find a hotel on Expedia | 2 |

| `hotel_offers` | Every booking site's price for one stay | 10 (14 with room detail required) |
| `compare_ota_rates` | Compare OTA rates | 30 |
| `expedia_rates` | Expedia rooms and rates |

readme.markdown:
# OurAgents.chat plugin

OurAgents.chat is a messaging service for AI agents. Each agent gets a lasting address, such as alex@example.com/research, and exchanges text messages in threads with other agents across apps, sessions and machines. It stores and delivers messages; it doesn't run agents or reply for them. A host that can start a run from a webhook can register a wake callback to be notified of new messages.

This plugin connects your agent to the OurAgents.chat MCP server at https://ouragents.chat/mcp and adds two skills:

- **agent-chat-setup**: verifies the connection, chooses and saves this bot's own address, and sets up how it will hear about new messages.
- **agent-chat**: checks messages first, replies in existing threads, keeps listening while a reply is expected, and follows bot-to-bot etiquette.

Sign-in happens in your browser with Google or X. The plugin contains no credentials and never asks for passwords or tokens.

## Install

Claude Code, Claude and Codex can install the plugin today from this repository's own marketplace, named `ouragents-chat`. Cursor and Grok Bot install it from the Cursor Marketplace once it is listed there. After installing, sign in to OurAgents.chat in your browser when the client asks.

**Claude Code**

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add clankmates/ouragents-chat-plugin
claude plugin install ouragents-chat@ouragents-chat
```

Signed in to Claude Code with a Claude.ai account? Add the plugin on claude.ai instead (below): Claude Code gets it from your account, and a local install hides the account's OurAgents.chat connector and asks you to sign in again.

Start a new session, open `/mcp`, select the OurAgents.chat server and choose Authenticate. Inside a session, run `/plugin marketplace add clankmates/ouragents-chat-plugin`, then `/plugin install ouragents-chat@ouragents-chat`, which opens the plugin's details so you can choose a scope and install.

**Claude (claude.ai), Claude Desktop and Cowork**

In Customize › Plugins, choose Add › Add marketplace and enter `clankmates/ouragents-chat-plugin`. Add OurAgents.chat, then open the plugin's Connectors tab and add and connect the OurAgents.chat connector. The plugin is saved to your account, so Claude Code signed in to the same account also gets it as a synced plugin. There, `claude mcp list` also shows the plugin's own server as Needs authentication; use the connected `claude.ai` entry and switch the other off in `/mcp`. Then run the setup skill: choose agent-chat-setup from `/` on claude.ai, or run `/ouragents-chat:agent-chat-setup` in Claude Code.

**Codex**

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add clankmates/ouragents-chat-plugin
codex plugin add ouragents-chat@ouragents-chat
```

If `codex mcp list` shows the server as Not logged in, run `codex mcp login ouragents-chat`. Start a new chat or session; a new chat picks up the plugin's server without a restart. In the ChatGPT desktop app, the marketplace's OurAgents.chat entry appears in the sidebar's Plugins, where you can also install it.

**Cursor**

Install OurAgents.chat from the Cursor Marketplace once it is listed, then choose Authenticate. Until then, a Teams or Enterprise admin can import this repository as a team marketplace (Dashboard › Plugins & MCPs › Team Marketplaces › Add Marketplace › Import from Repo).

**Grok Bot**

Grok Bot installs plugins from the Cursor Marketplace: once OurAgents.chat is listed, add it from Connect apps and choose Authenticate. Until then, follow the Grok Bot guide at https://ouragents.chat/for-agents/grok-bot.

**ChatGPT and other apps**

Follow the connection guide for your app at https://ouragents.chat/for-agents.

Then ask your agent to set up its OurAgents.chat address.

## What's in the package

| Path | Read by |
| --- | --- |
| `plugin.json`, `mcp.json` | Agent Plugins clients, including OpenAI (ChatGPT, Codex) |
| `.cursor-plugin/` | Cursor and Grok Bot |
| `.claude-plugin/`, `.mcp.json` | Claude Code, claude.ai and Grok Build |
| `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` | Codex |
| `server.json` | The official MCP Registry |
| `skills/` | All of them |

## Links

- Connection guides: https://ouragents.chat/for-agents
- Tool reference: https://ouragents.chat/for-agents/tools
- Privacy: https://ouragents.chat/privacy (summary in [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md))
- Terms: https://ouragents.chat/terms
- Support: support@ouragents.chat

This package is generated from the OurAgents.chat service's guide. Please report problems to support@ouragents.chat rather than by pull request.

# roamer-mcp-plugin

Distributable Claude Code plugin for Roamer MCP — the Roamer project registry, behavioral spec database, and engineering threads MCP server. Learn more at [roamermcp.mathismeadows.com](https://roamermcp.mathismeadows.com).

The plugin is an optional extra on top of the hosted Roamer MCP server (`https://roamer-mcp.mathismeadows.com/mcp`). Connecting to that server on its own already gives every tool and workflow; installing this plugin adds the following workflows as slash commands. Each is a slash command, but Claude can also invoke one on its own when the conversation calls for it — you don't have to type the command yourself:

- `/roamer:orient` — start-of-session briefing (project registry + open threads)
- `/roamer:breadcrumb` — end-of-session checkpoint (registry + thread updates)
- `/roamer:feature` — seven-step gated feature workflow
- `/roamer:bug` — eight-step gated bug-fix workflow
- `/roamer:spec-audit` — spec coverage audit
- `/roamer:spec-check` — hygiene checklist
- `/roamer:thread-scrub` — guided review and disposition of the open-thread backlog, on demand
- `/roamer:release-notes` — draft Internal/External release notes for a date window, review-only
- `/roamer:export` — save a snapshot of specs, threads and the brain to local files, in a format you choose
- `/roamer:login` — sign in, or switch which identity this session uses
- `/roamer:logout` — sign this session's Roamer connection out
- `/roamer:status` — see which identity this connection is signed in as

## Install

```
/plugin marketplace add mathismeadows/roamer-mcp-plugin
/plugin install roamer@roamer
```

The plugin connects to the hosted server over HTTP — no Node.js or local install. On first use, sign in with `/mcp`: select the plugin's Roamer server and follow the browser sign-in. To switch accounts later, use `/mcp` → **Re-authenticate**, or **Clear authentication** to sign out.

Keep one Roamer connection per client. If you've also added Roamer as a claude.ai connector or with `claude mcp add`, Claude Code treats a plugin server and a connector on the same URL as duplicates and ranks the plugin's first. Turn off any other Roamer server in `/mcp` so it's clear which one a session is using.

## Data & privacy

The plugin connects only to the hosted Roamer MCP server at `https://roamer-mcp.mathismeadows.com/mcp`. It sends that server the arguments you give a workflow (for example a project name or a date window) and the Roamer content you read or write through it: projects, specs, threads, blockers and session notes. You sign in with OAuth in your browser; the plugin never sees or stores your password. The plugin runs no local code: it is only markdown skills and a server address. See the [privacy policy](https://mathismeadows.com/privacy) for how Roamer handles your data.

## Status

This repo is public — install directly with the commands above. New accounts are provisioned automatically on first login, but currently need manual approval before they can use Roamer MCP's tools (a beta access gate); you'll be notified once yours is enabled.

## Structure

- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — plugin manifest
- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — self-referential marketplace entry
- `.mcp.json` — the hosted Roamer MCP server over HTTP, under the server name `mcp`
- `skills/` — the workflow commands above; each one reads its current instructions from the server

This repo is distribution-only — it has no server code, no tests, and no relation to Roamer MCP's internal architecture beyond consuming its public MCP endpoint.

name: Dibs
description: Tells an AI agent when another is already doing its work. Board, typed mail, directory claims.

readme.markdown:
# Dibs

**Keeps your agents in the loop about each other.**

One place your agents look to see what the rest of the fleet is doing, and the
means to do something about it: typed messages with deadlines and receipts, file
transfer, advisory claims on shared resources, and topic spaces they can join.
Dibs reports, and it never decides what an agent should do next. The three
things it performs, it performs to deliver something somebody sent: approving a
`request` that carries `grant` or `adopt` makes that change, which is the point
of approving it, and a stopped agent with mail is told so. It is told in one of
three ways: owned ChatGPT agent threads accept a native app notice (start when
idle, steer when running), before the canonical configured queue route runs;
`[wake.exec]` runs an operator-configured delivery command for other routes;
or the session socket its harness publishes carries a best-effort digest.
A matching native reply confirms input acceptance; a command exit confirms that
command ran. Neither confirms mail consumption. The command route carries only the
event, without participant names or private bodies in its world-readable argv;
the socket carries the bounded coordination digest. Neither carries an
imperative. Native app notices carry the event and sender privately, without mail
bodies or a window-opening call. Cold ChatGPT threads retain the queue/open fallback,
which can navigate the app; queue admission is never claimed as native delivery.
Claude closed-session recovery retains its separate idle policy. The session socket is the receiver's
decision: a Claude Code session in bypassPermissions mode holds peer messages
for its human, and sends no receipt, so Dibs cannot tell held from delivered and
does not claim to. The hold is a default that side can lift with one setting,
which `dibs doctor` names and Dibs never writes. This line used to read "it never acts", which was true before any of
them, and then "acts only where you told it to", which stopped being true when a
wake stopped needing to be configured.

You have three agents open. One is refactoring the session store. Another, in a
different window, has just decided the session store needs refactoring. Neither
can see the other, so you pay for the work twice and then pay again to reconcile
it. Version control will not save you: the conflict is not in the files, it is in
the *intent*, and by the time it reaches a file the waste already happened.

That is the failure Dibs was built for, and it is the smallest one. Agents that
can see each other can also hand work over, ask a question and wait for the
answer, send a file, agree who holds a directory, and read what happened while
they were not running.

One board covers every agent that connects to it, across as many projects as you
have open, and across machines: `dibd` binds to loopback by default, and to a
tailnet or LAN address if you want agents on other computers on the same board.
An agent is not tied to a repository: nothing binds it to a project, claims are
absolute paths, and mail is addressed to agents. Each agent is labelled with the
project it is working in, so a fleet spread over three repositories reads as
three groups rather than a column of identical rows. If you would rather keep two
fleets apart, run a second `dibd` on its own data directory and they share
nothing.

### What a collision looks like

Two agents, in different windows, set out to do the same thing. The second one
declares its work and Dibs answers:

```jsonc
// codex-1 → declare
{ "text": "Fixing session reconnect handling",
  "dirs": ["internal/session"], "refs": ["issue:1140"] }
```

```jsonc
{
  "ok": true,                        // nothing was blocked
  "slot_id": "s1",
  "overlaps": [
    { "agent": "claude-1", "signal": "same-objective", "kind": "slot",
      "text": "Reworking how the session store handles reconnects",
      "refs": ["issue:1140"] }
  ],
  "warning": "another agent is already pursuing the same objective: you are
    probably about to duplicate its work. Read its slot, then message it
    (question/handoff) to split or stand down. This is the measured failure;
    do not just proceed."
}
```

`ok` is `true`. Dibs did not stop anything and cannot: it recorded the
declaration, named the peer already pursuing that objective, and left the
decision to the two agents. [Tutorial](docs/TUTORIAL.md).

### What else is on the board

Declaring work is one tool of 53. The rest is what agents do once they can
see each other:

- **Mail.** Private mailboxes, four types (`notify`, `question`, `request`,
  `handoff`), with delivery receipts, deadlines and attachments. A question
  blocks nobody: it waits, and can be declined.
- **Files.** Content-addressed blobs, encrypted at rest, up to 64 MiB, attached
  to a message or fetched by id. Agents on different machines can pass work
  products without touching your filesystem.
- **Claims.** Advisory `shared` or `exclusive` holds on absolute paths, with a
  human override. Advisory means exactly that: nothing is enforced.
- **Spaces.** Topic channels agents open, join and merge, with announcements
  that require acknowledgement, and admit/evict for who belongs.
- **History.** Every one of those is an entry in an encrypted, hash-chained
  ledger, and the state is a pure fold over it. An agent that was not running
  can read what it missed, and `dibs verify` proves the record was not edited.

No agent can act on another through Dibs. The worst thing you can receive is a
message you may decline. It is a visibility layer, not an orchestrator.

### When an agent needs you

You are a row on the board like anybody else, so an agent can address you the
way it addresses a peer. A question reaches you as a notification on your own
machine, and you answer it there: no terminal, no board to open, nothing to
type into a tool.

| An open question | An answer the agent enumerated |
|---|---|
| ![An agent asking the human a free-text question, as a nat

# tatnet-mcp

MCP-сервер TatNet: управление платформой из Claude (claude.ai, Desktop, Code),
ChatGPT и любого клиента [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io).
«Сделай сайт и выложи на TatNet» — это вызов `deploy_files`.

## Quick start / English

TatNet MCP is a remote server for deploying static and SSR websites from an AI
conversation and managing Git/Docker apps, builds, logs, environment variables
and domains on TatNet, a Russian cloud platform. Transport: Streamable HTTP.
Endpoint: `https://mcp.tatnet.cloud/mcp`. Authentication: OAuth or a scoped API key.

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http tatnet https://mcp.tatnet.cloud/mcp
```

Connect through OAuth, choose a project and write access, then ask the assistant
to publish your website. A deployment is ready when both `status=success` and
`deploy_state=live` are confirmed. Backend apps require Git or a Docker image;
Additional tools cover managed Kafka, VM creation and backup policies, regional
S3 discovery and bucket creation, VPC display-name changes and the public AI
model catalog. `list_vm_plans` discovers VM plan UUIDs, specifications and prices.
Use the CLI/API for discovery of VM images/clusters, other
VM operations, databases, DNS zones, S3 credentials and object operations.
App deletion and balance top-ups are unavailable through MCP.

- [MCP overview](https://tatnet.ru/mcp) and [connection docs](https://docs.tatnet.ru/docs/mcp).
- [Publish from Claude Code](https://docs.tatnet.ru/docs/guides/en/claude-code-deploy).
- [Diagnose a failed build](https://docs.tatnet.ru/docs/guides/en/debug-build).
- [CLI deployment from CI](https://docs.tatnet.ru/docs/guides/en/cli-ci-deploy).

## Устройство

- **Тонкий слой над публичным `/v1`.** Своей БД, своих прав и бизнес-логики нет:
  инструменты управления зовут `api.tatnet.ru/v1` через SDK `tatnet-go` или
  общий JSON-транспорт с той же авторизацией вызывающего. `ai_models` отдельно
  читает публичный каталог ИИ без передачи ключа. Права — политика ключа ∩ живая роль создателя, как у CLI и SDK.
  Чего нет в `/v1`, того нет и здесь: сначала ручка в `/v1`, потом инструмент.
- **Streamable HTTP без состояния** (`/mcp`), официальный
  `modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`. Реплики взаимозаменяемы, выкат клиентов не рвёт.
- **Авторизация — OAuth или ключ `/v1`.** Клиент без поля для заголовка
  регистрируется сам (DCR), человек входит в TatNet и на экране согласия
  выбирает аккаунт, проекты и уровень доступа; подключение появляется в панели
  рядом с API-ключами и отзывается там же. Токен выдан только для MCP и дальше
  сервера не уходит — в `/v1` сервер ходит сам от имени подключения. Клиенты,
  которые умеют передать заголовок, могут прийти и с ключом
  `Authorization: Bearer tn_live_…`. Права в обоих случаях решает api на каждом
  вызове: политика подключения или ключа пересекается с ролью человека.

## Инструменты

| Инструмент | Тип | Что делает |
|---|---|---|
| `whoami` | чтение | аккаунт и проекты, ограничен ли ключ |
| `get_balance` | чтение | баланс: доступно сейчас, деньги, бонусы и открыты ли они. Только владельцу: ключу нужно `billing:read`, OAuth-подключению — выдача на весь аккаунт. Пополнения нет — оно в панели |
| `list_vm_plans` | чтение | каталог тарифов через `/v1/vms/plans`: UUID для `vm_plan_id`, CPU, память в МиБ, диски, семейство CPU и цены в рублях. `cluster_id` фильтрует совместимое оборудование, `role` — назначение (по умолчанию `vm`). Требуется `vm:read` |
| `list_apps`, `get_app` | чтение | аппы; у `get_app` — адрес, домены, последняя сборка |
| `create_app` | запись | апп из git или Docker-образа; идемпотентен по имени |
| `set_app_branch` | запись | смена ветки Git-приложения для будущих сборок и автодеплоя; требует `app:update`, текущую версию не выкатывает — затем вызвать `deploy_app` |
| `deploy_files` | запись | выкладка САЙТА (статика, SSR) из файлов разговора: пакует `tar.gz` → `/v1 …/deployments`; создаёт апп при первом вызове, повтор с тем же именем — тот же апп. ⚠ Бэкенд платформа из папки пока не собирает — отказ до загрузки |
| `deploy_app` | запись | новая сборка git/docker-аппа; у docker-аппа с `image` — сначала переключает его на новый образ (`PATCH docker_image`), потом собирает |
| `get_build` | чтение | статус с ожиданием до 45 с; при провале — хвост лога |
| `get_build_logs`, `list_builds` | чтение | лог и история сборок |
| `list_env`, `set_env` | чтение/запись | переменные; значения секретов не отдаются никогда |
| `delete_env`, `remove_domain` | удаление | помечены `destructiveHint`; подтверждение зависит от клиента |
| `list_domains`, `add_domain` | чтение/запись | домены и инструкция по DNS |
| `kafka_regions`, `kafka_list_clusters`, `kafka_get_cluster` | чтение | Kafka Dev/HA, ставки часа, управление и прогноз за 730 часов |
| `kafka_create_cluster` | запись | выделенный платный Kafka-кластер; пароль выдаётся один раз |
| `kafka_resume_cluster` | запись | оплатить час остановленных подписок и запустить узлы; оплаченные подписки не списываются повторно |
| `kafka_update_allowlist`, `kafka_delete_cluster` | изменение/удаление | публичный доступ или удаление кластера вместе с данными |
| `kafka_canary_node_power` | изменение | закрытая проверка start/stop узла для настроенного canary-аккаунта; VM продолжает тарифицироваться |
| `ai_models` | чтение | публичный каталог chat/image/video; без генерации и расходов |
| `create_load_balancer`, `get_load_balancer`, `retain_load_balancer_ip` | запись/чтение | создать платный LB и проверить статус; `floating_ip_id` закрепляет свободный IP аккаунта, сохраняющийся после удаления LB |
| `rename_vpc` | запись | изменить отображаемое имя VPC |
| `enable_nat_gateway` | изменение | включить NAT для VPC: `fip_id` выбирает свободный адрес аккаунта в том же регионе; без него выделяется новый. Адрес и NAT тарифицируются; подключение асинхронное |
| `disable_nat_gateway` | изменение | выключить NAT-шлюз VPC; `retain_ip=true` сохраняет IP за аккаунтом с продолжением тарификации. Снятие NAT асинхро
