readme.markdown:
**English** · [Русский](https://github.com/FROWNINGdev/django-orm-lens/blob/main/docs/i18n/README.ru.md) · [Español](https://github.com/FROWNINGdev/django-orm-lens/blob/main/docs/i18n/README.es.md) · [中文](https://github.com/FROWNINGdev/django-orm-lens/blob/main/docs/i18n/README.zh.md)

# Django ORM Lens

### ER diagrams, N+1 detection and migration-risk checks for Django — without booting it.

Your entire model graph — live in your editor sidebar, gating your CI, and answering your AI agent over MCP. All from static parsing: no database, no `runserver`, no working venv.

**Replaces:** `graph_models` + `django-schema-graph` + hand-drawn ER diagrams + grep archaeology.

<sub>Featured in Django News #347 · PyCoder's Weekly #746</sub>

---

## ⚡ 10 seconds to first insight

```bash
uvx django-orm-lens scan -f table   # every app and model at a glance
uvx django-orm-lens nplusone        # N+1 loops, with the select_related to add
uvx django-orm-lens migration-risk  # migrations that lock tables or fail on existing rows
```

Cold clone, broken venv, no settings module — you still see every app and model of the project, then the N+1 loops and risky migrations in it, right in your terminal. (`uvx` is from [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/); `pipx run` works the same way.)

**Then pick your surface** — three distributions, one parser core:

| You are | Install | You get |
|---|---|---|
| **Editor user** — VS Code / Cursor / Windsurf / VSCodium | `code --install-extension frowningdev.django-orm-lens` | Field autocomplete in `.filter()`, sidebar tree, live ER diagram, hover cards, 18 lint rules with QuickFixes |
| **Terminal / CI user** | `pip install django-orm-lens` | 17 subcommands, SARIF + PR annotations, pre-commit hooks, a GitHub Action |
| **AI-agent user** — Cursor / Claude Code / Aider / Zed / Continue | `pip install "django-orm-lens[mcp]"` | 13 read-only MCP tools answering schema questions from ground truth |

MCP setup is one JSON block — see [Integrations](#-integrations). Point `DJANGO_ORM_LENS_ROOT` at your Django project's absolute path.

---

## 🆓 Paid-tier capabilities, free and MIT

Schema review is a paid category nearly everywhere. A bot that reviews every pull request, analysis that follows a queryset past the function it was built in, a check that catches schema drift, index advice grounded in real table statistics — those normally sit behind a per-seat or per-database subscription.

All of it is here, MIT-licensed, with no tier gate, no seat count, no account, and no telemetry:

| Capability usually sold as a paid tier | Here |
|---|---|
| PR review bot for schema changes — posts once, then updates in place | [`blast-radius`](https://github.com/FROWNINGdev/django-orm-lens/blob/main/docs/rules/blast-radius.md) + the [Action](#️-gate-your-ci) |
| Analysis that follows a queryset across functions | [`nplusone`](docs/rules/nplusone.md) |
| Schema drift detection | [`drift`](docs/rules/drift.md) |
| Index proposals from observed QuerySet usage | `suggest-indexes` |
| Migration risk weighed against real table sizes | `blast-radius --stats` |
| Blast radius of a destructive migration | [`blast-radius`](https://github.com/FROWNINGdev/django-orm-lens/blob/main/docs/rules/blast-radius.md) |
| Cross-layer impact of removing a field | `impact` |

**There is no Pro tier, and none is planned.** If the tool saves you an afternoon, a star is the entire ask.

---

## 📊 Traction

> If the tool saves you a `grep` next time you touch a strange Django project — **[a star helps others find it](https://github.com/FROWNINGdev/django-orm-lens/stargazers)**.

### 📈 Star growth

  
    
      
      
      
    
  

---

## ⚡ Install

**VS Code / Cursor / Windsurf** (VS Code Marketplace):

```bash
code --install-extension frowningdev.django-orm-lens
```

**VSCodium / code-server / Gitpod / any OSS Code fork** (Open VSX):

```bash
codium --install-extension frowningdev.django-orm-lens
```

Or search **`Django ORM Lens`** in the Extensions view — same publisher `frowningdev` on both registries.

**Terminal & AI coding agents:**

```bash
pip install django-orm-lens              # CLI only
pip install "django-orm-lens[mcp]"       # + MCP server for AI agents
```

Requires Python 3.9+. Zero runtime dependencies for the CLI.

**Docker (v0.6+):**

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/workspace" ghcr.io/frowningdev/django-orm-lens scan --path .
```

Multi-arch (amd64 + arm64). No Python required on the host. Good for CI and one-off audits.

## 🎯 The problem

> **Works offline. Works on a broken venv. Works on someone else's laptop. Works in CI.**

You open a Django project. It has 20 apps. You need to answer a simple question:

> _"Which app owns the `Order` model, and how is it connected to `User`?"_

Today, that means: `Ctrl+P`, "models", scroll through 30 hits, open five files, `Ctrl+F` for `class Order`, read through 400 lines of `ForeignKey('otherapp.Something')` strings, try to remember what you learned two files ago.

**Half a day gone. Every time. On every project.**

## ✨ With Django ORM Lens

### 📚 A tree of everything

Every app → every model → every field → every `Meta` option. Grouped by application, sorted alphabetically, expandable.

Icons distinguish `CharField` from `ForeignKey` from `ManyToManyField` at a glance.

### 🕸️ A live ER diagram

One command opens a Mermaid entity-relationship diagram of your entire schema. Watch it redraw as you edit. Export to SVG.

`ForeignKey`, `OneToOneField`, and `ManyToManyField` become proper cardinality arrows.

### 🔎 Hover for relations

Hover over `ForeignKey('app.Model')` in any Python file → a card pops up with the target model's fields, relations, and a "Jump to" link. No `Ctrl+F`, no file dialog.

### 🧭 Jump-to-definition

Click any field in the tree → cursor lands on the exact line. Filter the tree by app or model name. Split `models/` packages are fully supported.

### ⚡ Zero configuration

No `DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE`. No `runserver`. Parses `mo

…

name: Uptimepage
description: Monitor uptime and incidents, run checks, and publish status updates from your Uptimepage org.

tools.name: acknowledge_incident
tools.description: Acknowledge an incident: take ownership and halt escalation. Internal/operational only — does NOT post anything to the public status page. Use post_incident_update for customer-facing updates. Asks for confirmation where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. Not read-only.

inputs.name: id
inputs.description: The incident id.

inputs.name: note
inputs.description: Optional internal note recorded on the incident's activity timeline. This is operator-facing, not published to the public status page.

readme.markdown:
# uptimepage

**Uptime monitoring, status pages and on-call. Open source, free to start. Live in 5 minutes.**

Monitor HTTP, TCP, ICMP ping, cron-job heartbeats, DNS, TLS-certificate and
domain expiry, plus scripted browser login flows, from multiple regions — then
turn green and red into a polished
public status page your customers can subscribe to, and page whoever is on
call through rotations and escalation policies. Drive it by click, REST
API, or Terraform. Self-host the single binary or use the hosted service.

[**Try it free →**](https://uptimepage.dev)  ·  [Docs](https://uptimepage.dev/docs)  ·  [Self-host](#self-host)  ·  [Terraform](#terraform)  ·  [MCP](#mcp-server)

## Quick start

Hosted, no install:

1. Sign up at **[uptimepage.dev](https://uptimepage.dev)** with GitHub, Google or your email address — no card.
2. Add a monitor: paste a URL, pick a check type and interval, save.
3. Bind a notification channel (Slack, email, PagerDuty, …) so failures reach you.
4. Turn on a public status page and share the link.

Prefer code? Drive the same account by [REST API](docs/api.md), [Terraform](#terraform), or [MCP](#mcp-server). Want to run it yourself? Go to [Self-host](#self-host).

## Why uptimepage

Monitoring with a built-in status page isn't new — the bet here is doing it
free, self-hostable, and fully as code:

- **Free hosted tier, no card** — and AGPL if you'd rather run it yourself.
- **One self-contained binary** — `docker compose up` and you're live, not a Kubernetes platform to operate.
- **Everything as code** — REST API, scoped tokens, an official Terraform provider, and an MCP server your LLM can query.
- **Probes you own** — run multi-region agents wherever your users are, on your own boxes.
- **Status page + incidents + on-call in one** — components, subscribers, on-call rotations and escalation, and multi-channel paging that repeats until acknowledged, no second tool.
- **Core isn't paywalled** — checks, status pages, subscribers, the API and every alert channel are in the free tier.

### Who it's for

- **Founders / small SaaS** — a professional status page in minutes, free, no self-host headache.
- **Platform / SRE leads** — monitors as code, multi-region probes, incident paging to your on-call channels, without vendor sprawl.
- **Self-hosters** — one binary plus two databases, no SaaS lock-in.

## Live status

uptimepage monitors itself. These badges are served by the running app from a
public status page — no third-party service, no cron job updating a JSON file.

| Surface | HTTP | DNS | TLS cert | Domain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **uptimepage.dev** (website) | [![http](https://uptimepage.uptimepage.dev/api/public/v1/badge.svg?component=9ffa993c-fc72-4a54-a7d7-259249cd30eb)](https://uptimepage.uptimepage.dev) | [![dns](https://uptimepage.uptimepage.dev/api/public/v1/badge.svg?component=480a9ed0-dc21-4042-9cc3-f67814bc75be)](https://uptimepage.uptimepage.dev) | [![tls](https://uptimepage.uptimepage.dev/api/public/v1/badge.svg?component=70083a5c-0463-4c1e-99e5-c780473a96cf)](https://uptimepage.uptimepage.dev) | [![domain](https://uptimepage.uptimepage.dev/api/public/v1/badge.svg?component=cc34930e-a1d8-41a3-a448-722fec4c28f4)](https://uptimepage.uptimepage.dev) |
| **app.uptimepage.dev** (dashboard) | [![http](https://uptimepage.uptimepage.dev/api/public/v1/badge.svg?component=c2510a68-d830-4e93-b8db-28d0ec5e05ff)](https://uptimepage.uptimepage.dev) | | | |
| **mcp.uptimepage.dev** (MCP) | [![http](https://uptimepage.uptimepage.dev/api/public/v1/badge.svg?component=49f2209c-d54e-49fd-a38a-bc5f03b9f77f)](https://uptimepage.uptimepage.dev) | | | |

Embed your own with the snippet in **Settings → Pages → your page → Badge**.

## Features

| | |
|---|---|
| **Checks** | HTTP, TCP, ICMP ping, heartbeat (inbound dead-man's-switch), DNS, TLS-cert expiry, domain expiry, browser login flow with per-step timings, manual (state set by an operator); a circuit breaker per monitor, designed for ~50k concurrent in-flight |
| **Public status page** | HTML + JSON + RSS, per-component opt-in, incident narration, maintenance windows, email + webhook subscribers |
| **Alerting** | Slack, PagerDuty, Discord, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, Mattermost, Telegram, WhatsApp, SMS, email, webhook, ntfy, Gotify, Pushover — per-org channels, sealed secrets, fire-once + recovery, repeat until acknowledged |
| **Incidents** | Internal incident state ⊥ public phase, acknowledge to silence paging, per-monitor reminder cadence |
| **On-call** | Layered rotations (daily, weekly, custom) with weekly hours, calendar overrides, your shifts as an iCalendar feed, escalation policies that page channels and schedules level by level |
| **Multi-region** | Regional probe agents, per-region views, run your own agent anywhere |
| **Automation** | REST API, scoped API tokens, Terraform provider, MCP server for LLM clients |
| **Built on** | Rust 1.95 / Tokio / Axum, Postgres + ClickHouse, one ~23 MB self-contained binary |

**Live service: <https://uptimepage.dev>** — hosted, free, sign in with GitHub, Google or your email address.
**Full docs: <https://uptimepage.dev/docs>**

## Check types

| Type | Purpose | Default interval | Floor |
|---|---|---|---|
| `http` | request a URL, match status / body / latency | 60 s | `max(plan_min, 10 s)` |
| `tcp` | open a TCP socket within a timeout | 60 s | `max(plan_min, 10 s)` |
| `ping` | ICMP echo request, fail on a missing reply | 60 s | `max(plan_min, 10 s)` |
| `heartbeat` | your job pings a URL; a missing ping past period + grace opens an incident | 60 s | `max(plan_min, 60 s)` |
| `dns` | resolve a record, optionally match a value | 60 s | `max(plan_min, 10 s)` |
| `tls_cert` | open TLS, parse leaf cert, alert before `notAfter` | 86 400 s (daily) | `max(plan_min, 3600 s)` |
| `domain_expiry` | query RDA

# mcphost

where agents host their own tools · [mcphost.dev](https://mcphost.dev) · [status](https://mcphost.dev/status.html) · [llms.txt](https://mcphost.dev/llms.txt) · [llms-install.md](https://mcphost.dev/llms-install.md)

Find it in the registry: [dev.mcphost/mcphost](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers/dev.mcphost%2Fmcphost/versions/latest) — connect with the one-URL quickstart at [mcphost.dev](https://mcphost.dev).

## What it is

mcphost is a remote MCP server where your agent publishes its own tools. Your agent writes a tool mid-task, publishes it with one call, and keeps working: the tool is live with no restart and no deploy, and it outlives the conversation that built it. A schedule can fire it while you sleep, another agent can share it, and every run lands in a log you can read.

Under the hood, `mcphost serve` is one Rust binary that speaks streamable-HTTP MCP at a single endpoint. Everything is a tool call: publish, run, schedule, log, meter, store secrets, share with another agent, act as one of your end users over OAuth. There is no dashboard; `/status` is the one page, and the operator works through `admin.*` tools on the same endpoint.

Measured, not promised: p95 34.2 ms across 200 concurrent calls with zero errors, committed next to the test that produces it. The public site is [mcphost.dev](https://mcphost.dev); the machine-readable summary at [`/llms.txt`](https://mcphost.dev/llms.txt) is generated from the same source as the quickstart below (`docs/agent-quickstart.md`, `scripts/gen-agent-docs.sh`).

## Connect

Paste one line into your client and it has mcphost. Your agent's first call creates its account on that connection: no signup form, no key to paste.

**Claude Code**

```
claude mcp add --transport http mcphost https://mcphost.dev/mcp
```

Docs: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp> (checked 2026-10-09)

**Cursor**

[Add to Cursor](cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=mcphost&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL21jcGhvc3QuZGV2L21jcCJ9), or add `https://mcphost.dev/mcp` to your MCP config directly.

Docs: <https://docs.cursor.com/en/tools/mcp> (checked 2026-10-09)

**VS Code**

[Add to VS Code](vscode:mcp/install?%7B%22name%22%3A%22mcphost%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22http%22%2C%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fmcphost%2Edev%2Fmcp%22%7D), or add `https://mcphost.dev/mcp` to your MCP config directly.

Docs: <https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-guides/ai/mcp> (checked 2026-10-09)

# Grey Ridge Signals — Agent-Native x402 Data & Security APIs

**Pay-per-call crypto, DeFi, prediction-market, and on-chain data for AI agents — plus MCP
security scanning — over the [x402 payment protocol](https://x402.org) on Base mainnet.**

No account, no API key, no subscription. An agent pays inline in USDC (from $0.001/call) and
gets the data back in the same request. Every data endpoint has a **free preview** so an agent
can taste the payload before paying.

- **Base URL:** `https://x402-data-api.sigrunner.workers.dev`
- **MCP endpoint (streamable-http):** `https://x402-data-api.sigrunner.workers.dev/mcp`
- **Canonical domain:** `https://x402-data-api.sigrunner.workers.dev` (same API)
- **Discovery:** [`/.well-known/x402`](https://x402-data-api.sigrunner.workers.dev/.well-known/x402) · [`/openapi.json`](https://x402-data-api.sigrunner.workers.dev/openapi.json) · [`/llms.txt`](https://x402-data-api.sigrunner.workers.dev/llms.txt)
- **Network:** Base mainnet (`eip155:8453`), USDC. Settles via the non-custodial [xpay](https://facilitator.xpay.sh) facilitator — no Coinbase/CDP account needed. Also listed on the CDP x402 Bazaar.

---

## Two flagships — what agents actually pay for

1. **MCP server security scan** (`/scan/mcp`, $0.05) — a prompt-injection / tool-poisoning audit of an MCP server's tools (OWASP LLM01/LLM08). **Zero-egress**: for private/OAuth-gated servers you POST only the `tools/list` JSON — nothing else leaves your side. *There is no free equivalent for this* (unlike token-safety, where free multi-chain scanners exist). Free preview: `POST /scan/mcp/preview`. CI gate (on the [GitHub Marketplace](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/mcp-server-tool-poisoning-scan)): `uses: rezearcher/greyridge-x402-tools@v0.3.2`.
2. **Pre-trade decision gate** (`/gate/swap`, $0.008 · `/chain/token-report`, $0.01) — a *decision* (GO/HOLD/BLOCK, SAFE/CAUTION/AVOID) sized to your trade, not raw flags your agent has to interpret. **Base-native**; if you trade other chains, keep your multi-chain scanner and use this on Base.

Everything below is the full catalog (crypto/DeFi data, on-chain reads, LLM, enrichment). Measured reliability at [`/status`](https://x402-data-api.sigrunner.workers.dev/status) (not an SLA).

---

## Endpoints

### Crypto & DeFi data
| Endpoint | Price | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /crypto/prices?coins=bitcoin,ethereum,solana` | $0.001 | Spot token prices (DefiLlama), keyless. Up to 25 CoinGecko ids. |
| `GET /crypto/funding?limit=20` | $0.001 | **Cross-venue** perp funding rates (Hyperliquid + OKX, graceful fallback) with the **funding spread** + best long/short venue — the arb signal, not just a single-venue list. |
| `GET /defi/yields?limit=20&project=&chain=&stable=` | $0.001 | Top DeFi lending/LP yields (DefiLlama) with APY breakdown, **7d/30d APY trend, IL risk, and DefiLlama's stability forecast** — decision-grade, not a raw list. |
| `GET /pm/markets?query=&limit=20` | $0.005 | Live Polymarket prediction markets: question, outcomes, prices, volume, liquidity, end date. |

### Base on-chain (JSON-RPC read primitives)
Base-native, multi-provider RPC with automatic failover (never fails a paid call on one provider's rate limit).

| Endpoint | Price | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /chain/block-number` | $0.001 | Current Base block number |
| `GET /chain/gas-price` | $0.001 | Current gas price (wei + gwei) |
| `GET /chain/balance?address=` | $0.001 | Native ETH balance |
| `GET /chain/token-balance?address=&token=` | $0.001 | ERC-20 token balance |

readme.markdown:
# Speak To Your Database (STYD)

**Odoo, PostgreSQL & MySQL MCP server for Claude and ChatGPT. Ask your business data in plain words, from the AI app you already use. Real numbers, computed read-only from your data.**

STYD is a hosted MCP server. Connect it once to Claude, ChatGPT, Le Chat, VS Code or any app that supports remote MCP servers, then ask things like:

- "How much revenue did we make last month, compared with the month before?"
- "Which customer invoices are overdue, and how much does each customer owe?"
- "Show all sales orders grouped by customer and status, with the number of orders, the total amount and the date range."
- "Top 10 products by sales this year"
- "Why did sales drop this month?"

Follow-ups work too: after the sales orders question, ask *"and only the confirmed ones?"* and STYD keeps the same grouping.

STYD works out the answer from your data and sends back the numbers, with the period and the definition it used (for example, *revenue = posted customer invoices, excluding tax*).

- Website: https://speaktoyourdatabase.com
- MCP endpoint: `https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp`
- Demo video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZffAbynuc0
- Docs: https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/docs/mcp
- Odoo MCP guide: https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/docs/odoo-mcp

> This repository holds the public setup guide and the registry file. STYD itself is a hosted service; its source code is not public.

---

## Odoo MCP connector

STYD is an Odoo MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT and other MCP apps. Ask about sales, invoices, unpaid amounts, customers, products and stock in plain words, and get the figures with what was counted, over which period and with which filters.

- **Odoo 15 to 20**, on Odoo Online, Odoo.sh or your own server.
- **Two ways to connect:** an Odoo API key (Online, Odoo.sh, on-premise) or the free STYD Bridge module (Odoo.sh, on-premise).
- **Read-only:** STYD cannot create, change or delete anything in Odoo.
- **Nothing to install on your computer:** STYD is hosted, and your AI app signs in to your STYD account.
- **Several companies:** each company stays in its own workspace, and every answer names the one it comes from.

Example questions: *"Which customers owe us the most, and how much is overdue?"*, *"Top 5 products by quantity sold this quarter"*, *"Compare this month's sales with the same month last year."*

Full guide: https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/docs/odoo-mcp

## Try it in 2 minutes

1. Add the connector to your AI app (see below).
2. Sign in to STYD when your app asks. The free plan includes sample data, so you can ask questions straight away.
3. When you are ready, connect your own Odoo, PostgreSQL or MySQL database at https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/connections.

## Set up in your AI app

### Claude (web, desktop, mobile)

Open **Settings → Connectors**, search the directory for **Speak To Your Database**, and click **Connect**.
Directory page: https://claude.ai/directory/speak-to-your-database

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http styd https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp
```

Then run `/mcp` in Claude Code and sign in.

### VS Code (GitHub Copilot)

Run **MCP: Add Server** from the Command Palette, choose **HTTP**, and paste `https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp`. Or add this to `.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "styd": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Start the server, sign in when VS Code asks, then use Copilot Chat in **Agent** mode.

### Le Chat (Mistral)

Add a custom MCP connector with the URL `https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp`, then sign in to STYD when asked.

### ChatGPT

Open **Plugins** in ChatGPT, search for **Speak To Your Database**, and click **Install plugin**. Sign in to STYD when asked.
Plugin page: https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6ac9e3034d488191bd0b9a624cb1f0ae

### Cursor and other apps

Any app that supports remote MCP servers with OAuth sign-in can use `https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp`. For Cursor and apps without sign-in support, use a workspace API key: see https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/docs/mcp/other-apps.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `list_workspaces` | Lists the STYD workspaces (companies) you belong to |
| `list_connections` | Lists the data sources in a workspace: Odoo, PostgreSQL, MySQL, sample data |
| `describe_available_data` | Shows what a connection can answer, with example questions |
| `ask_question` | Asks one business question and returns the answer computed from your data |
| `get_answer` | Fetches the result of a longer-running question |

Every answer names the workspace it comes from, so data from different companies is never mixed.

## Security

STYD reads your data; it never changes it.

- **Read-only:** STYD cannot create, change or delete anything in Odoo or your databases.
- **Secrets protected:** database passwords and API keys are stored encrypted and never shown back.
- **Standard sign-in:** AI apps connect through OAuth. You approve each app on a STYD consent page, and you can revoke it at any time.
- **Uploaded files checked** with a malware scan before use.
- **Backups** with an encrypted off-site copy.
- **Abuse protection** and rate limits.
- **Not used for training:** your data and questions are not used to train AI models.

Details: https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/security and https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/privacy

Need STYD on your own server, with nothing leaving your network? See https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/private.

## Registry

STYD is published in the official MCP Registry as `com.speaktoyourdatabase/styd` (the [`server.json`](server.json) in this repository) and as `com.speaktoyourdatabase/odoo-mcp` (the Odoo MCP connector entry).

Also listed in the [ChatGPT plugin directory](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6ac9e3034d488191bd0b9a624cb1f0ae), the [Claude connectors directory](https://claude.ai/directory/speak-to-your-database) and

### The Apple docs MCP your AI actually deserves.

*Apple docs. WWDC26 transcripts. RAG retrieval + [Jev](https://typesafe.ai/) relevance ranking. One clean tool.*

[Website](https://apple-rag.com) · Powered by [ Jev](https://typesafe.ai/)

[![CI](https://github.com/BingoWon/apple-rag-mcp/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/BingoWon/apple-rag-mcp/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE) [![Listed on mcpservers.org](https://mcpservers.org/badge.svg)](https://mcpservers.org/servers/bingowon/apple-rag-mcp) · **English** | [中文](./README.zh-CN.md)

---

## Not Just Another Docs Tool

Hybrid retrieval combines keyword and semantic search to find Apple sources. [Jev](https://typesafe.ai/) then ranks the merged candidates for relevance to your question, bringing the best matches to your agent.

**Minimal footprint. Maximum signal.** Our MCP tools are designed to be lean—no bloated responses, no wasted tokens, no noise cluttering your agent's context. Just the information that matters.

### Powered by [ Jev](https://typesafe.ai/)

[Jev](https://typesafe.ai/), a decision model, scores candidate Apple documentation
and video transcripts against each query's API, platform, and version requirements.
We use its relevance scores to rank the sources returned through MCP. A backup
reranker takes over if the API call fails.

---

## Open Source. Ready to Use.

The [hosted service](https://apple-rag.com/) connects your agent to an Apple knowledge base that is already collected, cleaned, and indexed.

- **Ready-to-query sources:** Official developer documentation and video transcripts, available through one connection.
- **Retrieval model calls included:** Embeddings, [Jev](https://typesafe.ai/) ranking, and the backup reranker run on our service.
- **Ongoing upkeep:** We handle content collection, index updates, database backups, and protocol compatibility.

The source is public for inspection and self-hosting. Running your own instance means operating a database, building and refreshing your corpus, and managing your model API credentials.

[Start free](https://apple-rag.com/). [Pro](https://apple-rag.com/#pricing) includes 50,000 tool calls/week and 50/minute for $1/week, shared by `search` and `fetch`.

---

## Start in Seconds

**Configure with your agent:** In the [dashboard](https://apple-rag.com/overview),
select a token and click **Copy Install Prompt**. Paste it into your current
agent to configure the connection and verify the tools.

**One click:**

Open [Cursor](https://cursor.com) and confirm installation.

### Option 2: Manual Setup for Other MCP Clients

**JSON Configuration (Copy & Paste):**
This is a configuration example, not a universal client format. The dashboard
also retains manual configuration examples.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "apple-rag-mcp": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.apple-rag.com"
    }
  }
}
```

**Manual Configuration Parameters:**
- **MCP Type:** `Streamable HTTP`
- **URL:** `https://mcp.apple-rag.com`
- **Protocol:** `2026-07-28`, with legacy `initialize` support for `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18`, and `2025-03-26`
- **Authentication:** `Optional` (MCP Token for higher limits)
- **MCP Token:** Get yours at [apple-rag.com](https://apple-rag.com) for increased quota

Saving a configuration alone does not verify a working connection.

> **Note:** No MCP Token required to start! You get free queries without any authentication. Add an MCP Token later for higher usage limits.

## 🌟 Why Developers Love Apple RAG MCP

### ⚡ **Fast & Reliable**
Get quick responses with our optimized search infrastructure. No more hunting through docs.

### 🎯 **AI-Powered Hybrid Search**
Hybrid search combines keyword and semantic retrieval for Apple documentation and video transcripts. [Jev](https://typesafe.ai/) then ranks the combined candidates against your question, giving your agent more relevant context.

### 🔒 **Always Secure**
MCP authentication ensures trusted access for your AI agents with enterprise-grade security.

### 📝 **Code Examples**
Get practical code examples in Swift, Objective-C, and SwiftUI alongside documentation references.

### 🔄 **Real-time Updates**
Our documentation index is continuously updated for WWDC26, Xcode 27 beta, and the latest Apple developer resources.

### 🆓 **Start Free**
Try without an account: 30 tool calls/week and 3/minute. Register at [apple-rag.com](https://apple-rag.com/) for 50/week and 5/minute, shared by `search` and `fetch`.

## 🎯 Features

- **🔍 Semantic Search** - Vector similarity with semantic understanding for intelligent retrieval
- **🔎 Keyword Search** - Precise technical term matching for API names and specific terminology
- **🎯 Hybrid Search** - Combines keyword and semantic retrieval
- **📚 Complete Coverage** - iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27, tvOS 27, and visionOS 27 documentation
- **🎬 WWDC26 Videos** - Full transcripts from Apple Developer videos and WWDC26 sessions
- **⚡ Fast Response** - Optimized for speed across all content types
- **🚀 High Performance** - Multi-instance cluster deployment for maximum throughput
- **🔄 Always Current** - Synced with Apple's latest docs, WWDC26 sessions, and Xcode 27 beta references
- **🛡️ Secure & Private** - Your queries stay private
- **🌐 MCP 2026 Native** - Stateless MCP `2026-07-28`, with legacy Streamable HTTP compatibility

readme.markdown: # Codex Bridge 简体中文 | English **Codex Bridge** 是一个面向个人自托管场景的原生 macOS App 与后台 Service。它把 ChatGPT 网页版、Qwen Studio 和本机工作台连接到已授权的本地项目，并在同一套任务、审批、对话和持久化系统中运行 Codex、OpenCode、DeepSeek Harness 与 Antigravity。 Bridge 不依赖开发者自建的云端中转、账号系统或远程数据库。通过 ChatGPT、模型 API 或 Provider 执行任务时，请求内容仍会发送给你主动选择和配置的对应服务；“本地优先”不等于所有数据永远不离开 Mac。 ## 当前能力 | 层级 | 当前实现 | | --- | --- | | ChatGPT 网页版 | OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel；Tunnel Helper 随正式 App 打包并由 Service 管理 | | Qwen Studio | 本机回环 Streamable HTTP `/mcp`；App 一键复制带认证 Header 的 JSON | | Codex | 默认 Provider；`codex app-server --stdio`、Thread/Turn、实时 steer、interrupt、审批与 Supervisor | | OpenCode | ACP stdio；Plan/Build、动态模型与 effort、permission 回传、同 Session 排队继续 | | DeepSeek Harness | 固定版本 ACP 适配；外部 `cordis.yml`、模型/effort、Web/工具/子代理、执行证据与逐次本机审批 | | Antigravity | `agy` CLI stream-json；Plan/Accept Edits、原生 sandbox、CLI 权限规则、会话继续与 queued steer | | Direct Workspace | 受控读写、revision 校验、Patch、结构化命令、进程会话和本地 Git 提交 | | Skills | 安全发现 `SKILL.md`，只执行显式声明的 Action | 外部 Agent 必须由用户明确登记、Probe、启用并在任务中显式选择；没有 `provider_id` 的 `submit_task` 始终使用 Codex。 ## 架构 ```text ChatGPT Web Qwen Studio │ OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel │ localhost /mcp └──────────────────┬────────────────┘ ▼ CodexBridgeService ├─ MCP / XPC 应用服务 ├─ 单一 service.sqlite ├─ 项目策略与本机审批 ├─ Provider 任务协调 ├─ Direct Workspace └─ Tunnel / Skill 生命周期 │ ┌──────────────┼───────────────┬────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ Codex app-server OpenCode ACP DeepSeek Harness ACP agy CLI │ └─ Supervisor（当前仅 Codex） CodexBridge.app ── XPC ──► CodexBridgeService 项目 / 工作台 / 连接 / 设置 / 审批 / 状态 ``` 生产 Service 只使用一个 SQLite 数据库保存项目、设置、任务、消息和展示事件。App 负责配置、查看和本机授权，不持有 Provider、MCP、Tunnel 或 Supervisor 的进程生命周期。 ## 快速开始 完整首次配置请直接阅读 [详细使用指南](./docs/USER_GUIDE.md)。以下步骤用于快速建立正确顺序。 ### 1. 安装并启动 - 运行环境：macOS 14.0 或更高版本，支持 Apple Silicon 与 Intel。 - 发布包按 `arm64` 与 `x86_64` 分开提供；请选择与 Mac 一致的架构。 - 首次打开后，如果 App 显示“等待 macOS 登录项批准”，点击“打开系统设置”并允许 Codex Bridge 后台 Service，然后回到 App 刷新状态。 - 关闭窗口不会停止 Service。`设置 → 后台运行与远程 Agent 授权` 中的“退出 App 后保持后台服务运行”决定按 ⌘Q 后是否继续，默认开启。 从源码构建： ```bash git clone https://github.com/yeyuancc0-glitch/codex-bridge.git cd codex-bridge Scripts/with-xcode.sh xcodebuild \ -project CodexBridge.xcodeproj \ -scheme CodexBridge \ -configuration Debug \ -destination 'platform=macOS,arch=arm64' \ -derivedDataPath .build/Xcode \ build CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO ``` 普通 Debug 构建可能没有打包 OpenAI `tunnel-client`，因此可以使用本地 MCP，但未必能连接 ChatGPT Secure Tunnel。ChatGPT 接入请使用“连接”页面显示 Helper 就绪的正式构建。 ### 2. 添加项目并设置硬权限 1. 打开 `项目 → 添加`，选择允许 Bridge 访问的项目根目录。 2. 在项目的“访问与执行权限”中配置读取、写入与网络策略。 3. 需要 Direct 命令时，再配置命令模式、允许命令和工作目录。 Bridge 只接受已登记项目。项目硬策略优先于 Workbench 默认和单任务请求；项目禁止写入时，任何 Provider 的写模式都会被收窄。 ### 3. 选择远程任务默认项目与模式 打开 `工作台`： 1. 选择 ChatGPT/Qwen 新任务应使用的项目。 2. 在“GPT/Qwen 新任务”中选择 `Read Only` 或 `Write`。 远程请求省略 `project_id` 时使用这里选中的项目。若显式传入 `project_id`，它必须来自 MCP `list_projects`，不能填写项目显示名。远程客户端通常应省略权限覆盖字段，使用 Workbench 的统一默认值。 ### 4. 配置执行 Provider - **Codex**：默认 Provider，不在“本机 Agent 引擎连接”中登记。请先在官方 Codex/ChatGPT 环境完成登录，再到 `设置 → Codex 执行默认偏好` 选择模型、effort、访问权限和 Fast 模式。Bridge 不读取 Codex 认证文件。 - **OpenCode**：`连接 → 本机 Agent 引擎连接 → 登记 Agent → OpenCode`，选择真实 `opencode` 可执行文件并 Probe。详见 [OpenCode 连接指南](./docs/OPENCODE_CONNECTION_GUIDE.md)。 - **DeepSeek Harness**：登记官方 `dsh-v0.1.1-rc.2` 构建出的 `packages/examples/acp-demo/lib/bin.js`，再选择 DSH 源码树之外的 `cordis.yml`；为隔离凭据，建议 Profile 也位于任务项目和 Bridge 仓库之外。`.env` 与 `cordis.yml` 同目录，由 Harness 自己读取。详见 [DeepSeek Harness 接入指南](./docs/DEEPSEEK_HARNESS_CONNECTION_GUIDE.md)。 - **Antigravity**：先用 `command -v agy` 找到真实 CLI，在目标项目中交互登录，并通过 `/settings`、`/permissions` 配置 headless 所需的命令、URL 与 MCP 规则；不要登记 Desktop App。详见 [Antigravity / AGY 连接与权限指南](./docs/ANTIGRAVITY_CONNECTION_GUIDE.md)。 外部 Provider 登记成功后还要打开“启用”，然后到 `设置` 中刷新该 Provider 的模型目录并保存默认模型/effort。模型 ID 以当前 Provider 实际返回值为准，不要跨 Provider 猜别名。 ### 外部 Provider 权限要点 - ChatGPT/Qwen 的 `Read Only / Write` 由工作台决定；Provider 设置页中的访问权限只是后备默认。 - DSH 保持 `approval.policy: ask`，运行中在工作台对每个 `session/request_permission` 选择“仅本次允许”或拒绝。`full-access` 和自动批准任务启动都不会跳过该步骤。 - AGY 正常使用前，必须在交互式 `agy` 的 `/settings` 中确认 **Tool Permission = `proceed-in-sandbox`**（沙箱内终端命令自动执行），再用 Project 作用域的 `/permissions` 添加窄 allow 规则。Bridge 已强制传入 `--sandbox`。 - readme.markdown:
# plori

**Plori runs AI agents that collaborate on one product in the cloud.**

[Plori](https://plori.ai) runs AI agents that collaborate on one product in the cloud.
Code, research, content: each works on its own copy, and Plori merges their changes
back. The agents work in a cloud Workspace that keeps the product's files with saved
revisions. Only the Workspace files persist between runs. You talk to your
agents in the web app, or drive them from your own tools over MCP and REST.

This repository is the integration front door. The product itself lives at
[plori.ai](https://plori.ai); the remote MCP server lives at `https://api.plori.ai/mcp`.

## Connect your MCP client

plori is a **remote** MCP server (streamable HTTP). There is nothing to install or run
locally. Sign-in happens in your browser via OAuth 2.1 the first time your client
connects; headless environments can use an API key instead.

**Claude Code**

Paste this into your Claude Code conversation:

> Set up https://plori.ai/SKILL.md

Claude reads the setup instructions and configures MCP if needed. If the new server
has not loaded, type `/reload-plugins` when Claude asks, then continue in the same
conversation. With pairing, open the short address Claude shows, enter the code,
sign in, and approve. You can use a phone while Claude Code runs on a remote machine.
No installed skill or plugin is required.

**Cursor**

Use the one-click [Add to Cursor](https://plori.ai/mcp) button, or add manually:
`Settings -> MCP -> Add server` with URL `https://api.plori.ai/mcp`.

**VS Code**

```sh
code --add-mcp '{"name":"plori","type":"http","url":"https://api.plori.ai/mcp"}'
```

**Codex CLI**

```sh
codex mcp add plori --url https://api.plori.ai/mcp
codex mcp login plori
```

Codex auto-detects plori's OAuth on `login`. One-install alternative with the skill
bundled: `codex plugin marketplace add plori-ai/codex-plugin` then `codex plugin add
plori@plori`.

**Cline**

Follow [llms-install.md](./llms-install.md), written for Cline's automated installer.

**Any other client**

Native streamable-HTTP clients connect to `https://api.plori.ai/mcp` directly. Clients
that only speak stdio can bridge with the [`plori-mcp` npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/plori-mcp)
(a thin wrapper around `mcp-remote` with the endpoint pinned; this repository is its source):

```sh
npx plori-mcp
# headless / CI: authenticate with an API key instead of the OAuth flow
npx plori-mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer plori_sk_..."
# equivalent, without the wrapper:
npx mcp-remote https://api.plori.ai/mcp
```

API keys are minted in [Dashboard -> Settings](https://plori.ai/dashboard/settings) on
a registered account.

## Or skip MCP: your own terminal

The [plori CLI](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@plori/cli) is not an MCP client. It is a
door of its own, and it opens the same live session the web app shows: the recent
history, a prompt, streaming output, and the approval queue in one place. A turn you
send in the terminal appears in an open browser tab as it streams.

```sh
curl -fsSL https://plori.ai/install.sh | sh
plori login && plori attach <agent-name>
```

The installer drops one static binary in `~/.local/bin` and needs no Node; if that
directory is not on your PATH yet, the script prints the line to add. `npm i -g
@plori/cli` works too. The argument to `attach` is an agent name, an agent id, or a
session id, so a session id copied out of the web app works on its own. `Ctrl-D`
detaches and leaves the run going on the server.

The terminal does not give the agent access to your local files. The shell and the
Workspace files are in Plori's cloud.

## Verify the connection

Ask your client:

> List my plori Workspaces and tell me how many credits I have left.

You should see `list_workspaces` and `get_credits` tool calls and a real answer.

## What the tools do

The server exposes 24 tools in five groups. A Workspace holds durable files with
saved revisions, a main conversation, and run history. An agent runs in a Workspace
with a shell and the Workspace files under `/workspace`.

- **Workspaces and account**: `list_workspaces` (the Workspaces you own, with state,
  default agent, current revision, and `storage_readiness` while storage starts),
  `create_workspace` (a Workspace with its first revision. Unless you pass
  `default_manager_agent_id`, it also creates a default agent. `idempotency_key`
  makes a retry return the same Workspace), `delete_workspace` (permanently delete a
  Workspace with its files, revisions, copies, and conversations),
  `read_workspace_file` (a file or a directory listing in a saved revision),
  `upload_workspace_file` (write a file into a Workspace's current files, replacing
  any file at path; pass UTF-8 text as `content`, or omit `content` for a one-time
  `upload_url` for a larger or binary file),
  `get_workspace_costs` (the amount charged for the runs of a Workspace or of one
  task group in a time window), `get_credits` (prepaid balance, plan, and limits).
- **Runs**: `send_workspace_message` (send a message to a Workspace conversation and
  wait for the reply, with `wait_seconds` to set how long to hold, `idempotency_key`
  to make a retry return the original run, and `callback_url` plus `callback_secret`
  to post a signed status notification to your endpoint), `get_run_result` (a run's
  status, timestamps, credits, tokens, tool progress, and the reply once it
  finishes; for a Workspace manager that waits for its workers, `worker_inputs`
  lists the workers' open questions and approvals and `next_run_id` names the
  run that continues it), `list_runs` (an agent's run history, most recent first), `cancel_run`
  (stop an in-flight run, which reports `cancelling` and then `cancelled`),
  `schedule_run` (run an agent once later, after a delay or at a timestamp. It
  returns `awaiting_confirmation` and a `confirm_url`. Plori queues the run only
  after you confirm it in the Plori web app).

readme.markdown:
# Speak To Your Database (STYD)

**Odoo, PostgreSQL & MySQL MCP server for Claude and ChatGPT. Ask your business data in plain words, from the AI app you already use. Real numbers, computed read-only from your data.**

STYD is a hosted MCP server. Connect it once to Claude, ChatGPT, Le Chat, VS Code or any app that supports remote MCP servers, then ask things like:

- "How much revenue did we make last month, compared with the month before?"
- "Which customer invoices are overdue, and how much does each customer owe?"
- "Show all sales orders grouped by customer and status, with the number of orders, the total amount and the date range."
- "Top 10 products by sales this year"
- "Why did sales drop this month?"

Follow-ups work too: after the sales orders question, ask *"and only the confirmed ones?"* and STYD keeps the same grouping.

STYD works out the answer from your data and sends back the numbers, with the period and the definition it used (for example, *revenue = posted customer invoices, excluding tax*).

- Website: https://speaktoyourdatabase.com
- MCP endpoint: `https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp`
- Demo video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZffAbynuc0
- Docs: https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/docs/mcp
- Odoo MCP guide: https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/docs/odoo-mcp

> This repository holds the public setup guide and the registry file. STYD itself is a hosted service; its source code is not public.

---

## Odoo MCP connector

STYD is an Odoo MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT and other MCP apps. Ask about sales, invoices, unpaid amounts, customers, products and stock in plain words, and get the figures with what was counted, over which period and with which filters.

- **Odoo 15 to 20**, on Odoo Online, Odoo.sh or your own server.
- **Two ways to connect:** an Odoo API key (Online, Odoo.sh, on-premise) or the free STYD Bridge module (Odoo.sh, on-premise).
- **Read-only:** STYD cannot create, change or delete anything in Odoo.
- **Nothing to install on your computer:** STYD is hosted, and your AI app signs in to your STYD account.
- **Several companies:** each company stays in its own workspace, and every answer names the one it comes from.

Example questions: *"Which customers owe us the most, and how much is overdue?"*, *"Top 5 products by quantity sold this quarter"*, *"Compare this month's sales with the same month last year."*

Full guide: https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/docs/odoo-mcp

## Try it in 2 minutes

1. Add the connector to your AI app (see below).
2. Sign in to STYD when your app asks. The free plan includes sample data, so you can ask questions straight away.
3. When you are ready, connect your own Odoo, PostgreSQL or MySQL database at https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/connections.

## Set up in your AI app

### Claude (web, desktop, mobile)

Open **Settings → Connectors**, search the directory for **Speak To Your Database**, and click **Connect**.
Directory page: https://claude.ai/directory/speak-to-your-database

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http styd https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp
```

Then run `/mcp` in Claude Code and sign in.

### VS Code (GitHub Copilot)

Run **MCP: Add Server** from the Command Palette, choose **HTTP**, and paste `https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp`. Or add this to `.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "styd": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Start the server, sign in when VS Code asks, then use Copilot Chat in **Agent** mode.

### Le Chat (Mistral)

Add a custom MCP connector with the URL `https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp`, then sign in to STYD when asked.

### ChatGPT

Open **Plugins** in ChatGPT, search for **Speak To Your Database**, and click **Install plugin**. Sign in to STYD when asked.
Plugin page: https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6ac9e3034d488191bd0b9a624cb1f0ae

### Cursor and other apps

Any app that supports remote MCP servers with OAuth sign-in can use `https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp`. For Cursor and apps without sign-in support, use a workspace API key: see https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/docs/mcp/other-apps.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `list_workspaces` | Lists the STYD workspaces (companies) you belong to |
| `list_connections` | Lists the data sources in a workspace: Odoo, PostgreSQL, MySQL, sample data |
| `describe_available_data` | Shows what a connection can answer, with example questions |
| `ask_question` | Asks one business question and returns the answer computed from your data |
| `get_answer` | Fetches the result of a longer-running question |

Every answer names the workspace it comes from, so data from different companies is never mixed.

## Security

STYD reads your data; it never changes it.

- **Read-only:** STYD cannot create, change or delete anything in Odoo or your databases.
- **Secrets protected:** database passwords and API keys are stored encrypted and never shown back.
- **Standard sign-in:** AI apps connect through OAuth. You approve each app on a STYD consent page, and you can revoke it at any time.
- **Uploaded files checked** with a malware scan before use.
- **Backups** with an encrypted off-site copy.
- **Abuse protection** and rate limits.
- **Not used for training:** your data and questions are not used to train AI models.

Details: https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/security and https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/privacy

Need STYD on your own server, with nothing leaving your network? See https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/private.

## Registry

STYD is published in the official MCP Registry as `com.speaktoyourdatabase/styd` (the [`server.json`](server.json) in this repository) and as `com.speaktoyourdatabase/odoo-mcp` (the Odoo MCP connector entry).

Also listed in the [ChatGPT plugin directory](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6ac9e3034d488191bd0b9a624cb1f0ae), the [Claude connectors directory](https://claude.ai/directory/speak-to-your-database) and

readme.markdown:
biblical-atlas-mcp

  
  

biblical-atlas-mcp is an MCP server that gives AI agents the [biblical-atlas](https://github.com/GeiserX/biblical-atlas) Bible atlas as ten read-only tools: people, places, events, reigns, letters, journeys and Bible passages. Answers carry the atlas id, a link to the record's card on [the atlas site](https://biblical-atlas.geiser.cloud/) where the record has one, and links to its sources: a list answer carries the first one and the total, and `get_record` returns them all. The atlas is in Spanish, and the server returns its names and summaries as they are.

## Features

- Search every record by its Spanish name; accents and case are ignored ("jerusalen" finds Jerusalén).
- Read one record in full: family and relations in both directions, offices, coordinates and candidate sites, what happened at a place.
- List events by year or range, person, place, role, kind or Bible book, in date or story order.
- Ask who was alive, ruling or active in a year, with the evidence for each person.
- Look up a Bible reference ("Hch 16:1", "Hch 16", "Rut") and get the events, people, places and records that cite it.
- Find the shortest chain of family ties, succession and companionship between two people.
- Find places within a radius of a place or a coordinate.
- Years are signed in both directions: -607 means 607 a.e.c.
- No database and no atlas data in the package: the server downloads the atlas's public data file, caches it and refreshes it hourly with a conditional request.

## Quick start

Needs Node.js 18 or newer. The npm package downloads the release binary for your platform on first run and checks it against the checksums published with the package.

| Client | Setup |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `claude mcp add biblical-atlas -- npx -y biblical-atlas-mcp` |
| Claude Desktop | `claude_desktop_config.json`: the `mcpServers` block below |
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/mcp.json` or `.cursor/mcp.json`: the `mcpServers` block below |
| VS Code | `.vscode/mcp.json`: the `servers` block below |
| Codex | `~/.codex/config.toml`: the TOML block below |

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "biblical-atlas": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "biblical-atlas-mcp"] }
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "biblical-atlas": { "type": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "biblical-atlas-mcp"] }
  }
}
```

```toml
[mcp_servers.biblical-atlas]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "biblical-atlas-mcp"]
```

Then ask "who was alive in 607 a.e.c.?". The container image for HTTP clients, release binaries and every setting are in [Getting started](https://github.com/GeiserX/biblical-atlas-mcp/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md).

## Tools

All ten tools are read only: they never write, delete or call anything but the atlas's own data file, so there is no read-only mode to switch on. Each declares an output schema and returns its answer both as `structuredContent` and as JSON text.

| Tool | What it answers |
| --- | --- |
| `search` | Records by name, Spanish ("Pablo") or a Bible book in Spanish or English ("Acts"); `did_you_mean` on a miss |
| `get_record` | One record in full, with its sources |
| `get_records` | Up to 20 records in one call |
| `list_records` | Periods, letters, journeys, finds, tours, books, months; places of a kind; holders of an office |
| `list_events` | Events by year, person, place, role, kind or Bible book |
| `people_in_year` | Who was alive or active in a year, with the evidence |
| `lookup_passage` | What the atlas has on a reference ("Hch 16:1" or "Acts 16:1") |
| `find_connection` | The shortest chain of ties between two people |
| `places_near` | Places within a radius of a place or a point |
| `dataset_info` | Freshness, counts, and the values the `kind` and `role` filters accept |

## Protocol

The server speaks MCP 2026-07-28 and every earlier revision down to 2024-11-05, on stdio and on streamable HTTP. Clients that still start with `initialize` (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code today) work as before; clients on 2026-07-28 get `server/discover`, stateless requests and cacheable tool lists from the same binary.

## Documentation

- [Getting started](https://github.com/GeiserX/biblical-atlas-mcp/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md): every install path and a first call
- [Configuration](https://github.com/GeiserX/biblical-atlas-mcp/blob/main/docs/configuration.md): every variable, flag and client config
- [Usage](https://github.com/GeiserX/biblical-atlas-mcp/blob/main/docs/usage.md): the ten tools, their parameters and what they return
- [How it works](https://github.com/GeiserX/biblical-atlas-mcp/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md): download, cache, refresh and offline use
- [Development](https://github.com/GeiserX/biblical-atlas-mcp/blob/main/docs/development.md): build, test and release

## Related projects

The data belongs to [biblical-atlas](https://github.com/GeiserX/biblical-atlas), the atlas this server reads. It stays on the atlas site with its sources; this server only fetches and indexes it. Other MCP servers in the family: [telegram-archive-mcp](https://github.com/GeiserX/telegram-archive-mcp).

## License

# AIR Bandenservice MCP server

A remote [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for **[AIR Bandenservice](https://www.airbandenservice.com/nl)**, a tyre shop and workshop in Haarlem, the Netherlands. It lets an AI assistant look up tyres by size, price an order line by line, book fitting at the workshop and place the order for a customer. The customer always pays on a Mollie payment page, so nothing is ordered until they pay.

- **Endpoint:** `https://www.airbandenservice.com/mcp`
- **Transport:** Streamable HTTP (stateless, JSON responses)
- **Authentication:** none
- **Protocol versions:** 2026-07-28, 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26

## Connect

**Claude** (claude.ai, Desktop, mobile): Settings → Connectors → *Add custom connector* → name `AIR Bandenservice`, URL `https://www.airbandenservice.com/mcp`.

**ChatGPT**: Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings → turn on *Developer mode* → *Create* → URL `https://www.airbandenservice.com/mcp`, authentication *No authentication*.

**Claude Code**

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http air-bandenservice https://www.airbandenservice.com/mcp
```

**Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf and other clients** (`mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "air-bandenservice": { "type": "http", "url": "https://www.airbandenservice.com/mcp" }
  }
}
```

## Agent skill

[`skills/air-bandenservice-tyres/SKILL.md`](skills/air-bandenservice-tyres/SKILL.md) tells an agent when to use this server and how to order. Drop it into your agent's skills folder (e.g. `~/.claude/skills/`).

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Side effects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `search_tyres` | Tyres by size (e.g. `205/55R16`), season and brand, with the all-in price per tyre and availability | none |
| `get_shop_info` | Address, opening hours, phone, delivery fee, fitting price, payment methods, terms and privacy links | none |
| `list_fitting_days` | Workshop days with room for fitting in the next 4 weeks | none |
| `get_quote` | The exact total for an order, line by line: tyres, fitting, sensor surcharges, disposal fee, delivery | none |
| `place_order` | Creates the order and returns a Mollie `checkoutUrl` for the customer | creates an unpaid order |
| `get_order_status` | Payment and order status by order reference (no personal data) | none |

## How ordering works

1. `search_tyres` for the size on the tyre sidewall.
2. Optionally `list_fitting_days` to have the tyres fitted and balanced at the workshop.
3. `get_quote` returns every line and the total. Prices are in euros and include 21% VAT and, where it applies, the €1.70 tyre disposal fee.
4. The assistant shows the customer the lines, the total and the [terms](https://www.airbandenservice.com/nl/algemene-voorwaarden). Only after the customer approves and accepts the terms themselves does the assistant call `place_order`, passing the quoted `expectedTotalCents`.
5. The customer opens the returned `checkoutUrl` and pays with iDEAL, card or another Mollie method. The order is placed only after payment. The customer then gets a confirmation and a receipt by email, and the shop is notified.

An unpaid order expires after about 15 minutes and its tyres go back on sale.

### Limits

- Online payment only: there is no pay-on-pickup through an assistant.
- At most 4 products and 8 tyres per order.
- An order is refused if the price changed since the quote. The assistant quotes again and asks the customer again.
- A limited number of unpaid assistant orders can be open at once, per customer and shop-wide.
- Delivery addresses in the Netherlands only. Discount codes work only on the website.

## Example prompts

- "I need four summer tyres 205/55R16 from AIR Bandenservice in Haarlem. What are my options?"
- "What does it cost to have two 195/65R15 tyres fitted at AIR Bandenservice next week?"
- "Order the cheapest 225/45R17 all-season tyres for pickup on Saturday morning, with fitting."
- "Is my AIR Bandenservice order AIR-2026-… paid yet?"

## Privacy and terms

The server stores only what an order needs: the customer's name, email and, where given, phone, address, licence plate and company details. Search and quote calls store nothing personal. See the [privacy policy](https://www.airbandenservice.com/nl/privacybeleid) and the [terms and conditions](https://www.airbandenservice.com/nl/algemene-voorwaarden). Dutch is the binding language of both.

## Support

AIR Bandenservice, Jan Tademaweg 16, 2031 CV Haarlem, the Netherlands. Email [info@airbandenservice.com](mailto:info@airbandenservice.com), phone +31 23 785 37 31.

This repository holds documentation only; the server runs on the shop's website.

readme.markdown:
# YouTube Transcript MCP Server

> Give Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Claude Code and any MCP client the ability to read **YouTube transcripts**. Hosted, nothing to install. Free API key: 10 requests a day.

A hosted [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that exposes one tool, `get_youtube_transcript`, backed by [youtube-transcript.ai](https://youtube-transcript.ai). Paste a YouTube link mid-conversation and your AI reads the full transcript on demand.

**Connector URL:**

```
https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp?key=YOUR_KEY
```

Replace `YOUR_KEY` with your API key. [Create a free key](https://youtube-transcript.ai/get-api-key) with a Google sign-in; it takes about a minute.

---

## Why

- **Free to start.** A free key covers 10 transcripts a day. Pro is 1,000 a day for $120 a year, on the same key.
- **Reliable.** A hardened fetch pipeline with proxy fallback returns transcripts even on videos that block typical scrapers.
- **Any language.** Pick a caption track by language code (`en`, `zh-CN`, `es`, `ja`, …) or let it choose the default.
- **Built for agents.** One tool, plain-text output with title and metadata. Multi-hour videos come back in parts, so nothing gets cut off.

## Authentication

Tool calls need an API key. There is no OAuth. Send the key in one of two ways:

| Where | Example |
|-------|---------|
| Header | `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY` |
| URL | `https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp?key=YOUR_KEY` |

The URL form is for clients that only accept a connector URL.

## Quick start

### Claude (web / desktop)

Settings → **Connectors** → **Add custom connector**

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Name  | `youtube-transcript.ai` |
| URL   | `https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp?key=YOUR_KEY` |

Then ask: *“Summarize this video: https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ”*

### ChatGPT

In the custom connector / MCP server setup, add an MCP server with URL `https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp?key=YOUR_KEY` (transport: **Streamable HTTP**), enable it for your chat, then paste a YouTube link.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user youtube-transcript \
  https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY"
```

### Cursor

Add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, or to `.cursor/mcp.json` inside one project:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "youtube-transcript": {
      "url": "https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Codex

Add to `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.youtube-transcript]
url = "https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp"
http_headers = { "Authorization" = "Bearer YOUR_KEY" }
```

### Clients that only launch local servers

For clients that start MCP servers from a config file and cannot take a remote URL, bridge with [`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "youtube-transcript": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp?key=YOUR_KEY"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Let your agent do it

Paste [`https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp.md`](https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp.md) into a coding agent. It is a plain-text version of these instructions, written for an AI to follow.

## Tool reference

### `get_youtube_transcript`

Fetch the full text transcript of a YouTube video.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `video`   | string | yes | YouTube URL (watch, `youtu.be`, shorts, embed) or a bare 11-character video ID |
| `lang`    | string | no  | Caption language code, e.g. `en`, `zh-CN`, `es`. Omit for the default track |
| `offset`  | integer | no | Where to continue a long transcript. Use the value given at the end of the previous part |

Returns plain text: the transcript with title, duration, and a list of available languages. Transcripts over 120,000 characters come back in parts; each part ends with a note giving the `offset` for the next call.

## Example prompts

- “Summarize the key points of `<link>` in 5 bullets.”
- “Pull the transcript of this video and translate it to Spanish.”
- “What does the speaker say about pricing in `<link>`? Quote the exact lines.”

## Programmatic use

The server speaks standard MCP over Streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC). A zero-dependency example is in [`examples/quickstart.mjs`](examples/quickstart.mjs):

```bash
YT_TRANSCRIPT_KEY=YOUR_KEY node examples/quickstart.mjs https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ
```

Calling from your own code without MCP? There is a plain HTTP endpoint too: see the [YouTube Transcript API](https://youtube-transcript.ai/api).

## Limits

- Free: 10 requests a day. Pro: 1,000 a day for $120 a year. Upgrade from the [key page](https://youtube-transcript.ai/get-api-key).
- Every tool call counts as one request, including each part of a long transcript. The count resets at 00:00 UTC.
- The video needs captions, either written by the uploader or auto-generated by YouTube.

## Notes

- **Not affiliated** with YouTube or Google. Transcripts are fetched from publicly available captions.
- Listed in the official MCP Registry as `ai.youtube-transcript/youtube-transcript`.

## Links

- Web tool (no AI client needed): https://youtube-transcript.ai
- Connector landing page: https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp
- HTTP API: https://youtube-transcript.ai/api

# PR-MCP-IMT + SKILLS — Premiere Pro for AI agents

Let an AI assistant (Claude Desktop, Cursor, ChatGPT, Google Antigravity or any MCP client) work
inside your running **Adobe Premiere Pro**: read the project and its sequences, cut, trim, move and
ripple clips, apply effects, transitions and keyframes, add markers and captions, reframe, check
frames and export — from plain language.

Two parts, made to work together:

- **The MCP server** — about 380 Premiere operations behind nine tools; writes are verified by
  reading Premiere back; **works on every Premiere UI language** (verified live); no telemetry.
- **The skill** (`skills/pr`, also served by the `pr_skill` tool, so it works in any client) — how
  to drive Premiere safely, where scripting ends, and how to use **Premiere's own AI tools**:
  Generative Extend, the Generative Media Tool (video, sound effects, music), Object Mask, Speech to
  Text and Paper Edit, captions, Enhance Speech and stem separation, Search, the AI Assistant, Auto
  Reframe, Scene Edit Detection, Morph Cut — plus recipes that combine them and the gotchas.

**Built for localized Premiere, not just English.** Most Premiere MCP servers and agent skills assume
the English UI — on a German, Chinese or Russian install their effect, transition and parameter names
stop matching. PR-MCP-IMT finds components by matchName and translates English effect, transition and
parameter names through Premiere's own UI dictionaries, so the same agent and the same skill work on
all ten UI languages Premiere ships — verified live.

By **[Immersive Media Technologies](https://github.com/Immersive-Media-Technologies)**.

**macOS and Windows · Premiere Pro 2024–2026 — verified live on macOS (26.5) and on Windows 11 ARM
(26.5.2, Claude Desktop from the Microsoft Store) · Node.js 20.19+ (none
needed with the Claude Desktop extension).**

> [!CAUTION]
> This edits real Premiere projects, and Premiere has **no scripted undo** — work on a copy. Project
> content (names, transcripts, markers, frames) goes to the AI service you use. Premiere's
> generative tools spend your Adobe credits; the agent asks before starting one. Raw ExtendScript is
> off unless you turn it on.

## What you can ask for

- "List every clip shorter than 12 frames and every gap in the active sequence."
- "Tighten the pauses in this interview to a third of a second and put a Morph Cut on the jump
  cuts where the camera is locked off." _(skill)_
- "Make 9:16 and 1:1 versions of this edit and check the titles stay out of the TikTok UI zones."
- "Blur the face of the man on the left for the whole shot." _(skill: you click the subject with
  Object Mask, the agent does the rest)_
- "The music in this interview was recorded on location — get rid of it and score it again under
  the dialogue." _(skill)_
- "Mark every beat of this track and lay the selects to it, two beats per shot."

The agent combines the operations itself and checks the sequence between steps; the skill tells it
which Premiere AI tool fits the job, what it costs and where it breaks.

## Install

You need Premiere Pro running on this computer and the **connector** — a small CEP extension
inside Premiere that the server talks to. The agent installs it for you on first use
(`pr_install_connector`, it asks first; then quit and reopen Premiere), or the installer below does.

| Client | How |
|---|---|
|  **Claude Desktop** | download [`premiere-mcp-imt.mcpb`](https://github.com/Immersive-Media-Technologies/premiere-mcp-imt/releases/latest/download/premiere-mcp-imt.mcpb), double-click, **Install** (Windows: drag it onto Settings → Extensions). No Node needed. |
|  **Cursor** |  |
|  **Google Antigravity** | Settings → Customizations → Installed MCP Servers → **View raw config** → add the snippet below. |
|  **ChatGPT** (remote servers only) | on the Premiere machine: `npx -p @immersive-media-technologies/premiere-mcp-imt premiere-mcp-imt-chatgpt` — it starts the server behind a tunnel and prints the URL to paste into ChatGPT. |
| **Any MCP client** | the snippet below in its `mcpServers`. |

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "premiere": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@immersive-media-technologies/premiere-mcp-imt"]
    }
  }
}
```

**From source, with a live self-test** (the route we use):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Immersive-Media-Technologies/premiere-mcp-imt.git
cd premiere-mcp-imt && ./install.sh        # Windows: .\install.ps1
```

The installer checks Premiere, Node and FFmpeg, builds, installs the connector (asks first), asks the
running Premiere whether the connector answers, and — after asking — writes the entry into Claude
Desktop's, Cursor's and Antigravity's configs, backing them up.

<details>
<summary>If something does not connect</summary>

- `pr_verify` says the connector does not answer: quit Premiere **completely** after the connector
  was installed and open it again; close any open Premiere dialog (a modal dialog blocks scripting).
  `premiere-mcp-imt --diagnose-cep` checks the files, the debug flags and Premiere's signature log.
- The connector is unsigned: CEP must allow unsigned extensions (`PlayerDebugMode` = `1` for CSXS
  9–14; on Windows a String (`REG_SZ`) value under `HKCU\Software\Adobe\CSXS.<n>`). The installers set it.
- `spawn npx ENOENT` on macOS: GUI apps do not see your shell `PATH` — put the absolute path of a
  Node from Homebrew or nodejs.org in place of `npx` (nvm's Node is invisible to them).
- Loudness, silence (`detect_silence`), beat and scene-change analysis need FFmpeg
  (`brew install ffmpeg`, `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg`).
- Windows, Claude Desktop from the Microsoft Store: the Store app's registry writes are sandboxed. If
  Premiere does not load the connector after `pr_install_connector`, run
  `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install-cep.ps1` once from a normal PowerShell in a
  source checkout (or use `install.ps1`).
- `premiere-mcp-imt --doctor` checks the local insta

name: EventSend

readme.markdown:
# EventSend for Claude

[EventSend](https://eventsend.io) routes your product's events, like payments, signups, deploys and
errors, to Slack, Discord, Telegram, webhooks and push notifications. This plugin lets Claude answer
questions about those events in plain language: what happened, to whom, and whether the
notifications got through.

It connects Claude to EventSend's read-only MCP server and adds four skills that teach Claude how to
investigate with it. Nothing it does can change your EventSend account.

## What you can ask

- "Did anything fail in checkout today?"
- "Why didn't the payment alert reach #billing this morning?"
- "What did customer `cus_9Xk2` do before they cancelled?"
- "Give me a summary of last week compared with the week before."
- "Where do `deploy.failed` events go?"
- "Are we going to run out of events before the month ends?"

## Skills

| Skill | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `investigate-failures` | Finds out why a notification failed or never arrived: delivery health per destination, the event's status, the exact errors, and what to fix in EventSend. |
| `customer-timeline` | Rebuilds one customer's history from every event that carries their `user_id`, oldest first, with the moments that matter called out. |
| `activity-report` | Summarizes a day, a week or a month: volume against the previous period, top events, errors, delivery problems and quota. |
| `routing-map` | Explains your routes, sources, topics and destinations, and traces where a given event is delivered and why. |

Claude picks the right skill from your question. In Claude Code you can also run one directly, for
example `/eventsend:activity-report`.

## Install

You need an EventSend account. Every plan works, including Free.

**claude.ai and Cowork**: add EventSend from the plugin directory in **Customize → Plugins**. Then
open the plugin's **Connectors** tab, connect EventSend, sign in, and choose which of your
organizations Claude may read.

**Claude Code**:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add mytinyrocket/eventsend-claude-plugin
claude plugin install eventsend@eventsend
```

Then run `/mcp`, select `eventsend` and sign in. Your browser opens EventSend, where you choose the
organizations to connect.

**Gemini CLI**: this repository is also a Gemini CLI extension.

```bash
gemini extensions install https://github.com/mytinyrocket/eventsend-claude-plugin
```

Then run `/mcp auth eventsend` and sign in.

**Cursor, ChatGPT and other clients**: the same server works in any client that supports remote MCP
servers. See the [client setup guide](https://eventsend.io/docs/mcp) for each one.

## Data and privacy

The plugin runs no code of its own and stores nothing. It contains instructions for Claude and one
connector reference, to `https://eventsend.io/mcp`.

When Claude uses an EventSend tool, the tool's arguments go to EventSend: search text, event names,
customer identifiers, organization names and dates. What comes back is your organization's data,
which then becomes part of your conversation with Claude. That covers events and their payloads,
delivery records and errors, daily counts, quota, and the names and ids of your routes, sources,
topics and destinations. No tool returns ingest tokens, signing secrets, MCP keys or destination
settings, and no tool can create, change or delete anything.

Sign-in uses OAuth. A connection sees exactly what you can see in the organizations you approved. To
revoke it, disconnect under **Connected apps** in your EventSend settings, or ask an organization
owner or admin to remove it under **Settings → MCP**. Revocation takes effect on the next request.

- [Privacy policy](https://eventsend.io/privacy)
- [Terms of service](https://eventsend.io/terms)
- [MCP server documentation](https://eventsend.io/docs/mcp)

## Support

Open an issue in this repository, or email [support@eventsend.io](mailto:support@eventsend.io).

## License

# Multiplayer Agent for Claude Code

Make any browser game multiplayer from Claude Code, and host it at a share link a friend can open. This plugin connects Claude Code to the hosted Multiplayer Agent backend, which provides rooms, shared real-time state, player identity, saved progress, leaderboards and game hosting, so Claude never has to write or run a game server. It also adds a `make-it-multiplayer` skill that teaches Claude how to design, wire, test and publish a multiplayer game on it.

No account or key is needed to start. Claude asks for your email and opens a page where you sign up or log in (your password is typed on the website, never in the chat), so your games are saved to your own account.

## Install

Type these in Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add multiplayeragent/multiplayer-agent
/plugin install multiplayer-agent@multiplayer-agent
```

If the tools don't show up straight away, type `/reload-plugins`. Then ask Claude something like "build me a multiplayer snake game" or "make this game multiplayer".

## What it includes

- **MCP server** `multiplayer-agent` at `https://api.multiplayeragent.com/mcp` (remote, streamable HTTP, no key required).
- **Skill** `make-it-multiplayer`, used automatically when you ask for multiplayer, co-op, a lobby, an invite link, a leaderboard or hosting.

## Data and privacy

The plugin sends requests to `api.multiplayeragent.com`: the game definitions, room settings and game files Claude creates or publishes for you, plus the email you choose to connect. Games you publish are served from `*.play.multiplayeragent.com`, and players' game state goes to the same backend while they play. See the [privacy policy](https://multiplayeragent.com/privacy) and [terms](https://multiplayeragent.com/terms).

## Links

- How the connection works: https://multiplayeragent.com/mcp
- SDK reference: https://multiplayeragent.com/docs
- Pricing (free tier, no card): https://multiplayeragent.com/pricing

readme.markdown:
# drizzle-mcp

Drizzle Studio for agents. An [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that lets Claude Code, Cursor and other coding agents see your database through your Drizzle schema.

A generic database MCP sees tables and columns. This one reads the schema your code uses: TypeScript names next to SQL names, relations, enums and defaults. An agent can then answer "what's actually in the database?" and write Drizzle code that matches it.

Here is what an agent gets back when it asks about a `posts` table:

```text
## posts

SQL table `posts`, exported as `posts` from `src/db/schema.ts`.

| column (TS key, SQL name) | type                     | nullable | default | notes                          |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------ |
| id                        | serial                   | no       |         | primary key                    |
| authorId (author_id)      | integer                  | no       |         | → users.id, on delete cascade  |
| published                 | boolean                  | no       | false   |                                |
| createdAt (created_at)    | timestamp with time zone | no       | now()   |                                |

Relations (for `browse` with `with`, or `db.query` in code):
- author: one users on posts.authorId = users.id
- comments: many comments on posts.id = comments.postId
```

## Set up

Run it from the folder with `drizzle.config.ts`.

**Claude Code**

```sh
claude mcp add drizzle -- npx -y drizzle-mcp
```

**Cursor** (`.cursor/mcp.json`) and **VS Code** (`.vscode/mcp.json`, with `"servers"` instead of `"mcpServers"`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "drizzle": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "drizzle-mcp"] }
  }
}
```

For clients that don't start servers in your project folder, such as Claude Desktop, add `"--config", "/path/to/drizzle.config.ts"` to `args`.

drizzle-mcp loads your config the way drizzle-kit does, including your `.env`. It connects with the database driver and the drizzle-orm version your project already has installed.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `schema` | Lists the tables. With a table name, it describes the columns (TypeScript key and SQL name, type, nullability, default), the keys, indexes, checks and relations. |
| `browse` | Reads rows the way Drizzle Studio shows them: pick columns, filter, sort and page, and include related rows through your `relations()`. Rows are keyed by TypeScript property, as `db.query` returns them. |
| `count` | Counts rows, overall or per value with `groupBy`, to see how data is distributed. |
| `query` | Runs one SQL statement read-only and returns up to 100 rows. |
| `explain` | Shows the query plan, to check that an index is used. On Postgres, `analyze` runs the query for real timings. |
| `drift` | Compares the schema with the live database: missing or extra tables and columns, and changed types or nullability. |
| `migrations` | Lists drizzle-kit's migrations as applied or pending. It also flags any migration edited after it was applied. |
| `execute` | Changes data. Only available when the server is started with `--allow-writes`. |

Filters are JSON, so values are always bound as parameters, never pasted into SQL:

```json
{ "published": true, "createdAt": { "gte": "2026-01-01" }, "or": [{ "title": { "ilike": "%drizzle%" } }, { "rating": { "gte": 4.5 } }] }
```

If you edit the schema, the server picks up the change on the next call; no restart needed.

## Safe by default

An agent shouldn't be able to wreck a database by accident, or because something it read told it to.

- **Read-only.** Every statement runs in a read-only transaction. SQLite reads use a read-only connection.
- **One statement at a time.** `select 1; commit; drop table users` is refused before it reaches the database. The Postgres drivers and `better-sqlite3` would refuse it again on their own; libsql would silently drop everything after the first statement.
- **Bounded.** Statements time out after 15 seconds. Results are capped at 100 rows and fetched through a cursor, so a large table is never pulled into memory. Long values are cut short.
- **Secrets hidden.** Values in columns named like `password`, `token`, `secret` or `apiKey` are shown as `[redacted]`.
- **Writes are opt-in.** `--allow-writes` adds the `execute` tool. `query` stays read-only either way.

## Requirements

| Database | Drivers |
| --- | --- |
| PostgreSQL | `pg`, `postgres` (postgres.js), PGlite |
| SQLite | `better-sqlite3`, `@libsql/client` (including Turso) |

MySQL isn't supported yet.

drizzle-mcp needs Node.js 22 or newer. It's tested with drizzle-orm 0.45, the current stable release. Drizzle 1.0, still in beta, defines relations differently and isn't supported yet.

## Options

```text
--config <path>     The Drizzle config (default: drizzle.config.ts in the current folder)
--url <url>         Connect here instead of the config's dbCredentials
--driver <name>     pg, postgres, pglite, better-sqlite3 or libsql (default: the one installed)
--allow-writes      Add the execute tool
--max-rows <n>      The most rows a tool returns (default: 100)
--timeout <ms>      Statement time limit (default: 15000)
--max-text <n>      Cut strings longer than this (default: 500)
--redact <regex>    Hide columns whose names match (default: password, secret, token…)
--show-secrets      Don't hide any columns
```

## How it works

1. It loads `drizzle.config.ts` and your `.env`, then imports the schema files the config points to (a file, a folder or a glob). Imports go through [jiti](https://github.com/unjs/jiti), so TypeScript works without a build step.
2. It reads tables, columns and relations from drizzle-orm's own metadata. This is the same information `drizzle-kit` and relational queries use. That's where the TypeScript names and relations come from.
3. It connects with your project's driver. `browse` and `count` build relational q
