# parseapi-mcp

Official ParseAPI MCP server. Look up places, addresses, company numbers, email, phone, weather, timezones, dates and more from your AI agent.

## Hosted

One URL, nothing to install. Add the server and sign in once in the browser. Free plan works.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "parseAPI": { "url": "https://mcp.parseapi.com" }
  }
}
```

**Cursor:** [Add to Cursor](cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=parseAPI&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL21jcC5wYXJzZWFwaS5jb20ifQ==)

Repo-root `.mcp.json` is keyless on purpose. [cursor.directory](https://cursor.directory/plugins/parseapi) auto-detects it when you submit or refresh the listing.

CI and headless setups skip the browser with a key from [parseapi.com](https://parseapi.com):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "parseAPI": {
      "url": "https://mcp.parseapi.com",
      "headers": { "X-API-Key": "your-api-key" }
    }
  }
}
```

## Local

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "parseAPI": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "parseapi-mcp"],
      "env": { "PARSEAPI_KEY": "your-api-key" }
    }
  }
}
```

## API versions

Since version 1.0.0, the package explicitly selects the API contract supported by this MCP package. Every API tool request sends `Parse-Version: 2.0.0`, matching this release's tool descriptions and SDK response types. The contract is fixed for both local stdio and hosted HTTP, including retries. Your key, OAuth identity and team's saved default stay the same.

For local stdio, pin the MCP package version in your application configuration and test the new release before deploying it. A future major MCP upgrade can select a newer API contract. There is no version argument to add to individual tool calls. The hosted service uses the API contract supported by its deployed MCP release.

MCP packages older than 1.0.0 keep their existing behavior and use the team's default. Keep that default unchanged while older applications depend on it. Rolling back to a package without a version header restores the team default, so rollback only restores the old contract when that default has stayed unchanged. See [API versions and migration](https://parseapi.com/docs/versioning).

## Tools

Full mode provides 68 local lookup tools and 67 hosted lookup tools, plus `discover` for local metadata and `preflight` for authenticated task estimates. `ip_self` is local only. `time` returns current local time and Unix seconds. It accepts a timezone or coordinates and defaults to UTC when both are omitted. `date` parses the supplied date, or returns today in UTC when omitted. Existing `timezone` calls remain supported with their original arguments. Every lookup returns the JSON the API serves.

Tools follow the lookup names: `country_states`, `city_search`, `postal_nearby`, `address`, `address_search`, `company`, `company_id`, `company_search`, `company_coverage`, `email`, `bank_us_ach`, `card`, `industry`, `industry_search`, `dns`, `asn`, `mac`, `currency_rate`, and the rest. Text searches take `query`. Company directory search supports one name/domain/ticker/identifier selector or country/exact-SIC discovery filters.

The existing `naics` and `naics_search` tools remain available as compatibility names for Industry.

Industry paid deep records include classification `deep.exclusions`, each with a description and linked codes. Generic exclusions can have no linked codes. Omitted or null exclusions in older responses remain unknown. Search results also include `match`: the matched `field` (`name`, `term` or `naics`) and `text`, plus `corrections` with `from` and `to` tokens for typo fallback. Corrections are empty for exact, plural and prefix matches. Direct code lookups omit `match`. Older responses may omit it.

Example tool arguments:

| Tool | Arguments |
|---|---|
| `stack` | `{"domain":"example.com"}` (website technologies and versions by category) |
| `domain` | `{"domain":"example.com"}` (registration status) |
| `domain` | `{"domain":"example.com","deep":true}` (registration details on paid plans) |
| `dns` | `{"domain":"example.com","type":"TXT"}` |
| `mx` | `{"domain":"example.com"}` |
| `asn` | `{"asn":"AS13335"}` |
| `card` | `{"bin":"424242"}` |
| `country_states` | `{"code":"US"}` |
| `address_search` | `{"query":"1600 Pennsylvania","country":"US","city":"Washington","state":"DC"}` |
| `company` | `{"number":"552100554","country":"FR"}` |
| `company_search` | `{"query":"Cloudflare","country":"US"}` |
| `company_id` | `{"id":"co_xw3f22es6cjq","deep":true}` |
| `company_coverage` | `{}` |
| `time` | `{}` (UTC now) |
| `time` | `{"timezone":"America/New_York","at":"2026-09-05T09:00:00","to":"Asia/Tokyo"}` |
| `time` | `{"lat":40.71,"lon":-74.01}` |
| `time` | `{"timezone":"UTC","targets":["America/New_York","Asia/Tokyo"]}` |
| `time_zones` | `{"query":"New York"}` |
| `time` | `{"timezone":"America/New_York","at":"2026-11-01T01:30:00","to":"UTC","disambiguation":"later"}` |
| `date` | `{"date":"03/04/2026","format":"dmy"}` |
| `elevation` | `{"lat":35.2271,"lon":-80.8431}` |
| `elevation` | `{"points":"35.2271,-80.8431|40.7128,-74.006"}` |
| `elevation` | `{"path":"35.2271,-80.8431|35.5951,-82.5515","samples":100}` |

Time uses `disambiguation` only for offsetless `at` with `to` or `targets`. The default `compatible` selects the earlier repeated time or advances a skipped time. `earlier` and `later` choose the respective instant. `reject` returns `ambiguous_time` for repeated times and `nonexistent_time` for skipped times. Prefer it for user-entered appointments. Ask for an explicit offset or the user's choice before retrying a rejected local time. Explicit offsets select an instant directly. Time deep is available in the same pooled request on every plan.

# HarflowMCP

HarflowMCP is a local MCP server that dispatches coding tasks to Claude Code, Codex, opencode, Vibe, and Antigravity. It provides persistent task history, bounded reads, cancellation, continuation, and reusable workflows. On measured Claude Code versions, callers can opt in to approving individual Bash, Read, Write and Edit requests one exact action at a time (see [harness permissions](docs/harness-permissions.md#exact-action-caller-approvals)); on macOS with codex-cli 0.163.0 the same opt-in approves individual Codex commands and, with `caller_write_approvals`, patches through `codex app-server` (see [Codex caller approvals](docs/harness-permissions.md#codex-caller-approvals-codex-app-server)), and can grant a task a bounded list of specific Bash commands with `allowed_commands` instead of `unrestricted` access (see [dispatch-time command grants](docs/harness-permissions.md#dispatch-time-command-grants-allowed_commands)).

Workflow callers can see every pending child question in status and wait replies and answer them independently by decision ID through the root run. Questions and structured clarification items remain complete, and forwarded answers return a durable child acceptance receipt. Resolved attention reasons disappear when execution resumes; unreadable workflow approval metadata is reported separately from requests needing a decision. See [workflow input and recovery](docs/workflows.md).

Permission features use cached, binary-bound qualification: measured versions seed the cache, and unseen versions run isolated no-paid behavior probes before use. `harflow-ctl qualify <backend>` explicitly reruns the probes; discovery and permission previews report their per-feature results. Automatic probes currently require macOS isolation. See [qualification](docs/harness-permissions.md).

Current seed measurements for these two features: `allowed_commands` is qualified on Claude Code 2.1.310 and 2.1.312; caller approvals are qualified on Claude Code 2.1.302 (Bash approvals) and 2.1.310/2.1.312, and on Codex through `codex app-server` for codex-cli 0.163.0 on macOS only (commands, and patches with `caller_write_approvals`); other backends refuse them. Approvals are not available to native workflow children, and a request unanswered after 1800 seconds (or at the node's attempt deadline) is rejected by Harflow, never approved. After a denial there is no approve-later path: recovery is always a new `resume_task` or `continue_task` execution guided by `denial_remedy` (`allowed_commands` covers only Bash `approval_required` and chained-command parts; a denied Read, Write or Edit needs a resumed run so the agent can raise a fresh request; a `deny_rule` cannot be lifted by grants). Workflow permission-grant retry and approval notifications are not available. On compatible engines the Mac Monitor can answer caller-owned requests; authority follows the existing inferred, cooperative same-user model and does not authenticate a human or the app. See [harness permissions](docs/harness-permissions.md#exact-action-caller-approvals).

Vibe 3.0.1 headless dispatch uses its Rust CLI and the `ask` approval profile for `read_only`. This is an approval policy, not a write-tool exclusion: inherited policies or custom profiles can pre-approve writes. The retained `VIBE_CLI=python` selector is ignored by Vibe 3; interactive takeover inherits the user's environment.

Version 0.0.4 is a pre-release. [Harflow](https://github.com/Harflow-Dev/HarflowMac), the companion macOS application, is maintained separately and prepares its own exact paired engine runtime. Its managed runtime and MCP registrations work independently of the app process; see the [managed runtime guide](https://github.com/Harflow-Dev/HarflowMac/blob/main/docs/managed-runtime.md).

Detached task owners preserve output capture and live input across MCP server restarts.
Tasks can take turns on a named, exclusive resource (a simulator, a device, a database) with `resources`; a waiting task is acknowledged at once and reports `waiting_for_resources` until it spawns. A task can also run in its own linked Git worktree with `worktree`, leaving your checkout untouched. Workflows can declare run and node resource scopes and share one root-run worktree across nodes and linked child runs. See [resources and worktrees](docs/resources-and-worktrees.md). Final review summaries and workflow plans receive task-identifiable files discoverable through task artifacts, including read-only runs. Child workflows receive pinned parent specifications throughout their nodes. Every task also gets scratch folders shared across its resume chain and its group (`HARFLOW_CHAIN_SCRATCH`, `HARFLOW_GROUP_SCRATCH`), so outputs survive between runs; see [shared scratch](docs/shared-scratch.md).

Workflow scheduler recovery is explicit; see [supervision and recovery](docs/supervision.md).
Task status distinguishes the dispatching server, execution owner and responding server.
A normal attachment to a task launched by this server is not recovered; another observer or missing
identity is explained explicitly. Detail reads separately report dispatcher liveness, and routine
status polling provides a successor reference without scanning history. See [supervision and recovery](docs/supervision.md).
Git outcomes retain partial observations with per-probe failure and budget diagnostics. Commit
ranges include imported history and cannot identify task-created commits or authorship; see
[observed task outcomes](docs/task-outcomes.md).
Task observations retry transient metadata replacements up to three reads and retain uncertainty
when metadata cannot be read reliably.
Recovered tasks disclose owner/process uncertainty and capture continuity. Qualified Claude
transcripts can supply bounded display-only recovery activity; see [public contracts](docs/contracts.md#supervision-and-recovery-activity).

readme.markdown:
# desktop-touch-mcp

[日本語](README.ja.md)

> **Computer-use MCP server for Windows.** Lets Claude, Cursor, or any MCP client see and operate your Windows 10/11 desktop — screenshots, UI Automation, Chrome CDP, keyboard / mouse, terminal — with **semantic discover-then-act targeting** that avoids pixel-coordinate guessing, and **per-action perception guards** that catch wrong-window typing before it happens.

```bash
npx -y @harusame64/desktop-touch-mcp
```

32 tools, native Rust engine (UIA in 2 ms), zero-config PowerShell fallback, full CJK support, MIT licensed. Add the snippet above to your Claude / Cursor / VS Code Copilot config and Claude can drive Notepad, Excel, Chrome, Windows Terminal, and any other app on your machine.

> **Why this over pixel-clicking?** Two ideas run through every tool: **discover-then-act** — `desktop_discover` returns interactive entities with short-lived leases instead of raw coordinates, so `desktop_act` operates on *what* you mean, not *where* it was — and **per-action perception guards** that verify the target window's identity and bounds before input lands, catching wrong-window typing and stale-coordinate clicks before they happen.
>
> **2.1** reads UI Automation by element count instead of depth: Chrome, Edge and VS Code pages, Explorer and Settings values, and Word's body are read and can be acted on, and what UIA still cannot see falls back to OCR and Set-of-Marks as before. `desktop_act` also types into Word's body, and into Windows Terminal after asking the user. **2.0** refuses an action that cannot be done, with a reason, instead of reporting it done, and an action aimed by `hwnd` reaches that window only. See the [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md).

---

## Features

- **🔁 Every act reports what it did** — `desktop_act` answers with what changed: elements that appeared or disappeared, a modal, a focus move, the screen's repaint (`observation`), and with `narrate:"rich"` the values and names that changed. The agent reads the result of its click from the reply instead of taking another screenshot. On UIA-blind targets it can also attach a PNG of just the region that changed (`roiCapture`; on by default for a visible change, `returnCapture:"never"` to suppress, `"always"` to force).
- **🛑 An act that cannot be done is refused, not reported as done** — input that would not reach the field, a window blocked by a dialog, a closed window, a window on another virtual desktop: nothing is sent, and the reply names the reason and what to do next. An act aimed by `hwnd` never lands in another window with the same title.
- **🌐 Reads deep windows (2.1)** — The UI Automation read goes to depth 64 and 500 elements. Chrome, Edge and VS Code pages, which 2.0 called blind, Explorer and Settings values it left out, and Word's body are read and can be acted on (a Chrome page: 6 elements in 387 ms → 45 in 186 ms).
- **🎯 Set-of-Marks (SoM) visual fallback** — Games, RDP sessions and apps with no accessibility tree still return clickable elements: when UIA is blind, `desktop_discover` and `screenshot(detail="text")` switch to a Hybrid Non-CDP pipeline — Rust-powered grayscale + bilinear upscale → Windows OCR → clustering → red bounding boxes with numbered badges (`[1]`, `[2]`…). Two representations come back: a PNG for spatial orientation and an `elements[]` list with `clickAt` coords — no CDP required.
- **⌨️ Types where background input does not reach** — Windows Terminal, after asking the user each time (needs an MCP client with elicitation, over stdio), and Word's body, at Word's caret whether it is in front or behind.
- **🔐 Key Locker — the terminal autofills your SSH / sudo passwords** — Save a credential once into the locker's own secure dialog (stored encrypted on your machine with Windows DPAPI; never shown to the assistant), then run `ssh` / `sudo` in a console opened by `key_locker(action='launch_console')` — the password is filled in automatically when the hidden prompt appears, with a per-fill confirmation prompt by default. See [Key Locker](docs/guide.md#key-locker-terminal-credential-autofill).
- **⚡ Rust native core** — The UIA bridge and image diffing are a Rust native addon (`napi-rs` + `windows-rs`): UIA is called over COM from a dedicated thread instead of spawning PowerShell, and image diffs use SSE2 SIMD. Without the addon, every function falls back to PowerShell transparently. The npm launcher fetches only the GitHub Release matching its version and verifies the Windows runtime zip before extracting it.
- **LLM-native design** — Built around how LLMs think, not how humans click. `run_macro` batches multiple operations into a single API call; `diffMode` sends only the windows that changed since the last frame. Minimal tokens, minimal round-trips.
- **Reactive Perception Graph** — Register a `lensId` for a window or browser tab, pass it to action tools, and get guard-checked `post.perception` feedback after each action. It reduces repeated `screenshot` / `desktop_state` calls and prevents wrong-window typing or stale-coordinate clicks.
- **Full CJK support** — Uses Win32 `GetWindowTextW` for window titles, avoiding nut-js garbling. IME bypass input supported for Japanese/Chinese/Korean environments.
- **3-tier token reduction** — `detail="image"` (~443 tok) / `detail="text"` (~100–300 tok) / `diffMode=true` (~160 tok). Send pixels only when you actually need to see them.
- **1:1 coordinate mode** — `dotByDot=true` captures at native resolution (WebP). Image pixel = screen coordinate — no scale math needed. With `origin`+`scale` passed to `mouse_click`, the server converts coords for you — eliminating off-by-one / scale bugs.
- **Browser capture data reduction** — `grayscale=true` (~50% size), `dotByDotMaxDimension=1280` (auto-scaled with coord preservation), and `windowTitle + region` sub-crops help exclude browser chrome and other irrelevant pixels. Typical reduction for heavy captures: 50–70%.
- **Chromium smart fallback** — `detail="text"` on Chro

readme.markdown:
# Server4Agent

Servers your AI assistant builds on. It writes the code, runs it and ships each app to a live URL.

Server4Agent is a remote MCP server. Connect it to your AI assistant and ask
for a web page, a site, an app, an API, a bot or a scheduled job. The assistant
gets a server to build on, writes and runs the code there, and publishes each
project at its own live URL. Processes keep running after the conversation
ends, so backends and bots stay up.

There is nothing to install or run on your machine. The server is hosted at
`https://mcp.server4agent.com`, and this repository holds its listing in the MCP
Registry.

## Connect

- **Endpoint:** `https://mcp.server4agent.com`
- **Transport:** streamable HTTP
- **Sign-in:** OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration, or an API key sent
  as a bearer token

You need a Server4Agent account: https://www.server4agent.com

### VS Code and GitHub Copilot

Install Server4Agent from the MCP server gallery in the Extensions view
(search for `@mcp Server4Agent`), or add it to `.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "server4agent": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.server4agent.com"
    }
  }
}
```

Start the server and VS Code opens a browser to sign in. There is no key to
copy, and you can revoke the sign-in from the dashboard. The tools are then
available to Copilot Chat in agent mode.

### GitHub Copilot CLI

Create an API key in the dashboard, export it as `SERVER4AGENT_API_KEY`, and
add the server to `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "server4agent": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.server4agent.com",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${SERVER4AGENT_API_KEY}" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Any other MCP host

Add `https://mcp.server4agent.com` as a remote MCP server. A host that
supports OAuth opens a browser to sign in and needs nothing else. For a host without OAuth, or for CI,
send an API key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, and keep the key in an
environment variable rather than in a config file you commit.

Setup for more apps: https://www.server4agent.com/integrations

## Use it

Ask in plain language. For example:

- "Make a landing page for my bakery and put it online."
- "Build an API that turns a CSV upload into JSON, and give me the URL."
- "Check our website every hour and keep a log of when it is down."
- "What is running on my servers, and how much have I spent this month?"

How it fits together:

- A **server** is a sized box (small, medium or large) that holds projects. One
  server holds several.
- A **project** is a folder plus an app, with its own URL at
  `<slug>.apps.server4agent.com`. Projects are private until `deploy` makes
  them public.
- Your assistant can write the files itself, or hand a goal to the agent that
  runs on the server (`start_build`, `prompt`), which spends the account's
  AI budget.
- Tools that delete or overwrite are marked destructive, so your host can ask
  you before it runs one.

## Tools

38 tools. `[read-only]` never writes; `[destructive]` may delete or
overwrite.

### Servers

A server is a sized compute box. Projects live inside it and share its resources.

- `create_server`: Provision a sized server box.
- `list_servers` `[read-only]`: List your servers with their tier, kind, status, project sharing, and current project count.
- `get_server` `[read-only]`: Get a server's tier, kind, status, capacity, project count, and project sharing.
- `update_server` `[destructive]`: Update a server's nickname, region, or how much its projects may see of each other.
- `control_server` `[destructive]`: Pause a server (stop), resume it (start), or reboot it (restart).
- `delete_server` `[destructive]`: Tear down a server and every project on it.
- `get_usage` `[read-only]`: Get the account's AI spend and budget: how much has been spent this billing period, the plan's included credits, any budget cap, and whether new tasks are blocked (with the reason).

### Projects

A project is a workspace plus an app inside a server, with its own slug and URL. New projects are private: the URL only serves once you make it public.

- `list_templates` `[read-only]`: List the available project starters.
- `create_project`: Create a project on a server: the home for one web page, site, app, API or bot, with its own URL at <slug>.apps.server4agent.com.
- `list_projects` `[read-only]`: List projects.
- `get_project` `[read-only]`: Get a single project: name, slug, description, public URL, listen port, run plan, timestamps.
- `update_project` `[destructive]`: Rename a project, update its description, change visibility, link access or lifecycle, or correct its run plan.
- `init_project`: Start or resume bring-up for a project seeded from a git/archive source: the on-server agent installs dependencies, starts the app, and confirms it responds.
- `export_project`: Package a project into a portable bundle and return a time-limited download link.
- `import_project`: Recreate a project on a server from a bundle that export_project produced, here or on another Server4Agent deployment.
- `cleanup_project` `[destructive]`: Clean up an ephemeral project once its task is done.
- `delete_project` `[destructive]`: Delete a project.

### Secrets

Env vars for servers and projects. Values are write-only: no tool ever reads one back.

- `set_secret` `[destructive]`: Create or update a secret (an env var, key → value) on the account.
- `list_secrets` `[read-only]`: List the account's secrets: keys, notes, and where each is bound (servers/projects).
- `attach_secret` `[destructive]`: Bind a secret to a scope so runs there see it as an env var.
- `delete_secret` `[destructive]`: Delete a secret and all of its bindings.

### Agent runtime

Start and keep your app running, delegate work to the agent running on the server, or drive the shell yourself.

- `start_app` `[destructive]`: Start a project's app and keep it running: the step that puts a project online aft

readme.markdown:
# @txscribe/mcp

An [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for the txscribe developer API. It lets an AI
assistant transcribe a link with your txscribe account and read the transcript and the summary
back, through the same API documented at <https://txscribe.ai/developers>.

There are two ways to connect, with the same eight tools:

- **Hosted** — `https://txscribe.ai/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). Claude and ChatGPT connect to it as
  a custom connector and sign you in to txscribe with OAuth; nothing to install. Clients that
  take a header can send an API key instead.
- **Local** — this package, run as a command (`npx -y @txscribe/mcp`) by Claude Desktop, Claude
  Code, Cursor and other clients that start MCP servers themselves, with your API key in its
  environment.

Both are thin wrappers: every tool is one call to the developer API as you. What a tool may do,
and the minutes it uses, is exactly what your account may do in the app. Nothing is cached or
stored on your machine.

## Hosted: Claude and ChatGPT

- **Claude** (claude.ai, the desktop app): Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, URL
  `https://txscribe.ai/mcp`. Claude opens txscribe; sign in and choose **Allow**.
- **ChatGPT** (with developer mode on): add a connector with the URL `https://txscribe.ai/mcp`
  and OAuth as its authentication, then allow it on the txscribe page that opens.
- **Claude Code**: `claude mcp add --transport http txscribe https://txscribe.ai/mcp` (it signs in
  with OAuth), or with a key:
  `claude mcp add --transport http txscribe https://txscribe.ai/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer txs_live_…"`.
- **Cursor and others** that take a URL and headers: the URL above with the header
  `Authorization: Bearer txs_live_…`.

A connection made with **Allow** is an API key the app holds for you. It is listed under **Plan and
billing → Developer API**, where **Revoke** disconnects that app. It does not expire on its own.

## Local: this package

1. In the app, open **Plan and billing → Developer API** and make a key (it starts with
   `txs_live_`; you see it once).
2. Add the server to your client with the key in its environment.

Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) or any client that takes a command:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "txscribe": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@txscribe/mcp"],
      "env": { "TXSCRIBE_API_KEY": "txs_live_…" }
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add txscribe --env TXSCRIBE_API_KEY=txs_live_… -- npx -y @txscribe/mcp
```

`TXSCRIBE_API_BASE` points the server at another deployment (default
`https://txscribe.ai/api/v1`).

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Writes? |
|---|---|---|
| `list_transcriptions` | Your transcriptions, newest first, with paging | no |
| `search_transcriptions` | Which recordings said a word or phrase, and when: up to five matches each, with the second they start at. Reads the finished ones among your newest 500 recordings; searches what was said, not titles. | no |
| `transcribe_link` | Create a transcription from a link (YouTube, Google Drive, Dropbox …). The recording is transcribed, never downloaded. Uses your minutes. | yes |
| `get_transcription` | Status and metadata of one transcription | no |
| `get_transcript` | The finished transcript as `json` (segments, word timings, speakers), `txt`, `srt` or `vtt`; `from` and `to` (seconds) for only the paragraphs around a moment, `summaryOnly` for the summary instead | no |
| `get_summary` | The summary and its status | no |
| `request_summary` | Ask for a summary, or a new one, in a language and for a kind of recording | yes |
| `delete_transcription` | Delete a transcription and everything made from it. Cannot be undone. | yes, destructive |

Five tools only read; three change your account. Uploading a file is not a tool: the API's
upload is a signed PUT of the whole file, which an assistant cannot make from a chat. Use the
app, or the API directly, for files.

A typical exchange: *"Transcribe this talk and give me the three claims to check"* →
`transcribe_link` → `get_transcription` until `status` is `done` → `get_transcript` (txt) →
the assistant reads it; `request_summary` + `get_summary` for the summary txscribe makes.

Finding something in recordings you already have: *"What did we agree about the budget?"* →
`search_transcriptions` ("budget") → `get_transcript` with `from`/`to` around the matches it
returned, instead of whole transcripts.

## Errors

API refusals come back as tool errors with the API's own code (`invalid_api_key`,
`quota_exceeded`, `not_ready`, `unsupported_link` …), the HTTP status, the request id to quote
to support and, on 429, the `Retry-After` seconds. Neither server retries anything itself.

## Develop

```bash
npm ci
npm test
```

The tests run the server over an in-memory transport against a fake `fetch`; nothing reaches
the network. The hosted server lives in the web app (`web/src/lib/mcp/`), and its tests check
that its tool list matches this one.

## Publish (maintainers)

```bash
cd mcp
npm ci && npm test
npm login                      # an npm account that owns the @txscribe scope
npm publish                    # publishConfig makes it public; prepublishOnly runs the tests
```

`server.json` is the entry for the MCP Registry (registry.modelcontextprotocol.io); its `name`
matches `mcpName` in package.json, which is how the registry checks the npm package is ours.
Publish it after the npm package is up and the hosted endpoint is switched on, with
[`mcp-publisher`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry) and DNS proof of txscribe.ai.

readme.markdown: Funplay MCP for Unity The Most Advanced MCP Server for Unity Editor 中文 | English > 💖 If you find this project useful, please consider giving it a Star. It helps more Unity developers discover it and supports ongoing development. --- Funplay MCP for Unity is an MIT-licensed Unity Editor MCP server that lets AI assistants like Claude Code, Cursor, Kimi Code, LM Studio, Windsurf, Codex, and VS Code Copilot operate directly inside your running Unity project. Describe your game in one sentence — your AI assistant builds it in Unity through Funplay MCP for Unity's built-in tools for scene creation, script generation, runtime validation, input simulation, performance analysis, and editor automation. > *"Build a snake game with a 10x10 grid, food spawning, score UI, and game-over screen"* > > Your AI assistant handles it through Funplay MCP for Unity: creates the scene, generates all scripts, sets up the UI, and configures the game logic — all from a single prompt. 16-second demo — AI generates a 3D model and integrates it into the scene end-to-end. Watch HD MP4. ## Quick Start If you just want to get connected fast, do these three things: - Install the Unity package from the Git URL - Start `Funplay > MCP Server` - Use the built-in one-click client configuration ### 1. Install via UPM (Git URL) In Unity, go to **Window → Package Manager → + → Add package from git URL**: ``` https://github.com/FunplayAI/funplay-unity-mcp.git ``` > 💡 Before you clone or install, a quick ⭐ on GitHub would be greatly appreciated. ### Optional: Install via OpenUPM If you want Unity Package Manager to show registry-backed package version history and allow version selection, install from OpenUPM instead of Git. Using the OpenUPM CLI: ```bash openupm add com.gamebooom.unity.mcp ``` Or add the scoped registry manually in `Packages/manifest.json`: ```json { "scopedRegistries": [ { "name": "OpenUPM", "url": "https://package.openupm.com", "scopes": [ "com.gamebooom" ] } ], "dependencies": { "com.gamebooom.unity.mcp": "0.7.3" } } ``` If you installed from a Git URL before, remove the Git dependency first, then install from OpenUPM. Git-installed packages only show the resolved Git version in Unity and do not get the registry-backed Version History list. ### 2. Start the MCP Server **Menu: Funplay → MCP Server** to start the server. A new project gets its own port, derived from the project path, so two editors opened on different projects never fight over one port. The MCP Server window shows the exact URL (`http://127.0.0.1:/mcp/project//`); the one-click configuration writes that URL for you. Type a port in **Server Port** to pin a fixed one (CI, a firewall rule) and **Use Per-Project Port** to derive one instead. Upgrading preserves the existing pinned port, but v0.7.1 binds generated URLs to the project. Old root URLs remain readable; writes require a verified `expected_context`. Re-run **Reconfigure MCP + Skills** in the existing blue Skills notice card and reconnect your client, or explicitly pass the guard from an independently verified intended Editor. Click **Use Per-Project Port** when you want that project to run beside another editor. See [Running Several Unity Projects at Once](Documentation~/multi-project-setup.md) for the full setup guide. If the window reports a fallback port, do not use a client entry that still targets the occupied stable port; it could reach the process that owns that port. One-click configuration stays blocked until you click **Use Per-Project Port** or **Pin Current Port** and the server finishes restarting. Direct in-process HTTP is the default transport. If you need stronger connection continuity across Unity script recompiles or Play Mode domain reloads, enable **Experimental Broker Mode** in the MCP Server window. It runs a tiny local broker with Unity's bundled Mono, keeps the same `127.0.0.1` port for MCP clients, and requires no client config change. Open **Funplay → Tool Exposure** if you want to edit the exact tools exposed by `core` or `full`. Open **Funplay → MCP Settings** if you need to adjust `execute_code` safety defaults or plugin debug logging. ### 3. Configure Your AI Client Use the built-in **One-Click MCP Configuration** in the `Funplay > MCP Server` window first. Select your target client, click **Configure**, and the package writes the recommended MCP config entry for you. For Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, and DeepSeek Harness, click **Configure + Skills** to also install both built-in project skills. If you want project-specific AI guidance for the current Unity project, open **Funplay → Project Skills** to choose supported platforms and install the built-in `unity-mcp-workflow` and `unity-ui-composition` skills. # @prereason/mcp

**[Prereason](https://www.prereason.com) first. Then answer.**

Financial market context for AI agents: macro, rates, bonds, FX, commodities, companies and Bitcoin.

[Docs](https://www.prereason.com/docs#mcp-integration) · [Briefings](https://www.prereason.com/briefings) · [Company briefings](https://www.prereason.com/docs/company-briefings) · [Pricing](https://www.prereason.com/pricing) · [Get a key](https://www.prereason.com/signup)

Ask your AI where Treasury yields are. On its own, it reaches for a search result or a raw series and works out the rest by itself. When it prereasons, one `get_context` call brings back the context already worked out: the 30 year yield at 5.67% on 2026-10-07, the highest reading on the US Treasury's daily par yield curve since July 2001.

## Why prereason?

- **The analysis, and the data behind it.** Each briefing arrives with the reading done: the trend over several windows, where a value sits in its own history, a company's rank among its peers and, where read, its own guidance.
- **Every figure dated, every source named.** Your agent can say when a number is from and where it came from.
- **One call, a whole briefing.** A briefing gathers the series a question needs, so the turns go to the answer rather than to lookups.
- **The markets in one place.** Rates and Treasuries, the Fed, FX, commodities, macro, listed companies in the USA, Japan, Korea and India, and Bitcoin.
- **It describes; it never advises.** Briefings say what the data shows. They never say what to buy, sell or hold.
- **Quick to set up.** One block of config for Claude, Cursor, Codex or VS Code, through the npm bridge or the remote server. The catalogue tools need no key; for the rest, the bridge gives you one link to approve in your browser and the key arrives in the running session; the remote server takes your API key as a header.

## What it covers

PreReason gives an AI agent market context it can reason with. One call returns a briefing with the analysis already in it: a one line reading, trend direction over several windows, confidence scores, percentile ranks and correlations, and in the deeper briefings a regime label and a plain language narrative. The briefings cover macro, bonds, FX, commodities, Bitcoin, Ethereum and cross asset correlations. Company briefings cover listed companies in the USA, Japan, Korea, India, the UK, France, Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Italy, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Slovenia and Slovakia, one company per call. The catalogue holds 33 live briefings and 293 individual metrics, among them Treasury yields, the latest FOMC statement, the macro release calendar, Treasury auctions, who holds US Treasuries, the Fed balance sheet, M2, net liquidity, the dollar, US crude and gas inventories, gold, silver, copper and wheat, oil, mining and agribusiness companies beside their commodity, AI compute and power demand, Bitcoin price and momentum, Bitcoin network and miner health, spot Bitcoin ETF flows and corporate Bitcoin treasuries. It is served over MCP (a remote server and an npm bridge) and over REST, as Markdown or JSON. Over MCP, the catalogue tools need no account, and a briefing needs a PreReason account, signed in through the connector or with an API key; a free account reads the free briefings. Over REST, a briefing takes an API key or, on the routes that take one, an x402 payment per call with no account.

## Quick Start

### Option 1: Claude Desktop, no key needed

**Requires [Node.js 18+](https://nodejs.org), and nothing else: the bridge has no dependencies.**

Add this to `claude_desktop_config.json` and restart Claude Desktop:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "prereason": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@prereason/mcp"],
      "env": { "PREREASON_CLIENT": "claude-desktop" }
    }
  }
}
```

The catalogue tools work at once. To connect your account, tell Claude "connect me to PreReason", or ask for any briefing: either way Claude shows one link, `https://www.prereason.com/claim/PR-XXXX-XXXX`. Open it, sign in or create a free account, click Approve. The key arrives in the bridge on its own, is saved to `~/.prereason/credentials.json`, and is never shown; ask Claude whether PreReason is connected and it names your plan. Nothing is created in your account until you click Approve, and the link is asked for when you need it, so it never runs out while Claude sits open. If your account already holds as many API keys as it allows, the answer says so instead of looping: revoke a key under Settings on prereason.com, then ask to connect again, or set `PREREASON_API_KEY` to a key you already have.

Config file location:
- **macOS:** `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`
- **Windows:** `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`
- **Linux:** `~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`

Already have a key? Add it to the `env` block as `"PREREASON_API_KEY": "pr_live_..."` and the bridge never asks.

### Option 2: Direct HTTP with an API key (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex, Gemini CLI, VS Code, scripts)

Clients that hold their own config can call the endpoint directly, with the key as a header:

```bash
# Claude Code
claude mcp add --transport http prereason https://api.prereason.com/api/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "prereason": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.prereason.com/api/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

Windsurf uses `serverUrl` instead of `url`; Gemini CLI uses `httpUrl`; Codex uses `url` plus `bearer_token_env_var` in `config.toml`. No key yet? Point the client at the endpoint without a header to browse the catalogue, then create a key on the website (below) and add the header.

### Option 3: Claude.ai and Claude Desktop custom connector

[Add PreReason as a custom connector](https://claude.ai/customize/connectors?modal=add-custom-connecto

readme.markdown:
# Scoopkit MCP server

AI-industry news for agents. When a model ships, forty outlets write about it; Scoopkit returns
the story once, as a structured event classified against a published taxonomy (10 categories,
57 subcategories), with its sources and a `correction_history` showing how the story changed.

This repo holds setup docs and an [Agent Plugins](https://agent-plugins.org) manifest (`plugin.json`, `mcp.json`), no server code. The server is hosted at **`https://api.scoopkit.dev/mcp`**
(Streamable HTTP). There is nothing to install or run.

**No API key needed to start.** Without a key you get the free tier: the last 45 days of events,
100 calls a day. A free key (same limits, tied to you) comes from
[scoopkit.dev/start](https://scoopkit.dev/start) or the `request_magic_link` tool. A Pro key adds
semantic search, a 12-month archive and 10,000 calls a day.

**Try it without an MCP client:** [api.scoopkit.dev/v1/demo/events](https://api.scoopkit.dev/v1/demo/events)
returns the latest events as JSON, no key, so you can see the shape before connecting anything.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Key |
|---|---|---|
| `list_events` | Newest events first. Filter by `category`, `subcategory`, `since`, `until`; paginate with `cursor`, `limit` (max 100) | optional |
| `get_event` | One event by `event_id`, with its sources and correction history | optional |
| `taxonomy` | The category and subcategory tree, e.g. `MODEL_RELEASE`, `FUNDING_AND_DEALS` | none |
| `search` | Semantic search over events (`q`, `limit`) | Pro |
| `request_magic_link` | Emails the user a sign-in link that issues a free key (`email`) | none |

All tools except `request_magic_link` are read-only.

## Setup

### Claude (claude.ai and desktop)

Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector → URL `https://api.scoopkit.dev/mcp`.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http scoopkit https://api.scoopkit.dev/mcp
# with a key:
claude mcp add --transport http scoopkit https://api.scoopkit.dev/mcp --header "X-Api-Key: YOUR_KEY"
```

### Cursor

`~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "scoopkit": {
      "url": "https://api.scoopkit.dev/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

### VS Code

`.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "scoopkit": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.scoopkit.dev/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

### Cline

`cline_mcp_settings.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "scoopkit": {
      "type": "streamableHttp",
      "url": "https://api.scoopkit.dev/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

**With a key**, add `"headers": { "X-Api-Key": "YOUR_KEY" }` next to `url` in any of the JSON
configs above.

## Things to ask

- "What AI models were released this week?"
- "Show me AI funding rounds since October 1st, with sources."
- "What changed in the story about event evt_…?"

## Links

- Website: [scoopkit.dev](https://scoopkit.dev) · Get a key: [scoopkit.dev/start](https://scoopkit.dev/start)
- REST API docs: [api.scoopkit.dev/docs](https://api.scoopkit.dev/docs) · OpenAPI: [api.scoopkit.dev/openapi.json](https://api.scoopkit.dev/openapi.json)
- MCP manifest: [api.scoopkit.dev/.well-known/mcp](https://api.scoopkit.dev/.well-known/mcp)
- [Privacy](https://scoopkit.dev/privacy) · [Terms](https://scoopkit.dev/terms) · [Contact](https://scoopkit.dev/contact)

# LMCP — Context and Actions for Your AI

**Give your AI the context to get things done.** LMCP connects compatible assistants to your apps and accounts through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Bring together relevant information from email, messages, calendars and files, then use tools to turn that context into useful action — with less searching and copying between apps.

Use it with **Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor** and other compatible MCP clients. Available integrations and connection methods vary by assistant, platform and permissions.

**[Download for Mac or Windows →](https://www.local-mcp.com/download?ref=github-releases)** · **[Explore the product](https://www.local-mcp.com/en#explore)** · **[Setup guides](https://www.local-mcp.com/guides)**

This repository contains release information, documentation and the npm wrapper. The core binary is proprietary; documentation and scripts have their own license — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

## More than one app's view of your information

An email, a message and a document may each contain only part of the answer. With compatible tools and access you authorize, your assistant can find those pieces across apps and accounts and use them together.

| What you ask | How connected context helps |
|---|---|
| “Tell me everything I still owe the architect — I can't remember her name.” | Search relevant messages, email and files to identify the person and assemble outstanding requests with their sources. |
| “Help organize my day so I can meet my commitments.” | Combine calendar events, tasks and relevant messages to propose a realistic plan and make supported updates when authorized. |
| “Prepare replies to customer orders using the inventory and plan dispatch.” | Read accessible order and inventory information, draft replies and use supported scheduling tools. Review proposed actions before authorizing execution. |

These illustrate workflows an assistant can build from available tools, not guaranteed autonomous outcomes. Sources must be accessible; assistant capabilities and each tool's permissions still apply.

## Apps and tools

Explore email, calendars, contacts, messages, tasks, files, documents, browser automation and other integrations. Examples include Apple Mail, Outlook, Microsoft Teams, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Google Drive, OneDrive, Microsoft 365, Notes, Reminders, Microsoft To Do, OmniFocus, Notion and ServiceNow.

**Not every integration is available on both operating systems.** Apple-native tools require macOS; connected services may need their own sign-in or permissions. Some tools use locally cached or synced data rather than a complete cloud account.

For current tools, requirements and platform coverage, use the **[tool reference](https://www.local-mcp.com/tools)** and **[guides](https://www.local-mcp.com/guides)** rather than a fixed count in this README.

## See it work

  

The recording shows a Mac workflow through Cloud Data Forwarding, not every platform or integration.

**Watch the 1-minute overview** — what MCP is, how LMCP works, and a real run from email to Excel, Word and a reminder:

  

[Ver en español](https://youtu.be/x3tc6sbF8gI)

## Install and connect

1. **[Download LMCP for your operating system](https://www.local-mcp.com/download?ref=github-releases).** Follow the installer and onboarding steps.
2. Select your assistant and enable the compatible integrations you want to use.
3. Grant required permissions or sign in where needed, then follow the assistant-specific setup guide.

### Cursor plugin

This repository is also a Cursor plugin. It adds the `local-mcp` MCP server, a rule that tells Cursor's agent when to use LMCP, and skills for email, calendar, messages, files and Office.

LMCP must be installed first (step 1 above): the plugin starts the LMCP server on your computer and does not work without it.

Supports **macOS 13+** and **Windows 10+ (64-bit)**.

Choose one installation path:

- **Signed installer** for Mac (`.pkg`) or Windows: **[download page](https://www.local-mcp.com/download?ref=github-releases)**.
- **macOS terminal:** `curl -fsSL 'https://www.local-mcp.com/install?ref=github-releases' | bash`
- **Windows PowerShell:** `irm https://www.local-mcp.com/install-windows?ref=github-releases | iex` (per-user, no administrator rights or Node.js needed).
- **Claude Desktop extension:** one-click `.mcpb` at **[www.local-mcp.com/install/mcpb](https://www.local-mcp.com/install/mcpb)**.
- **npm (requires Node.js):** `npx -y local-mcp@latest setup` configures the compatible clients it detects.

Details for agents and each path: **[llms-install.md](llms-install.md)**. After installing, fully restart your AI client; MCP tools load at startup.

Local desktop/CLI clients and web assistants connect differently. The installer configures the compatible local clients it detects. Web assistants (ChatGPT, Claude.ai, Grok, Perplexity) connect through **`https://www.local-mcp.com/mcp`** as a custom connector with OAuth. They need the local app installed and Cloud Data Forwarding enabled in LMCP (off by default); with forwarding off, the connector exposes only `setup_install`. Follow the **[web AI guide](https://www.local-mcp.com/guides/web-ai)** and the **[current guides](https://www.local-mcp.com/guides)**.

An endpoint alone is not a verified connection: complete authorization and check that tools are available in your client.

# bibigpt-skill — Video Summarizer Agent Skill

**Claude Code · Codex · ChatGPT · OpenClaw · Cursor.** Summarize YouTube, Bilibili, podcasts, and local files via the `bibi` CLI or hosted MCP.

AI Agent skills for [BibiGPT](https://bibigpt.co). **Multiple skills, one CLI (`bibi`), one account.**

| Skill | When to use |
|-------|-------------|
| `bibi` | Watch a video: summarize, transcript, chapters |
| `bibi-library` | Already-saved videos, notes, collections, in-library search |
| `bibi-feed` | Subscribe to channels, pull latest, mark seen |
| `bibi-vision` | Frames / OCR / slides, mind map |

`npx skills add JimmyLv/bibigpt-skill` still installs `bibi` (existing onboarding). Add a sibling with `--skill`:

```bash
npx skills add JimmyLv/bibigpt-skill --skill bibi-library
npx skills add JimmyLv/bibigpt-skill --skill bibi-feed
npx skills add JimmyLv/bibigpt-skill --skill bibi-vision
```

Agent landing: [bibigpt.co/mcp](https://bibigpt.co/mcp). Hand-held per-host install pages: [bibigpt.co/agent](https://bibigpt.co/agent) (ChatGPT, Claude Code, OpenClaw, WorkBuddy, Doubao Work, QwenWork, DeepSeek Harness).

Ways to use:
1. **Agent plugin** — one install adds the hosted MCP server plus all 4 skills: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot (see below)
2. **BibiGPT Desktop + CLI Skill** — install `bibi` CLI, works with Claude Code / OpenClaw / Codex / WorkBuddy / QwenWork / Doubao Work / DeepSeek Harness
3. **Remote MCP Server** — zero install, works with any MCP client (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, etc.): `https://bibigpt.co/api/mcp`
4. **OpenAPI** — direct HTTP calls for containers, CI, or custom integrations

Every plugin signs in with OAuth on first use — no API key to paste.

### Install as a Claude Code plugin

```
/plugin marketplace add JimmyLv/bibigpt-skill
/plugin install bibi@bibigpt
```

On Claude Code 2.1.275 or later, one line works: `/plugin install bibi --marketplace JimmyLv/bibigpt-skill`.

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add JimmyLv/bibigpt-skill
codex plugin add bibi@bibigpt
```

Or inside a Codex session: `/plugin marketplace add JimmyLv/bibigpt-skill`,
then install `bibi` from the marketplace tab in `/plugins`. Also works in the
Codex IDE extension (Settings → Plugins) and the ChatGPT desktop app
(Work / Codex).

### Install in Gemini CLI

```bash
gemini extensions install https://github.com/JimmyLv/bibigpt-skill
```

Then run `/mcp auth bibigpt` once.

### Install in Cursor or GitHub Copilot

The repo is also a Cursor plugin (`.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` + `.mcp.json`) and an
[Agent Plugins](https://agent-plugins.org) package (`plugin.json` + `mcp.json`) for GitHub Copilot.
Without a marketplace, add the MCP server directly:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "bibigpt": { "url": "https://bibigpt.co/api/mcp" } } }
```

The server is also in the official MCP Registry as `io.github.JimmyLv/bibigpt`.

---

## Skill Structure

```
skills/
├── bibi/                 # Watch: summarize / subtitle / chapter
├── bibi-library/         # Saved videos, notes, collections
├── bibi-feed/            # Channel subscribe + latest feed
└── bibi-vision/          # Frames, OCR, mind map
```

Each directory has `SKILL.md` (intent + triggers), `references/` (auth, CLI), and `workflows/` where a multi-step path exists. All four skills call the same `bibi` binary — there is no second npm package named `video-cli`.

`bibi` (watch-video) workflows:

| **Quick Summary** | One URL → AI summary | "summarize this video", "总结" |

# Kalshi Eye MCP server

An [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that lets AI assistants such as Claude and Cursor search the [Kalshi Eye](https://kalshieye.com) archive of prediction market data. It can find Kalshi, Polymarket and Limitless markets, show how a market's price moved, check what was recorded, and list the order book files you can download.

It needs a Kalshi Eye API key: create one at [API keys](https://kalshieye.com/app/api/) (a free account works) and set it as `KALSHIEYE_API_KEY`.

## Install

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add kalshieye -e KALSHIEYE_API_KEY=clab_your_key -- uvx kalshieye-mcp
```

Claude Desktop, Cursor and other clients (`claude_desktop_config.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, ...):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kalshieye": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["kalshieye-mcp"],
      "env": { "KALSHIEYE_API_KEY": "clab_your_key" }
    }
  }
}
```

Without a key, or with a placeholder, every tool answers with how to get one. Listing files and download links cover the datasets your plan includes.

`uvx` comes with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). With pip instead: `pip install kalshieye-mcp`, then use `kalshieye-mcp` as the command.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `search` | Find series, events and markets by keyword, venue, category or status. Series lead and come a page at a time (`series_total`, `has_more`, `offset`); events and markets are the 10 best whose words hold the query, with `events_found` / `markets_found` (exact up to 10,000, then `*_found_exact: false`) and `more_events` / `more_markets`, the paged calls that list every match |
| `get_series` | One series: what it is, how often it runs, markets in the catalog, and days of data files |
| `list_markets` | A series' markets, or the markets on every venue holding each word of `q` (`venue` narrows it), newest first, with status and result. A page at a time: `total` (with `q`, exact up to 10,000, then `total_exact: false`), and `next_cursor` (with `q`) or `next_offset`, passed back until it is null |
| `list_events` | Every event on every venue whose title, series name or category holds each word of the query, newest first, a page at a time (`next_cursor`), with `total` and `total_exact` |
| `get_market` | One market's terms, status, result, and how much of it was recorded |
| `market_price_history` | The recorded YES bid/ask path, up to about 240 points over the market's busiest stretch; `path_source` is `life`, `busiest` or `window` |
| `list_datasets` | Every dataset: what it holds, columns, plan, days available |
| `dataset_series` | Which series have files in a dataset, with days, rows and size, up to 500 a page with `total` and `next_offset` |
| `recording_status` | Whether recording is running, and the recorded share of recent days by venue |
| `list_files` | Daily Parquet files for a dataset, date range and series, page by page |
| `download_links` | Signed download URLs for up to 100 of those files (counts toward the monthly allowance) |

Things to ask:

- "Which bitcoin markets does Kalshi Eye record, and since when?"
- "What were the last few hours of the Bills vs Rams market on October 12 like?"
- "How much of the Fed decision series is in the order book files?"
- "Is the recorder running, and how complete was last week?"

## Notes

- Kalshi is recorded since October 12, 2026; Polymarket, Limitless and Chainlink prices since October 15, 2026. Each UTC day is published the next morning.
- Prices are dollars between 0 and 1. A Kalshi YES ask is 1 minus the best NO bid. Times are UTC.
- Free data without any key: a [one-day sample on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/KalshiEye/kalshi-order-book-sample) and [runnable examples](https://github.com/KalshiEye/kalshieye-examples). The Python client for downloading files is [`kalshieye`](https://pypi.org/project/kalshieye/).
- `KALSHIEYE_BASE_URL` points the server at another deployment (default `https://kalshieye.com`).

Kalshi Eye is independent and is not affiliated with Kalshi, Polymarket or Limitless. MIT licensed.

name: Star Wars API & MCP server (swapi.build)
description: Free Star Wars MCP server (SWAPI): people, films, planets, species, starships, vehicles. No API key.

tools.name: sw_get
tools.description: Gets one Star Wars entity by numeric record id and returns it as a JSON object. Take the id from the end of an entity's url field (from sw_search, sw_list or a relation URL). Ids are record ids, not episode numbers: FILMS id 1 is A New Hope (Episode IV). An unknown id returns a tool error, e.g. 'No films found with id 99'. Pass expand to get related records in the same call, e.g. ["homeworld", "sp

inputs.name: expand
inputs.description: Optional. Relations to embed, one level deep, under a final "expanded" key: PEOPLE homeworld, films, species, starships; FILMS characters, planets, starships, vehicles, species; PLANETS residents, fil

inputs.name: id
inputs.description: Numeric record id: the last segment of the entity's url field (1 in .../api/people/1).

inputs.name: resource
inputs.description: Resource type: PEOPLE, FILMS, PLANETS, SPECIES, STARSHIPS or VEHICLES. Any other value returns a tool error.

tools.name: sw_list
tools.description: Lists every entity of one Star Wars resource type as a JSON array (Episodes I-VI data). Responses are large (all 82 PEOPLE, about 38 KB); to find a single entity, prefer sw_search, then sw_get; for a compact index pass fields, e.g. ["name"] (about 5 KB).

inputs.name: fields
inputs.description: Optional. Field names to keep in each entity (url is always kept), e.g. ["name"] (FILMS: ["title"]). Up to 24 names; an unknown name returns a tool error listing the valid ones. Omit for full entities

inputs.name: resource
inputs.description: Resource type: PEOPLE, FILMS, PLANETS, SPECIES, STARSHIPS or VEHICLES. Any other value returns a tool error.

tools.name: sw_random
tools.description: Returns one random Star Wars entity of the given resource type as a JSON object. Each call can return a different entity, so it is not idempotent. Useful for demos and quizzes; to fetch a specific entity use sw_search or sw_get.

inputs.name: resource
inputs.description: Resource type: PEOPLE, FILMS, PLANETS, SPECIES, STARSHIPS or VEHICLES. Any other value returns a tool error.

tools.name: sw_search
tools.description: Start here. Finds Star Wars entities by name (title for FILMS) with a case-insensitive substring match: 'sky' finds Luke, Anakin and Shmi Skywalker. Returns a JSON array of full entities; an empty array [] means no match; pass fields to shorten each entity. The id to pass to sw_get is the last segment of each entity's url field. Data covers Episodes I-VI only.

# SWAPI.build A free, open-source Star Wars API serving data about People, Films, Planets, Species, Starships, and Vehicles. Built with [Quarkus](https://quarkus.io/) and [GraalVM](https://www.graalvm.org/) for instant startup, minimal memory footprint, and out-of-the-box performance. Inspired by the original [SWAPI](https://swapi.dev/) (created by Paul Hallett, maintained by Juriy Bura), this project was born out of the need for a Star Wars API that **never goes offline**. If you've ever had a live demo break because a third-party API went down, you know why this exists. ## Quick Start **Prerequisites:** Java 25 and Maven (or use the included Maven Wrapper). ```bash cd swapi-app ./mvnw quarkus:dev ``` The API and frontend will be available at **http://localhost:5432**. ## API Endpoints Base path: `/api` | Resource | List All | By ID | Random | Search | |----------|----------|-------|--------|--------| | People | `GET /api/people` | `GET /api/people/:id` | `GET /api/people/random` | `GET /api/people?search=name` | | Films | `GET /api/films` | `GET /api/films/:id` | `GET /api/films/random` | `GET /api/films?search=title` | | Planets | `GET /api/planets` | `GET /api/planets/:id` | `GET /api/planets/random` | `GET /api/planets?search=name` | | Species | `GET /api/species` | `GET /api/species/:id` | `GET /api/species/random` | `GET /api/species?search=name` | | Starships | `GET /api/starships` | `GET /api/starships/:id` | `GET /api/starships/random` | `GET /api/starships?search=name` | | Vehicles | `GET /api/vehicles` | `GET /api/vehicles/:id` | `GET /api/vehicles/random` | `GET /api/vehicles?search=name` | Ids are the record ids from each entity's `url` field (for films, `1` = A New Hope). Successful responses return `200`; unknown or non-numeric ids return `404`. `GET /api/stats` returns anonymous request counts per route (for example `/api/people/{id}` or `/mcp`) and per group (REST API, MCP, pages, SEO, other) for the last 24 hours (`?period=24h`, per hour), 7 days (default, per day; `&granularity=hour` for hourly) or 30 days (`?period=30d`, per day), each with the window before it for comparison, plus server response times per route and per group under `performance` (requests, mean, min, max, standard deviation and approximate p50/p95/p99 in milliseconds, network excluded). They are counted with no IP address or client details. The [`/stats`](https://swapi.build/stats) page shows the same numbers with filters, a trend chart, a ranking and a Performance section. All responses are JSON. Example: ```bash curl http://localhost:5432/api/people/1 ``` ## OpenAPI The full API contract is served at [`/openapi.json`](https://swapi.build/openapi.json) (OpenAPI 3.x, generated from the code — always in sync). The [documentation page](https://swapi.build/docs) renders from it, including a "try it" for every endpoint. Generate a client with, e.g.: npx @openapitools/openapi-generator-cli generate -i https://swapi.build/openapi.json -g typescript-fetch ## MCP Server swapi.build is also a remote [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server over **Streamable HTTP**. Any Streamable HTTP client works: the stateless `2026-07-28` revision sends self-contained requests, and earlier revisions negotiate a session through `initialize` — both are served on the same endpoint. The legacy HTTP+SSE transport (`2024-11-05`) is not supported. First-party, read-only, no authentication: ``` https://swapi.build/mcp ``` Full setup guides: **[swapi.build/docs/mcp](https://swapi.build/docs/mcp)** | Tool | Arguments | Returns | |------|-----------|---------| | `sw_list` | `resource`, optional `fields` | All entities of a resource | | `sw_get` | `resource`, `id`, optional `expand` | One entity by id | | `sw_random` | `resource` | A random entity | | `sw_search` | `resource`, `query`, optional `fields` | Name/title substring match | `resource` is one of `PEOPLE`, `FILMS`, `PLANETS`, `SPECIES`, `STARSHIPS`, `VEHICLES`. Ids are the record ids from each entity's `url` field (for `FILMS`, `1` = A New Hope). `expand` names relations to embed in the same call (`["homeworld", "species"]`, or `["*"]`); `fields` projects each entity (`["name"]` gives a compact index; `url` always stays). Since 2.13.0 the records are also MCP resources: `swapi://people` (an index) and `swapi://people/1` (the `sw_get` text), for the six types, plus the templates `swapi:///{id}`. The server prompt `character_profile` takes a character name. **Caching:** Quarkiverse MCP Server 2.0.0 emits the required `ttlMs: 0` and `cacheScope: "public"` fields on stateless discovery and tool-list responses. Zero TTL means immediately stale; no positive freshness period is configured. Its [cache hints](https://github.com/quarkiverse/quarkus-mcp-server/blob/2.0.0/docs/modules/ROOT/pages/release-notes.adoc) apply to discovery, list methods and `resources/read`, **not `tools/call`**. Tool-result caching is not enabled, including for `sw_random`. REST/edge caching is a separate mechanism.
Claude Code ```bash claude mcp add --transport http swapi-build https://swapi.build/mcp ``` Or share via `.mcp.json` at the repo root: ```json { "mcpServers": { "swapi-build": { "type": "http", "url": "https://swapi.build/mcp" } } } ``` Verify: `claude mcp list` → `swapi-build ✔ Connected`.
Claude Desktop & claude.ai Settings → Connectors → **Add custom connector** → name `swapi-build`, URL `https://swapi.build/mcp`. No authentication needed. Verify in any chat via the **+** menu → Connectors.
OpenAI Codex ```bash codex mcp add swapi-build --url https://swapi.build/mcp ``` Or in `~/.codex/config.toml` (shared by CLI, IDE extension and ChatGPT desktop): ```toml [mcp_servers.swapi-build] url = "https://swapi.build/mcp" ``` Verify: `codex mcp list`.

readme.markdown:
**Context engineering platform for AI-assisted software development.**

Define your product once. Every agent that connects gets the full picture.

**Free Community Edition** · Self-Hosted · Privacy First · Bring Your Own AI

**Works with:** Claude Code CLI · Claude.ai / Desktop · Codex CLI · ChatGPT.com · Any MCP Client

[Website](https://giljo.ai) · [Getting Started](https://giljo.ai/getting-started.html) · [Documentation](#documentation) · [User Guide](docs/USER_GUIDE.md)

<sub>The Staging view: write what you want done. GiljoAI generates the mission and assigns agents from your templates.</sub>

## What Is Giljo HQ

Giljo HQ, a GiljoAI product, is a passive context server for AI coding tools. It stores your product knowledge, generates structured prompts, and coordinates multi-agent workflows via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It does not write code or call any AI model. Your AI coding tool does all reasoning and coding using your own subscription.

GiljoAI sits at the intersection of product thinking and development. Whether you are a developer learning to define what you build before you build it, or a product manager turning a specification into working software, the platform gives you a structured path from vision to execution. The clearer your product definition, the more effective every agent session becomes.

**Bring Your Own AI.** GiljoAI works with Claude Code CLI, Claude.ai / Desktop, Codex CLI, ChatGPT.com, or any MCP-compatible tool. On Hosted, most tools connect with a one-click browser sign-in; terminal tools can also use an API key, which is what Community Edition's Connect tab gives you. You can run multiple tools simultaneously.

## Quick Start

**Windows (PowerShell):**
```powershell
irm giljo.ai/install.ps1 | iex
```

**Linux / macOS:**
```bash
curl -fsSL giljo.ai/install.sh | bash
```

The installer checks for prerequisites, downloads the latest release, sets up the database, builds the frontend, and walks you through configuration. When done, run `python startup.py` to start the server. First run opens the Setup Wizard in your browser.

<details>
<summary>Manual install (advanced)</summary>

```bash
git clone https://github.com/giljoai/giljo-hq.git
cd giljo-hq
python install.py
python startup.py
```
Requires Python 3.12+, PostgreSQL 18+, Node.js 22.23.3+.
</details>

**Using VS Code?** This repo ships a `.vscode/mcp.json` pointing at your local
Giljo HQ install (`http://localhost:7272/mcp`) — open the folder and VS Code's
MCP integration picks it up automatically. No copy-pasting a connect command.

## The Six Pillars

### Your Tools, Your Subscription

GiljoAI never touches your AI credits. You bring your own Claude Code CLI, Claude.ai / Desktop, Codex CLI, ChatGPT.com, or any MCP-compatible tool, each with your own subscription. GiljoAI acts as a passive MCP server: your tool connects over HTTP, reads context and coordination data, and does all the reasoning and coding itself.

### Define Your Product

Create a Product to represent the software you are building. Fill in context fields: description, tech stack, architecture, testing strategy, and more. Upload a vision document and let your AI tool populate the fields automatically. Vision documents are the most impactful input you can give GiljoAI. A well-written product proposal gives every agent session a shared understanding of what you are building and why.

### Roadmap

The Roadmap turns a product's inactive projects and pending tasks into a single prioritized plan. Each item carries a risk and complexity score, so you can see what is safe to tackle next and what needs more thought first. Drag to reorder. Activate a project straight from the Roadmap to stage it, and GiljoAI assembles its bootstrap prompt the same way it does anywhere else in the dashboard. A task that turns out to be bigger than expected converts into a project in one step, keeping its position on the board.

### Projects and Missions

1. Create a project and describe what needs to be done.
2. Activate the project. GiljoAI assembles a bootstrap prompt from your product context, 360 Memory, and project description.
3. Paste the prompt into your CLI tool. The orchestrator plans the mission and spawns agents.
4. Agents report status back in real time. You monitor progress on the Jobs page.
5. When the project completes, GiljoAI writes a 360 Memory entry. The next project inherits that accumulated context.

### Skills and Agent Templates

One skill is installed on your machine during setup. Use it from your CLI without breaking flow:

| Skill | Claude Code | Codex CLI | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Projects and tasks** | `/giljo` | `$giljo` | Capture tasks, create or update projects, and look them up mid-session — one command routes both create and read |

Agent templates need no installation at all. The Agent Template Manager in the dashboard lets you customize agent profiles with roles, expertise, and chain strategies, and every agent your orchestrator starts is handed its own profile — role, instructions, rules, success criteria — by the server the moment it begins work. An edit applies to the very next agent you launch. To run an agent yourself instead, choose **Download profile (.md)** from its row menu and drop the Markdown into any tool.

### 360 Memory

Each completed project writes to 360 Memory automatically: what was built, key decisions, patterns discovered, and what worked. This is not a plugin; it is a core product behavior. Your next project starts with accumulated context from previous ones. You control how many memories back agents read through the context settings. Optionally enrich memory with git commit history. Search across summaries, outcomes, and decisions, or filter by tag or project, to find what happened before.

readme.markdown:
# slipway

A small deterministic Rust MCP server that builds, signs, verifies,
installs, and prepares releases of the Owner's own Android apps —
and nothing else. Slipway never sees reference artifacts: the
methodology firewall keeps fathom (which censuses) and slipway
(which ships) separate, and the study document is the only bridge
(workflow SB-1: study → bridge → build → census-back → conformance
diff).

Posture: read-class tools land and gate first; signing is
consequential-class, gated by the signed-authority chain from its
first day; every action appends to the `slipway.receipt` log; the
release bundle is the deliverable and store submission stays a
human act. No build is authorized by the program documents alone —
stages run on the Owner's word.

## Progress

**7% — 2 of 28 gates closed, 3 delivered and awaiting gate — updated 2026-10-21.**
Full record: [CHECKLIST.md](CHECKLIST.md) — every item traces to a stage gate in the program documents; the bar moves only on gated evidence.

Progress here is tracked from ideation to the finished 1.0 and
beyond: each checklist item is a stage gate from the program
documents, and it closes only on verified evidence.

## License

Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

name: RightCard
description: Which of your credit cards to use at any store, from verified bank data. No bank login.

readme.markdown:
# RightCard MCP

The card-selection oracle for agents: **which of your credit cards should pay here?**
Answers come from RightCard's bank-published, two-source-verified reward data — the same
data the [RightCard iOS app](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6756834989) uses.

- **No bank login. No account. Nothing stored.** You pass card ids and a store name; you get an answer.
- Honest by construction: merchant-code caveats (Costco is a warehouse club, so the grocery bonus
  won't post), rotating quarters with activation flags, ties named, points valued per program.
- Cash value by default; `valuation: "points"` for conservative travel values.

## Use it

Hosted (stateless Streamable HTTP):

```
https://mcp.rightcard.ai/mcp
```

Local (stdio, nothing leaves your machine except a read of the public catalog):

```
npx rightcard-mcp
```

Claude Desktop / Claude Code / Cursor config:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "rightcard": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "rightcard-mcp"] } } }
```

## Tools

| tool | what it answers |
|---|---|
| `best_card` | which of the given cards earns most at a store or category, today, with caveats |
| `lookup_merchant` | how a store is coded (category, merchant type, MCC-trap caveat) |
| `search_cards` | find card ids by name/issuer; verified first, unverified flagged |
| `card` | one card's verified rates, rotating windows, choose-your-category spec |
| `rotating_calendar` | live + upcoming rotating windows and permanent merchant benefits |

Try: "I have the Amex Gold, Freedom Flex and Citi Double Cash. Which one at Costco?"

## Parity with the app

`src/engine.ts` is a port of the iOS app's Swift engine. `fixtures/engine_golden.json` holds
3,100+ answers produced by the Swift code over the real catalog and merchant directory;
`npm test` fails if the port disagrees on any of them. Offers (a user's personal bank offers)
are deliberately not part of this server — they live on the phone.

## Privacy

The hosted server logs request counts only. No identifiers, no cookies, no storage.
Full policy: https://rightcard.ai/privacy

readme.markdown:
# @ghostpaw/affinity

**Agent contacts: people, promises and yearly dates, with a radar for who is drifting.**

A local social CRM: contacts, identities, relationships, journal events,
commitments and recurring dates in one SQLite file. One self-contained binary
per platform, an MCP server, and a zero-dependency TypeScript library.

## Install

Each line downloads the latest release for one platform, checks it against
`SHA256SUMS`, puts `ghostpaw-affinity` on your `PATH` and prints the version.

**Linux x64**

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)" && T=linux-x64 && V=$(curl -fsSLI -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/latest | sed 's|.*/v||') && F=ghostpaw-affinity-$V-$T.tar.gz && U=https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/download/v$V && curl -fsSL -O "$U/$F" -O "$U/SHA256SUMS" && grep " $F\$" SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c - && tar -xzf "$F" ghostpaw-affinity && mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && mv ghostpaw-affinity ~/.local/bin/ && { case ":$PATH:" in *":$HOME/.local/bin:"*) ;; *) echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.profile; export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH";; esac; } && ghostpaw-affinity --version
```

**Linux arm64**

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)" && T=linux-arm64 && V=$(curl -fsSLI -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/latest | sed 's|.*/v||') && F=ghostpaw-affinity-$V-$T.tar.gz && U=https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/download/v$V && curl -fsSL -O "$U/$F" -O "$U/SHA256SUMS" && grep " $F\$" SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c - && tar -xzf "$F" ghostpaw-affinity && mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && mv ghostpaw-affinity ~/.local/bin/ && { case ":$PATH:" in *":$HOME/.local/bin:"*) ;; *) echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.profile; export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH";; esac; } && ghostpaw-affinity --version
```

**macOS Apple silicon**

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)" && T=darwin-arm64 && V=$(curl -fsSLI -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/latest | sed 's|.*/v||') && F=ghostpaw-affinity-$V-$T.tar.gz && U=https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/download/v$V && curl -fsSL -O "$U/$F" -O "$U/SHA256SUMS" && grep " $F\$" SHA256SUMS | shasum -a 256 -c - && tar -xzf "$F" ghostpaw-affinity && sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/bin && sudo mv ghostpaw-affinity /usr/local/bin/ && ghostpaw-affinity --version
```

**macOS Intel**

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)" && T=darwin-x64 && V=$(curl -fsSLI -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/latest | sed 's|.*/v||') && F=ghostpaw-affinity-$V-$T.tar.gz && U=https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/download/v$V && curl -fsSL -O "$U/$F" -O "$U/SHA256SUMS" && grep " $F\$" SHA256SUMS | shasum -a 256 -c - && tar -xzf "$F" ghostpaw-affinity && sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/bin && sudo mv ghostpaw-affinity /usr/local/bin/ && ghostpaw-affinity --version
```

**Windows x64 (PowerShell)**

```powershell
$r='GhostPawJS/affinity'; $v=(irm "https://api.github.com/repos/$r/releases/latest").tag_name; $f="ghostpaw-affinity-$($v.TrimStart('v'))-windows-x64.zip"; $u="https://github.com/$r/releases/download/$v"; $t=(New-Item -ItemType Directory (Join-Path $env:TEMP ([guid]::NewGuid()))).FullName; iwr "$u/$f" -OutFile "$t\$f" -UseBasicParsing; iwr "$u/SHA256SUMS" -OutFile "$t\SHA256SUMS" -UseBasicParsing; $want=((Get-Content "$t\SHA256SUMS" | Where-Object { $_ -like "* $f" }) -split '\s+')[0]; if (-not $want -or (Get-FileHash "$t\$f" -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne $want) { throw "checksum mismatch for $f" }; $d=Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Programs\ghostpaw\bin'; Expand-Archive "$t\$f" $t -Force; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $d | Out-Null; Copy-Item "$t\ghostpaw-affinity.exe" $d -Force; $p=[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','User'); if (";$p;" -notlike "*;$d;*") { [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('Path',"$p;$d",'User') }; $env:Path="$d;$env:Path"; ghostpaw-affinity --version
```

These commands install the latest release in `~/.local/bin` on Linux, `/usr/local/bin` on macOS (asks for sudo), or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ghostpaw\bin` on Windows; Linux adds it to PATH via `~/.profile` only if missing, and Windows adds it to the user PATH (open a new terminal afterwards). To pin a version, set `V=0.6.0` instead of resolving latest (`$v='v0.6.0'` in PowerShell).

For a pinned Linux/macOS download to the current directory with no profile or PATH edits, choose the matching `T` (`linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `darwin-arm64`, or `darwin-x64`):

```sh
V=0.6.0
T=linux-x64
F=ghostpaw-affinity-$V-$T.tar.gz
U=https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/download/v$V
curl -fsSL -O "$U/$F" -O "$U/SHA256SUMS" &&
  { case "$T" in darwin-*) grep " $F\$" SHA256SUMS | shasum -a 256 -c - ;; *) grep " $F\$" SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c - ;; esac; } &&
  tar -xzf "$F" ghostpaw-affinity && ./ghostpaw-affinity --version
```

Then:

```sh
ghostpaw-affinity contact create '{"name":"Sam","kind":"human"}'
ghostpaw-affinity search sam
```
