# @ghostpaw/email

**Agent email: IMAP and SMTP in-process, cached in SQLite, with reading and sending as separate tools.**

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GhostPawJS/email/main/install.sh | sh
```

A standalone email engine for Node.js, built on SQLite.

Email treats IMAP sync, SMTP send, local caching, threading, search, and
transport errors as one coherent model instead of a grab bag of protocol
adapters. It ships as a single prebundled blob with zero runtime dependencies,
designed for three audiences at once: human developers working directly in
code, LLM agents operating through a structured `soul` / `tools` / `skills`
runtime, and agent operators who want a ready-to-use `email` CLI binary
without writing any wiring code.

## MCP server

Every client below starts the same stdio server: `ghostpaw-email mcp`.
For npm-based environments, use `npx -y @ghostpaw/email mcp` instead.
Cached messages live in `~/.ghostpaw/email.db` unless the `GHOSTPAW_EMAIL_DB`
environment variable (absolute path) or `--db <path>` says otherwise.

**Claude Code**

```bash
claude mcp add ghostpaw-email -- ghostpaw-email mcp
```

or as a plugin, which also installs the skill:

```bash
/plugin marketplace add GhostPawJS/email
/plugin install ghostpaw-email@ghostpaw-email
```

**Email CLI** (`~/.email/config.toml`)

```toml
[mcp_servers.ghostpaw-email]
command = "ghostpaw-email"
args = ["mcp"]
```

**Cursor** (`.cursor/mcp.json`), **Claude Desktop** (`claude_desktop_config.json`)
or a project `.mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ghostpaw-email": {
      "command": "ghostpaw-email",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Desktop users can also install `server.mcpb` from the
[latest GitHub release](https://github.com/GhostPawJS/email/releases/latest).
A Dockerfile is included for container hosts:
`docker build -t ghostpaw-email . && docker run -i --rm -v email:/data ghostpaw-email`.

The server speaks MCP 2026-07-28 (stateless, `server/discover`) and the
initialize-based revisions 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05.

Network operations use the existing CLI account configuration (`email account add`) or
`EMAIL_IMAP_HOST`, `EMAIL_SMTP_HOST`, `EMAIL_USER` and `EMAIL_PASS` (or
`EMAIL_ACCESS_TOKEN`). Discovery and cached reads need no account or credentials.
The surface database defaults to `~/.ghostpaw/email.db`; point `--db` at an
existing account cache to read it. Each network call opens and closes its IMAP
session. Connection commands do not retain a session between calls.

On POSIX, new accounts files and SQLite caches (including WAL/SHM sidecars) use mode `0600`, and newly created storage directories use `0700`. Existing permissions are preserved, except rewriting `accounts.json` sets it to `0600`.

Use `ghostpaw-email skill --short` for a compact command cheat sheet, `ghostpaw-email skill` for the full reference, and `ghostpaw-email skill --list` to list guides.

## Noun-verb CLI

Both `email` and `ghostpaw-email` accept this additive command tree. Existing
`account`, `read`, `search`, `compose`, `organize` and `sync` commands retain
their flags, output and exit codes. Use `mail --help` for the new tree and
`mail <verb> --help` for parameters.

```text
mail read | search
mail send | reply | forward | draft | update-draft | send-draft
mail mark-read | mark-unread | star | unstar | mark-answered
mail copy | move | archive | trash | junk | not-junk
mail set-labels | add-labels | remove-labels
mail create-folder | rename-folder | delete-folder | subscribe-folder | unsubscribe-folder
mail connect | disconnect | reconnect | sync | refresh-folders | watch
```

These 33 paths map to the 5 aligned tools. Action verbs set the tool's action;
`draft` sets `save_draft`. Search accepts its query as a positional argument.
Other fields use kebab-case flags, such as `--folder INBOX --uids 1 --uids 2`
and `--input @message.json` for a compose payload. Arrays accept repeated
flags or JSON; objects accept JSON. Values are literal, including a leading
`@`. Two flags read files: `--input` on the `mail` compose verbs and `--body`
on `compose send|reply|draft`. On those, `@path` reads the file, `@-` reads
stdin and `@@text` passes `@text`; help marks them `(@file, @- stdin, @@ literal @)`. An
empty or unreadable path exits 2. A single `-` reads stdin JSON;
explicit flags override stdin fields. `--` ends option parsing.

Global flags for the new commands: `--db <path>`, `--json`, `--quiet`,
`--compact`, `--help`/`-h`, `--version`/`-V`/`-v`, `--no-color`.
Output is JSON when piped or when `--json` is set. `--quiet` suppresses stdout.
`completions bash|zsh|fish` prints shell completion setup; `version` prints
the version and installation variant. The existing `tools [--json]`, `describe <tool>`,
`call <tool> [JSON|-]`, flat `mail_<tool> --parameter value`, `mcp` and `skill`
forms remain available.

| New command exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Success or no-op |
| 1 | Tool error |
| 2 | Usage or schema error |
| 3 | Clarification needed or not found |
| 4 | Conflict or version mismatch |
| 70 | Unexpected internal error |

Offline examples, run against an empty cache:

```sh
ghostpaw-email mail search invoice --db /tmp/email-port-example.db --json
ghostpaw-email mail read --view folders --db /tmp/email-port-example.db --json
ghostpaw-email mail --help
```

Search returns 0 matches and folder reads return 0 folders in an empty cache.
`GHOSTPAW_EMAIL_DB` sets the default cache path, otherwise
`~/.ghostpaw/email.db` is used. Local search and cached reads need no
credentials. Network operations use `email account add` configuration or
`EMAIL_IMAP_HOST`, `EMAIL_SMTP_HOST`, `EMAIL_USER` and `EMAIL_PASS` (or
`EMAIL_ACCESS_TOKEN`). Each invocation closes its network session;
`mail connect` does not retain a session for later commands.

## Tool CLI

```bash
ghostpaw-email tools
ghostpaw-email call mail_read '{"view":"folders"}' --db :memory:
ghostpaw-email call mail_search '{"query":"invo

…

# @ghostpaw/telegram

**Agent Telegram bots: every update mirrored into SQLite before your handler runs.**

```bash
ghostpaw-telegram --help             # after installing the release binary
```

Telegram bot channel engine — fetch transport with zero runtime dependencies, SQLite message mirror with FTS5 full-text search, eager file BLOB storage, markdown rendering, and a structured LLM tool facade.

Every incoming update is mirrored into a local SQLite database before your handler runs, giving you a persistent, queryable record of everything the bot sees — including the raw bytes of every photo, document, voice message, and video, which are downloaded in the background after the update is stored and kept once per SHA-256 hash. A failed download leaves the file row without a checksum, so you can retry it with `write.downloadFile`. It ships as a single prebundled blob designed for two audiences at once: human developers building bot backends in code, and LLM agents operating through a structured tool facade.

## MCP server

For npm-based environments, use `npx -y @ghostpaw/telegram mcp`.

environment variable (absolute path) or `--db <path>` says otherwise.

Without a token, these tools return plans; local reads and tool discovery work offline.
The `.mcp.json` token placeholder must be supplied by the client environment.
The server reads the mirror populated by your library transport; it does not poll for updates.

## Noun-verb CLI

The 27 command paths derive from the 4 tool schemas:

```text

message send <chatId> <text> | edit <chatId> <messageId> <text>
message delete <chatId> <messageId> | pin <chatId> <messageId> | unpin <chatId> <messageId>
message typing <chatId> | forward <fromChatId> <messageId> <toChatId>
member ban <chatId> <userId> | unban <chatId> <userId> | restrict <chatId> <userId>
member promote <chatId> <userId> | kick <chatId> <userId> | show <chatId> <userId>
member list <chatId>
```

Use `help <noun>` or `<noun> <verb> --help` for schema flags. Fields accept
kebab-case flags, such as `--can-send-messages true` and `--is-admin false`.
Objects accept JSON; arrays accept repeated flags or JSON. Values are literal,
including a leading `@`; no flag reads a file.
A single `-` reads stdin JSON; explicit flags override stdin fields.
`--` ends option parsing.

Global flags: `--db <path>`, `--json`, `--quiet`, `--compact`, `--help`/`-h`,
`--version`/`-V`/`-v`, `--no-color`. Piped output defaults to JSON;
`--quiet` suppresses stdout. `completions bash|zsh|fish` prints completion
setup and `version` prints the package version and installation variant.

Existing `tools [--json]`, `describe <tool>`, `call <tool> [JSON|-]`, flat
`tg_<tool> --parameter value`, `mcp` and `skill` forms keep their behavior.
The noun-verb send and moderation commands always return plans, including
when `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` is set. Execution remains available through
`createTelegramToolFacade({ client, execute: true })`; the existing tool-level
CLI and MCP forms execute when `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` is set.
Local mirror reads and plans work offline without credentials.
`GHOSTPAW_TELEGRAM_DB` sets the default database, otherwise
`~/.ghostpaw/telegram.db` is used; `--db` overrides both.

```sh
ghostpaw-telegram mirror chats --db /tmp/telegram-port-example.db --json
ghostpaw-telegram message send 123 'Offline plan' --db /tmp/telegram-port-example.db --json

The empty mirror returns no chats or messages. The send returns an action
descriptor without sending a Telegram message.

readme.markdown:
# TeamOnly MCP server

Deploy the internal apps you build with AI behind your company login, from Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, VS Code, Windsurf or any MCP client.

Say "deploy this on TeamOnly" and your agent puts the app online at `https://<app>.<company>.teamonly.app`. Only people with an email at your company can open it: they sign in with their work Google or Microsoft account, or a code sent to their work email. The app gets its own database, file storage and secrets, and can read and add rows in Google Sheets your team shares with it. Free for 14 days, no card.

Website: [teamonly.dev/mcp](https://teamonly.dev/mcp?ref=github-mcp) · npm: [teamonly](https://www.npmjs.com/package/teamonly) · MCP Registry: `dev.teamonly/teamonly`

## Install

The server is part of the `teamonly` npm package and runs on your computer (deploying reads your project's files). It needs Node.js 20 or newer (22 for `logs`).

**Claude Code**

```sh
claude mcp add teamonly -- npx -y teamonly mcp
```

**Cursor:** [Add to Cursor](https://cursor.com/en/install-mcp?name=teamonly&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoibnB4IiwiYXJncyI6WyIteSIsInRlYW1vbmx5IiwibWNwIl19), or put this in `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and Windsurf take the same:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "teamonly": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "teamonly", "mcp"] }
  }
}
```

**VS Code**

```sh
code --add-mcp '{"name":"teamonly","command":"npx","args":["-y","teamonly","mcp"]}'
```

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `get_app_rules` | The rules for an app that deploys: React + Vite front end, Hono API on one Cloudflare Worker, D1 database, and how to read the signed-in person. The agent reads this before writing code. |
| `init` | Starts an app in an empty folder (or from a template), or adds TeamOnly to an app you already have. |
| `deploy` | Builds the app and puts it online behind your company login. |
| `versions` | Lists the app's versions: when, who deployed each, and which is live. |
| `rollback` | Puts the previous version (or a chosen one) back live in seconds. |
| `pull` | Downloads a deployed app's code into a new folder, so you can change an app whose code isn't on your computer. Owner or admin. |
| `status` | Who is signed in, the plan, and every app with who can open it. |
| `logs` | Watches the live app's requests, `console.log` output and errors for 5 to 60 seconds. |
| `access` | Who can open the app: everyone at the company, or a list of people. |
| `roles` | Roles people have inside the app, like approver or finance. |
| `set_secret` | Saves an API key or password for the app. |
| `sign_in` | Signs in with a work email and the 6-digit code TeamOnly emails. |
| `start_trial` | Starts the free 14-day trial for a company new to TeamOnly. |
| `subscribe` | Returns a payment link for a paid plan. |
| `delete_app` | Deletes the app and its data. Needs the app name to confirm. |

## How sign-in works

There are no API keys to paste. The agent asks for your work email, calls `sign_in`, and asks you for the code from the email. If your company is new to TeamOnly it offers the free trial. The sign-in is saved on your computer in `~/.teamonly`, shared with the `npx teamonly` command line tool.

## Example

> Build a tool where people submit expenses and their manager approves them. Deploy it on TeamOnly so only people at our company can open it.

## Templates

Five ready-made internal tools (expense approval, customer lookup, inventory tracker, request form, ask the docs): [sohelsd/teamonly-templates](https://github.com/sohelsd/teamonly-templates).

## Source

[`src/mcp.ts`](src/mcp.ts) is the server. It ships inside the `teamonly` npm package next to the command line tool it runs: each tool call runs the matching `teamonly` command without a terminal and returns its output, so the MCP tools and the CLI always behave the same. This copy is updated with each release. The [Dockerfile](Dockerfile) runs the published package.

## License

This repository is MIT licensed. The `teamonly` npm package it runs has [its own license](https://www.npmjs.com/package/teamonly?activeTab=code).

## Support

Email hello@teamonly.dev.

# hellohop-mcp

HelloHop is an independent WhatsApp API for developers: send and receive messages, automate groups and communities, and get signed webhooks, from $25 USD per number per month with a free sandbox.

This is the HelloHop MCP server. It lets an MCP client (for example Claude Desktop, Claude Code or Cursor) work with one channel of the public API: read the channel's status, the chats it has observed, recent messages, its groups and communities, and a contact. Sending (a text, media by URL, a poll, a reaction) is **off by default** and available only when you turn it on. Docs: https://hellohop.app/docs/mcp. HelloHop is not affiliated with or endorsed by WhatsApp or Meta.

## Install

Requires Node.js 22 or later. Run it with `npx`, no separate install step:

```sh
npx -y hellohop-mcp
```

Your MCP client starts the server for you once it is configured (see Claude Desktop and Claude Code below). The server reads its settings from the environment variables listed under Environment.

## Tools

| Tool | Request | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `channel_status` | `GET {base}/sessions/{channel}` | `include_safety: true` also reads `GET {base}/sessions/{channel}/safety`. |
| `list_chats` | `GET {base}/sessions/{channel}/chats` | Up to 100 chats from the channel's own log. |
| `read_messages` | `GET {base}/sessions/{channel}/chats/{chat}/messages` | Up to `limit` messages (default 50, at most 500); `next_before` goes back as `before`. `chat` is sent as written, for example `15551234567@s.whatsapp.net`. |
| `list_groups` | `GET {base}/sessions/{channel}/groups` | Asks WhatsApp; do not poll (a throttled number answers 429 `whatsapp_rate_limited`). |
| `get_group` | `GET {base}/sessions/{channel}/groups/{group}` | Asks WhatsApp. |
| `get_community` | `GET {base}/sessions/{channel}/communities/{community}` | Asks WhatsApp. |
| `list_community_subgroups` | `GET {base}/sessions/{channel}/communities/{community}/subgroups` | Asks WhatsApp. |
| `get_contact` | `GET {base}/sessions/{channel}/contacts/{who}` | The channel's stored contact entry; does not ask WhatsApp. |
| `send_text` | `POST {base}/sessions/{channel}/messages/text` | Only when `GATEWAY_ALLOW_SEND=1`. Body `{to, text}`, plus `quoted` if given. |
| `send_media` | `POST {base}/sessions/{channel}/messages/{kind}` | Only when `GATEWAY_ALLOW_SEND=1`. `kind` is `image`, `video`, `audio`, `voice` or `document`; body `{to, url}` plus `caption`, `filename`, `mime_type` if given. The gateway fetches the URL. |
| `send_poll` | `POST {base}/sessions/{channel}/messages/poll` | Only when `GATEWAY_ALLOW_SEND=1`. Body `{to, question, options}` (2 to 12), plus `multiple` if given. |
| `react` | `PUT {base}/sessions/{channel}/messages/{message_id}/reaction` | Only when `GATEWAY_ALLOW_SEND=1`. Body `{emoji}`. |
| `unreact` | `DELETE {base}/sessions/{channel}/messages/{message_id}/reaction` | Only when `GATEWAY_ALLOW_SEND=1`. No body. |
| `delete_message` | `DELETE {base}/sessions/{channel}/messages/{message_id}` | Only when `GATEWAY_ALLOW_SEND=1`. No body. Deletes for everyone a message this number sent, within 48 hours. |

`check_numbers` (always registered; it sends no message) starts a number check from 1 to 50 `numbers` (`POST {base}/sessions/{channel}/number-checks`, plus `refresh` if given), or reads one by `job_id` (`GET` the check, then a page of its rows with `offset`, `limit` and `status`). The check runs in the background on the channel's own connected non-sandbox number, spaced out, with a daily check allowance by number age, so a long list takes hours or days and it cannot be made faster. The number checker is included with every paid number. The account needs at least one active non-sandbox channel, including one covered by a paid, complimentary, promotional or admin grant. Otherwise the service returns 403 `number_checker_requires_paid_number`; a sandbox request from an eligible account returns 403 `number_checker_requires_non_sandbox_channel`. A paused check says why and resumes by itself (only `channel_down` waits for you; `account_suspended` must be resolved); a failed check reports its code and reason in `failure` (`check_failed` for an upstream failure). Read its reason before retrying. Rows carry `phone_e164`, `country`, `jid`, `lid`, `is_business` (present only when true), `verified_name`, `checked_at`, and `cached` with `age_seconds`. A check is a point-in-time answer and can be wrong or out of date; it does not promise delivery.

Not exposed, on purpose: group and community invite links (an agent could paste an open invite into a chat), media download (bytes, not JSON) and webhook configuration.

`get_group` returns the group's participant list, which is your own group data, so it enters the MCP client's context like any other tool result. Use it only with a client you trust with those member identities.

The public API forwards only `limit` (1 to 500) and `before` on the conversation read, so `read_messages` pages with those two and no other query string reaches the API. The other list tools take no paging parameters.

A chat is sent in the URL path without percent-encoding, because the API refuses any path containing `%`. A chat containing anything other than letters, digits and `@ . : _ + -` is refused before a request is made.

Every request sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A successful response is returned as JSON text. An HTTP error is returned as a tool error with `status`, `code` and `error`, plus `retry_after` (and `window`, `resets_at`, `ambiguous`, `id`) when the API sends them. The token is redacted from every string returned, success bodies included. Nothing is retried automatically, and a redirect is refused rather than followed.

## Environment

| Variable | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `GATEWAY_API_URL` | no | Your API base. Defaults to `https://api.hellohop.app/v1`, the public API. Must be https (http is accepted only for localhost). |
| `GATEWAY_API_TOKEN` | yes | A channel key, or an account key for

readme.markdown:
# TracePass MCP Server

A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for
**[TracePass](https://www.tracepass.eu)** — the EU Digital Product
Passport platform. It lets AI assistants (Claude, Cursor, IDE agents)
manage products, Digital Product Passports, economic-operator parties,
and GS1 EPCIS 2.0 supply-chain events.

It speaks the full MCP protocol — **tools**, **resources**, **resource
templates**, and **prompts**.

## Two ways to use it

The same server core ships two ways:

1. **Hosted** — point your MCP client at `https://ai.tracepass.eu/mcp`.
   Nothing to install; always current.
2. **Local (npm)** — run `tracepass-mcp-server` via `npx`. The MCP
   client launches it as a subprocess and speaks MCP over stdio.

## Authentication

The server accepts **either** of TracePass's two v1 auth methods on the
same `Authorization: Bearer …` header — it forwards whatever you send to
the API, which decides. Pick the one that fits how you're connecting:

| | **API key** | **OAuth 2.0** |
|---|---|---|
| Best for | A single user, scripts, server-to-server | AI assistants / apps acting **on a user's behalf** |
| What you send | A static `tp_…` key as a Bearer token | A scoped access token obtained via the OAuth flow |
| Setup | Mint at **Developer → API Keys** | The user clicks **Connect** and approves scopes |
| Scope | All-or-nothing (the whole workspace) | Exactly the scopes the user granted; revocable |
| Works with | Hosted **and** local (npx) | Hosted endpoint only (needs a browser consent step) |

**Which should an AI assistant use?** If your MCP client supports OAuth
(Claude.ai, ChatGPT, and others), prefer **OAuth** — the user authorizes
the connection once on a TracePass consent screen, you never handle a
secret, and access is least-privilege and revocable. If your client only
takes a header/token, use an **API key**.

### OAuth 2.0 (recommended for hosted clients)

No config beyond pointing your client at the hosted endpoint — discovery
is automatic. On the first unauthenticated request the server returns a
`401` whose `WWW-Authenticate` header carries a `resource_metadata` URL
(RFC 9728) pointing at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, which
names the TracePass authorization server. The client runs the standard
**authorization-code flow with PKCE** (`/api/oauth/authorize` →
`/api/oauth/token`), the user approves scopes, and the client stores +
refreshes the token. If you distribute your own client, register an app
under **Developer → OAuth Apps** to get a `client_id`; many hosted
clients self-register via Dynamic Client Registration automatically.

Request only the scopes you need, e.g. `passports:read passports:write
offline_access`. Users manage connected apps (and revoke) under
**Developer → OAuth Apps → Connected Apps**.

### API key

Mint a `tp_…` key under **Developer → API Keys** and send it as a Bearer
token.

**Hosted:**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tracepass": {
      "url": "https://ai.tracepass.eu/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer tp_YOUR_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

**Local (npx / stdio)** — the local subprocess can't do an interactive
OAuth consent step, so it's API-key only, via the `TRACEPASS_API_KEY` env:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tracepass": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "tracepass-mcp-server"],
      "env": {
        "TRACEPASS_API_KEY": "tp_YOUR_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Optional env var: `TRACEPASS_BASE_URL` (defaults to
`https://app.tracepass.eu`) — point the tools at a different
TracePass deployment.

## Tools

The TracePass v1 API operations are grouped into **7 tools**.
Each takes an action enum plus action-specific arguments. The tools are:

- `tracepass_products` - manage the product catalogue (list, get, create, create_batch, update, archive products).
- `tracepass_passports` - manage Digital Product Passports (list, get, compliance check, registry-readiness check, get/set condition flags, create, suspend, archive, get QR, list snapshots, get snapshot), by id or by serial. Passports are identified via GS1 or four additional EN 18219 schemes (iso15459, iec61406, did, doi); battery passports accept only gs1 and iso15459 (Art. 77(3)). **Condition flags** are approved yes/no facts (e.g. battery: `hasBMS`, `rechargeable`, `externalStorageOnly`, `isStationaryBess`) that gate conditional legal duties — setting an approved flag may make additional fields required and block publishing if those fields are empty.
- `tracepass_passport_fields` - update a passport's category-specific data fields, by id or by serial.
- `tracepass_passport_parties` - set or remove a passport's economic-operator parties (manufacturer, importer, etc.).
- `tracepass_epcis` - export, capture, and query a passport's GS1 EPCIS 2.0 supply-chain events.
- `tracepass_templates` - list and get the DPP category field schemas, each field traced to the EU instrument that mandates it.
- `tracepass_scope` - check whether a product type needs a Digital Product Passport (check), read the company's catalogue-wide scope report (catalogue_report), and trigger or poll a catalogue refresh run (catalogue_run, catalogue_run_status).

Each tool's full action set:

| Tool | Actions |
|------|---------|
| `tracepass_products` | `list`, `get`, `create`, `create_batch`, `update`, `archive` |
| `tracepass_passports` | `list`, `get`, `get_by_serial`, `compliance`, `registry_readiness`, `get_condition_flags`, `get_condition_flags_by_serial`, `set_condition_flags`, `set_condition_flags_by_serial`, `capture_measurements`, `capture_measurements_by_serial`, `list_measurements`, `list_measurements_by_serial`, `latest_measurements`, `latest_measurements_by_serial`, `create`, `suspend`, `suspend_by_serial`, `archive`, `archive_by_serial`, `get_qr`, `get_qr_by_serial`, `list_snapshots`, `get_snapshot` |
| `tracepass_passport_fields` | `update`, `update_by_serial` |
| `tracepass_passport_parties` | `set`, `remove` |
| `tracepass_epcis` | `export`, `export_by

…

# Keeploop plugins for Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and Grok Bot

[Keeploop](https://keeploop.app) is the personal context layer for your AI: a Mac menu bar app
that lets the AI apps you already use read your Mail, Messages, Calendar, Notes and Slack, right
on your Mac. Your data stays on your Mac until an AI app you connect asks for it, and you decide what each AI can see and do.

This repository is the plugin marketplace for Keeploop. It has two plugins:

- `keeploop` runs on your Mac, for Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Grok Build. Local use is free.
- `keeploop-remote` is for Grok Bot. It connects through Keeploop's hosted connector at
  `https://mcp.keeploop.app/mcp` and is hidden in the Cursor editor. Needs Keeploop Pro or its
  free trial for remote use; local use is free.

The local plugin adds:

- **The Keeploop tools** (mail, threads and attachments, calendar and free time, messages, notes,
  contacts and Slack, monitors that wake the agent when a reply lands, drafts in your voice).
  They come from the Keeploop app through a small launcher; nothing in this repository reads
  your data itself.
- **The `/keep-` commands**:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/keep-today` | Today's schedule, the replies you owe, and today's monitor hits |
| `/keep-free [length and range]` | Open slots on your calendar, for example `/keep-free 30m this week` |
| `/keep-brief [account or category]` | Unread mail, what needs a reply, and today's monitor hits |
| `/keep-reply` | Threads where someone is waiting on you, with a suggested next step each |
| `/keep-thread <subject or mail id>` | Summarize a whole conversation: decisions and open questions |
| `/keep-draft <mail id> <what to say>` | Draft a threaded reply that sounds like you. Saves a draft only |
| `/keep-find <description>` | Find a file someone sent you by describing it |
| `/keep-waiting` | Mail you sent that nobody has answered yet, oldest first |
| `/keep-settings [what to change]` | See what the AI can do, or propose a change for approval on your Mac |
| `/keep-help` | List the commands |

## Requirements

- An Apple Silicon Mac on macOS 26 or later.
- **The Keeploop app**, installed in `/Applications` (or `~/Applications`) and opened once.
  Get it at [keeploop.app](https://keeploop.app). Without the app the plugin's server stops with
  "Keeploop is not installed on this Mac. Install Keeploop from https://keeploop.app ...".

If you already have Keeploop, the easiest route is Keeploop > Settings > Connect, which installs
this plugin for you.

## Install

### Claude Code

```
/plugin marketplace add keeploopapp/claude-plugin
/plugin install keeploop@keeploop
```

Or from a terminal:

```
claude plugin marketplace add keeploopapp/claude-plugin
claude plugin install keeploop@keeploop
```

Restart Claude Code, then type `/keep-help`.

### Cursor

Install **Keeploop** from the Cursor Marketplace in Customize, or add this repository as a
plugin source. The plugin reports itself to Keeploop as Cursor, so Keeploop's per-app rules apply.

### Grok Build

Grok Build reads Claude Code marketplaces, so the Claude Code commands above are all it needs.

### Gemini CLI

```
gemini extensions install https://github.com/keeploopapp/claude-plugin
```

The extension runs the same local launcher as the plugin (`gemini-extension.json` and
`GEMINI.md` at the repository root). Restart Gemini CLI, then ask "what needs my reply today?".

### Grok Bot

In Grok Bot, open Connect apps, find Keeploop, and add it (this is the `keeploop-remote`
plugin). Sign in to Keeploop in the window that opens, then approve Grok Bot on your Mac.

### Web and phone AI apps (Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Poke and others)

The plugin is for AI apps on your Mac. To use Keeploop from claude.ai, ChatGPT (including dots),
grok.com, Poke or any app that can add a custom MCP connector, add this one URL:

```
https://mcp.keeploop.app/mcp
```

Sign in to Keeploop in the window the app opens, then approve the app on your Mac. The same URL
works for every user; it reaches your Mac only after you approve it there. Remote apps are Read
only until you allow more in Keeploop. Web and phone AI apps need Keeploop Pro or its free trial;
the plugin on your Mac works on Free. Step by step for each app:
<https://keeploop.app/your-ai-apps>.

## What the plugin contains

- `plugins/keeploop/server/keeploop-mcp`: a shell launcher that runs the connector inside
  `Keeploop.app` (its signed `Contents/MacOS/keeploop-mcp`). The Keeploop app checks that
  signature and applies your permissions to every call.
- `plugins/keeploop/skills/keep-*`: the commands, as plain Markdown.
- `plugins/keeploop/hooks/hooks.json`: a Claude Code `SessionStart` hook that tells Keeploop
  which session is running, so a monitor can wake the session that asked for it. It does nothing
  when the app is not installed.
- `plugins/keeploop-remote/`: the Grok Bot plugin. Its `mcp.json` holds only the address
  `https://mcp.keeploop.app/mcp`, and it has the same `skills/keep-*`. It runs nothing on your
  computer.
- `.claude-plugin/` and `.cursor-plugin/`: the marketplace manifests.

Nothing in the local plugin makes a network connection, downloads code or installs packages. The
launcher only runs the Keeploop app's connector on your Mac, and that talks to the Keeploop app
over a local connection, so there is no Keeploop server in the path. If you also use Keeploop from
a web or phone AI app, that is a separate connection: your data stays on your Mac, and Keeploop's
connection service passes requests to your Mac and results back. It never stores them. What the
app itself can send, and only when you turn it on, is listed in the
[privacy policy](https://keeploop.app/privacy).

## Privacy Policy

The full policy is at <https://keeploop.app/privacy>. In short:

- **Collection:** this plugin collects nothing. It starts the Keeploop app's connector, which
  reads the Apple Mail data (and any other source you turn on) alre

{
  "mcpServers": {

```

pip install hongkong-company-mcp
hongkong-company-mcp

# Runtime

The SDKs, CLI, MCP server and agent integrations for
[Runtime](https://withruntime.com): sandboxes for AI agents. Each sandbox is a
Firecracker microVM with its own Linux kernel, started from one call.

```bash
npm install withruntime   # TypeScript SDK, the `runtime` CLI and the MCP server
pip install withruntime   # Python SDK, sync and async
```

```ts
import { Sandbox } from "withruntime";

await using sbx = await Sandbox.create();
const result = await sbx.exec("python3 -c 'print(6 * 7)'");
console.log(result.exitCode, result.stdout);
```

```python
from withruntime import Sandbox

with Sandbox.create() as sbx:
    result = sbx.exec("python3 -c 'print(6 * 7)'")
    print(result.exit_code, result.stdout)
```

The client reads `RUNTIME_API_KEY`, or the connection `npx withruntime login`
saved on this machine. A new account starts on a free trial with no card. The
[quickstart](https://withruntime.com/docs/start) takes it from there.

## MCP server

The MCP server gives an agent every Runtime product as tools. It needs Node
22.12 or later and no API key. Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user runtime -- npx -y withruntime mcp
```

Cursor, Cline, Windsurf and other clients that take this shape:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "runtime": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "withruntime", "mcp"] }
  }
}
```

The first time, the server offers one tool, `runtime_connect`. The agent calls
it and shows a link and a code; approve **Connect agent** in the browser, and
every Runtime tool appears. A machine already connected with
`npx withruntime login` skips this step. In CI, set `RUNTIME_API_KEY` instead.

Clients that connect over HTTP use `https://api.withruntime.com/mcp` (MCP
Streamable HTTP) and sign in through the browser. The server is in the
official MCP Registry as `com.withruntime/runtime`. Details:
[withruntime.com/docs/mcp](https://withruntime.com/docs/mcp).

## What is here

| Path                                                                              | What it is                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `packages/cloud-sdk`                                                              | The TypeScript SDK, the `runtime` CLI and the MCP server: [`withruntime`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/withruntime) on npm |
| `sdks/python`                                                                     | The Python SDK: [`withruntime`](https://pypi.org/project/withruntime/) on PyPI                                              |
| `sdks/python/integrations/langchain-withruntime`                                  | LangChain and Deep Agents sandbox backend                                                                                   |
| `sdks/go`, `sdks/java`, `sdks/ruby`                                               | The Go, Java and Ruby SDKs                                                                                                  |
| `integrations/openai-agents`, `pydantic-ai`, `google-adk`, `smolagents`           | OpenAI Agents SDK, Pydantic AI, Google ADK and smolagents integrations, each `<name>-withruntime` on PyPI                   |
| `integrations/claude-code`, `codex`, `cursor`, `gemini-cli`, `vscode`, `windsurf` | Skills, rules and MCP settings for coding agents                                                                            |
| `packages/cloud-guide/docs`                                                       | The guides served at [withruntime.com/docs](https://withruntime.com/docs), which the SDK tests check samples against        |

## Documentation

- [Start](https://withruntime.com/docs/start)
- [TypeScript](https://withruntime.com/docs/javascript) and [Python](https://withruntime.com/docs/python)
- [CLI](https://withruntime.com/docs/cli) and [MCP](https://withruntime.com/docs/mcp)
- [Frameworks](https://withruntime.com/docs/frameworks), and moving from
  [E2B](https://withruntime.com/docs/e2b-alternative) or
  [Daytona](https://withruntime.com/docs/daytona-alternative)
- [Pricing](https://withruntime.com/docs/pricing)

## How Runtime compares

Pages that answer what people ask when choosing a sandbox, each with the
providers' published rates and the date they were read:

- [Best sandbox for AI agents](https://withruntime.com/compare/best-sandbox-for-ai-agents)
- Alternatives to [E2B](https://withruntime.com/compare/e2b-alternatives),
  [Daytona](https://withruntime.com/compare/daytona-alternatives),
  [Modal](https://withruntime.com/compare/modal-alternatives) and
  [Vercel Sandbox](https://withruntime.com/compare/vercel-sandbox-alternatives)
- [E2B vs Daytona](https://withruntime.com/compare/e2b-vs-daytona), and
  [every comparison](https://withruntime.com/compare)
- [The agent sandbox price index](https://withruntime.com/pricing/agent-sandbox-price-index):
  every provider's rates, also as CSV and JSON
- [Sandbox cost calculator](https://withruntime.com/calculators/sandbox-cost-calculator)
  and [Runtime's pricing](https://withruntime.com/pricing)

## Tests

`bun test` in `packages/cloud-sdk` and `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`
in `sdks/python` run here as they are. The suites that start Runtime's API
server in-process, including all of the Go, Java and Ruby tests, run in
Runtime's main repository before each release.

## Contributing

Each release copies the SDKs here from Runtime's main repository, so each
commit here is one copy, named after the versions in its source; a copy made
before those versions reach npm and PyPI says so. Issues are welcome. A pull request is
reviewed here and carried into the next release with its author credited.

readme.markdown:
# Nido

**Real virtual machines for AI agents. One local engine, three ways to drive it: CLI, TUI and MCP.**

Give an agent a machine it can provision, use and delete. Nido runs QEMU locally,
clones cached images with copy-on-write disks, and exposes the same VM lifecycle
to your terminal and your MCP client. Each VM has its own guest kernel.

**Hatch your agents. Let them fly.** Retro shell, practical machinery.

[Get started](#press-start) · [Connect an agent](#connect-your-agent) · [Documentation](docs/README.md) · [Wiki](https://github.com/Josepavese/nido/wiki)

## Why Nido?

| You want to... | Nido gives you... |
| --- | --- |
| Test code away from your host | Disposable QEMU VMs with SSH access and cloud-init provisioning |
| Let an agent manage its own environment | A built-in stdio MCP server with compact tools, read-only resources and opt-in event subscriptions |
| Reuse an expensive setup | Templates and QCOW2 linked clones, with one shared base and a writable disk per VM |
| Switch between automation and hands-on work | Structured CLI JSON, shell completion and an interactive terminal dashboard |
| Keep multiple dashboards and agents in sync | [Shared local events](docs/events.md), live TUI updates and selective MCP notifications |
| Choose the right starting point | An automatically refreshed cloud-image catalog, local templates and buildable blueprints |

AMD64 and ARM64 host/guest selection, requirements and data-preserving upgrades:
[Architecture guide](docs/architectures.md). Omitted architecture selects native; use `--arch`
on CLI, `arch` on MCP, or the TUI **Arch** selector for an explicit guest ISA.

## Press start

QEMU is required to run VMs. Nido supports Linux, macOS and Windows hosts;
hardware acceleration depends on what the host actually exposes. Start with
`nido doctor`. See [installation and host requirements](installers/README.md).

### Install

**Linux / macOS**

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/Josepavese/nido/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows PowerShell**

```powershell
irm https://github.com/Josepavese/nido/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex
```

Open a new terminal, then check `nido version` and `nido doctor`. The quick
installers check prerequisites and offer QEMU setup where supported.

Prefer a package manager? npm works on Linux, macOS and Windows:

```bash
npm install -g nido-mcp                # Linux / macOS / Windows launcher
brew install Josepavese/nido/nido       # macOS / Linux
go install github.com/Josepavese/nido/v4/cmd/nido@latest
```

```powershell
scoop bucket add nido https://github.com/Josepavese/scoop-nido
scoop install nido
```

**Container** (Docker/Podman, bundles QEMU; needs a KVM-capable host):

```bash
docker run -i --rm --device /dev/kvm \
  --group-add "$(stat -c %g /dev/kvm)" \
  -v nido-home:/home/nido/.nido \
  ghcr.io/josepavese/nido mcp
```

Images are rebuilt on every release at `ghcr.io/josepavese/nido` (`:{version}`,
`:{minor}`, `:latest`) and speak MCP on stdio; pass `--group-add` so the
non-root user can open `/dev/kvm`.

**Debian / Ubuntu (APT) and Fedora / RHEL (DNF)** repositories are rebuilt on
every release and served from GitHub Pages:

```bash
# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings
sudo curl -fsSL https://josepavese.github.io/nido/nido-archive-keyring.asc -o /etc/apt/keyrings/nido.asc
echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/nido.asc] https://josepavese.github.io/nido/apt/ stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nido.list
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install nido

# Fedora / RHEL
sudo curl -fsSL https://josepavese.github.io/nido/rpm/nido.repo -o /etc/yum.repos.d/nido.repo
sudo dnf install nido
```

Install QEMU first (`qemu-system-x86 qemu-utils` / `qemu-kvm qemu-img`), then run
`nido doctor`. Both repositories are GPG-signed by the Nido package archive key
(`DBB87CB63A94ABA50B33C7B919C6A95C9D280B64`); see
[the installers guide](installers/README.md#apt-debian--ubuntu).

**Nix**: `nix run github:Josepavese/nido` builds the current source and brings
its own QEMU; see [the installers guide](installers/README.md#nix-flake-from-source).

**WinGet**: `Josepavese.Nido` is awaiting Microsoft review. See
[availability and commands](installers/README.md#winget-windows).

For MCP clients, use `npx -y nido-mcp mcp`, discover
`io.github.Josepavese/nido` in the **Official MCP Registry**, browse the **Glama**
directory for local installation instructions, or import the **MCPB bundle**.
[MCP catalogs and client installation](installers/README.md#mcp-catalogs-and-client-installation).

[All install options](installers/README.md) · [Distribution channel status](docs/DISTRIBUTION.md)

### Hatch your first VM

```bash
nido images update
nido images info ubuntu:lts
nido images pull ubuntu:lts
nido spawn agent-lab --image ubuntu:lts --memory 2048 --cpus 2
nido info agent-lab --json

# Once the guest has finished booting and SSH is ready:
nido ssh agent-lab
```

The first pull downloads the base image. Later VMs can reuse it. `ubuntu:lts`
follows the catalog's supported LTS selection; use a numbered tag from
`nido images list` when you need a specific OS release. Guest boot and cloud-init
take additional time; creating the overlay is only one part of startup.

When you have saved the work you need, shut down inside the guest and remove
**only your disposable VM**:

```bash
nido ssh agent-lab sudo poweroff
# After shutdown, confirm its state:
nido info agent-lab
nido delete agent-lab
```

`nido stop` terminates the managed QEMU process and waits for exit. Use guest
poweroff for a clean OS shutdown. VM data persists until you delete it.

[Provisioning, ports, templates and cleanup](docs/usage.md)

Watch core changes in another terminal with `nido events` or `nido events --json`.
TUI sessions update from the shared stream; agents explicitly subscribe only to
the resources they need. See [event delivery and mute controls](docs/events.md).

# Corsair agent plugins

Plugins that install [Corsair](https://corsair.dev) into AI clients. One tree serves Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code, GitHub Copilot, Grok Bot, Gemini CLI and `npx skills`.

| Plugin | For | Contains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`corsair`](plugins/corsair) | People using their connected apps from an agent | The Corsair MCP server and four skills for using it |
| [`corsair-sdk`](plugins/corsair-sdk) | Developers adding the Corsair SDK to an app | The `corsair` setup skill and the Corsair docs MCP server |

## Install

```bash
# Claude Code
claude plugin marketplace add corsairdev/agent-plugins
claude plugin install corsair@corsair      # or corsair-sdk@corsair

# Codex
codex plugin marketplace add corsairdev/agent-plugins
codex plugin add corsair@corsair

# Gemini CLI (installs the Corsair MCP server)
gemini extensions install https://github.com/corsairdev/agent-plugins

# Any agent that reads Agent Skills
npx skills add corsairdev/agent-plugins
```

Cursor installs from the [Cursor Marketplace](https://cursor.com/marketplace) once the plugins are listed.

## Support

Email [primary@corsair.dev](mailto:primary@corsair.dev).

## Layout

```
.claude-plugin/marketplace.json     Claude Code marketplace
.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json     Cursor marketplace
.agents/plugins/marketplace.json    Codex marketplace
gemini-extension.json               Gemini CLI, which installs only from a repo root
plugins/<name>/
  plugin.json                       Agent Plugins 1.0 manifest: Cursor, Codex and ChatGPT, VS Code, Copilot, Grok Bot
                                    (extensions.com.openai holds the Codex and ChatGPT listing copy)
  .claude-plugin/plugin.json        Claude Code manifest, pointing mcpServers at ./mcp.json
  mcp.json                          the plugin's MCP server, read by every client above
  skills/<skill>/SKILL.md           Agent Skills, read by every client above
  assets/icon.png                   512×512 (the directory takes 512–2048 px)
plugins/corsair/server.json         MCP Registry entry, dev.corsair/mcp
sync/corsair-skill.json             which corsairdev/corsair commit the corsair skill came from
```

Keep every path inside its plugin folder. Claude Code rejects `..` paths, and Agent Plugins clients skip symlinks that leave the plugin.

The Corsair MCP URL can't be shared through one file, so it's written in `plugins/corsair/mcp.json`, `plugins/corsair/server.json` and `gemini-extension.json`. `scripts/check.mjs` fails if they differ.

## The corsair skill comes from corsairdev/corsair

The SDK setup skill lives next to the SDK, in [`corsairdev/corsair/skills/corsair`](https://github.com/corsairdev/corsair/tree/main/skills/corsair). That way an SDK change and its skill change land in one PR, and `npx skills add corsairdev/corsair` keeps working. This repo carries a copy in `plugins/corsair-sdk/skills/corsair`. **Edit the skill there, never here.** A sync would overwrite the change.

`.github/workflows/sync-corsair-skill.yml` keeps the copy current:

1. Every day, and on demand from the Actions tab, it checks out `skills/corsair` from corsairdev/corsair `main`. The repo is public, so this needs no token.
2. If the files differ from the copy, it replaces the copy, bumps the corsair-sdk plugin's patch version in both manifests, and records the source commit in `sync/corsair-skill.json`.
3. It runs `scripts/check.mjs`, then opens or updates one PR from the `sync/corsair-skill` branch. Merging that PR releases the update.

The PR step needs **Settings → Actions → General → "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests"** turned on.

To sync right away instead of waiting a day, add this to corsairdev/corsair. It needs a token with Contents write on this repo, saved as `AGENT_PLUGINS_TOKEN`.

```yaml
# corsairdev/corsair: .github/workflows/notify-agent-plugins.yml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: [skills/corsair/**]
jobs:
  notify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: gh api repos/corsairdev/agent-plugins/dispatches -f event_type=corsair-skill-changed
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.AGENT_PLUGINS_TOKEN }}
```

To sync by hand from a local clone of corsairdev/corsair:

```bash
node scripts/sync-corsair-skill.mjs --from ../corsair/skills/corsair --commit "$(git -C ../corsair rev-parse HEAD)"
```

## Before you push

```bash
node scripts/check.mjs                 # cross-file checks
claude plugin validate .               # marketplace
claude plugin validate plugins/corsair
claude plugin validate plugins/corsair-sdk
```

CI (`.github/workflows/check.yml`) runs these and validates every `plugin.json` and `mcp.json` against the Agent Plugins schemas.

To release a change to a plugin, bump `version` in both of its manifests. For `corsair`, also bump it in `server.json` and `gemini-extension.json`. Clients decide whether to update by version.

[Demo](https://demo.recued.com) | [Documentation](https://recued.com/docs) | [Marketplace](https://recued.com/packs)

# Recued

Recued is a server you run yourself. It sits between AI and your accounts.
Your mail, calendar, files, and CRM records stay on a machine you control.

It works two ways. An AI agent you already use gets in over MCP, through a
contract that lists exactly what it may do. Or Recued does the job itself: you
ask in its chat, or a recipe runs on a schedule or when something happens.
Either way, every action passes one gate. By default, anything that writes or
deletes waits for your yes.

Recued does not replace the AI you use. Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, or a local
model still does the thinking. Recued is where that thinking meets your data
and your accounts, on terms you set. That is the space it holds, between you
and AI.

This repo holds the complete self-hosted **server** and the **webclient**. It
also holds the workspace packages they are built from.

## Recued as a gateway

- **One door per agent.** You make a contract for each AI agent: Claude,
  Codex, OpenClaw, or your own. It lists the tools that agent may use. The
  agent connects over MCP with the contract's key.
- **One gate for every call.** The gate checks the contract first, and asks
  you when a call writes. It logs the call, and only then runs it. An unknown
  caller is refused. One switch pauses everything.
- **Your yes for risky actions.** By default, anything that writes, sends,
  or deletes waits for you. Approve one, a batch, or a whole session.
- **Keys stay home.** Your account keys stay on your server, or with a
  broker you pick. Recued's cloud never holds them. An agent gets the tools a
  contract grants, never the keys behind them.

## Recued does jobs on its own

- **Ask it.** Recued has its own chat: in the web app, by email, and in Slack
  and Telegram. It answers from your saved records first. A lookup like "What
  is Maya's email?" needs no AI at all. When a question does need AI, Recued
  swaps out the personal details and brings the relevant facts along, so the
  model has them before it starts. [Replay Maya's questions](https://demo.recued.com/app/?example=maya-answers)
  in the demo.
- **Let it run.** A recipe is a job Recued runs by itself, on a schedule or
  when something happens. Mail about a parcel, a bill, a booking, an order, or
  a lead can start one. So can a new record. It calls a model only where
  judgment is really needed.
- **Same gate.** Its own jobs pass the same gate as an outside agent. By
  default, a step that writes or deletes still waits for your yes.

## What Recued is not

- Not a coding agent.
- Not a general chat app. Its chat is for your own records and accounts.
- Not a runner for `SKILL.md` files. Recued cannot run them.
- Not built for open-ended questions that take many steps over a long stretch.

## What Recued is

- One server, one owner. Each Recued server stands on its own. It stands for
  one person or one organization (a company, a team, a family, and so on).
- It connects to any provider and any API. It makes your command-line tools
  reachable too.
- Any AI agent can connect over MCP: Codex, Claude, OpenClaw and the other
  Claw variants, or your own.
- It keeps a local copy of your mail, contacts, and CRM records. So reads are
  fast.
- Before an AI sees any of your warehouse data, it tries to swap out the
  personal bits. Those are names, emails, organizations, phone numbers, and
  addresses. Safe stand-ins go in their place. This is the PII alias. It does its best, it is safe, and it can be undone. The stand-ins still show
  the region (city, state, country). They still show which people and sites
  belong to the same organization. So the model can reason over that.
- It encrypts your data at rest (while it sits on disk). The 24-word recovery
  key is the only way back in.
- No third party sits in the middle. Nobody takes a cut of your money. Nobody
  pipes your data.
- It works with any AI provider, hosted or local. You get two default slots,
  plus an unlimited pool of extra provider slots it rotates through.
- Every risky action can be gated. Then it runs only after you say yes.
- Free to run. No feature is locked away.

## Install

One command. It fetches the signed binary for your platform. That is the
program file, stamped so you know it is really from Recued. It checks it
against the release key. It puts `recued` on your PATH, so you can run it from
anywhere. And it sets it to start when you log in.

```sh
# Linux and macOS
curl -fsSL https://recued.com/install.sh | sh
```

```powershell
# Windows — in PowerShell
irm https://recued.com/install.ps1 | iex
```

The installer starts the server too. So when it is done, the server is
already running. To pair a browser, run `recued pair`. It prints a pairing
code and a link to the webclient. Open the link and type in the code. If
`recued` is not found in that terminal, open a new one.

Do not want it to start at login? Put `RECUED_AUTOSTART=0` just before `sh`:
`curl -fsSL https://recued.com/install.sh | RECUED_AUTOSTART=0 sh`. Put it
before `curl`, and only `curl` sees it. In PowerShell, run
`$env:RECUED_AUTOSTART=0` on its own line first. Then start it yourself with
`recued serve`. It prints the pairing code. The install location, the release
channel, and the rest are in [INSTALL.md](./INSTALL.md#options).

A **headless Linux** box is one with no screen or desktop. There, starting at
boot needs root, the admin account. Run the installer with `sudo`, and pair
with `sudo` too. The installer prints the exact command. Here is why. Without a desktop keyring, there is only one way to
seal the key file to the machine. That way reads a host key only root can
read. A Linux desktop session installs a user unit and needs no root.

## Pack

A pack is a JSON file. It says how to connect to any resource: a CLI, a SaaS,
a REST API, or MCP. You can set permissions for each operation. By default,
every write

env.description: Shared secret clients must present as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. Required before exposing the server beyond loopback.

# Anteater MCP Release **1.0.0-beta.3** returns structured error codes from every tool and from the REST facade, so clients can tell a rejected API key from a rate limit or an upstream outage. See [Changes](#changes) for the REST response change. An MCP server that lets Claude and ChatGPT help you pick classes at UC Irvine. It wraps [Anteater API](https://icssc.link/about-anteaterapi) — UCI's course catalogue, the live schedule of classes (WebSoc), historical grade distributions, enrollment history, prerequisite trees, AP credit, degree requirements and supplementary RMP ratings — and exposes them as **20 tools, 6 guided prompts and 4 reference resources**, shaped around the questions students actually ask. **Zero runtime dependencies.** Run the source with Node 24 LTS, or download a standalone Linux, macOS or Windows executable that already contains the same Node runtime. ``` "Find me a GE-2 for Fall that ends before 5pm and still has seats, ranked by how well people do." Course Title Units GPA A% n SeatsOpen Example meeting ------------ ------------------- ----- ---- --- ---- --------- --------------------------- BIO SCI 17 EVO PSYCHOLOGY 4 3.80 88% 2410 2 TuTh 15:30-16:50 @ SH 134 UNI STU H30A ANALYSIS HEALTH LIT 4 3.77 84% 864 15 TuTh 12:30-13:50 @ ALP 1600 LPS 31 INTRO INDUCT LOGIC 4 3.61 80% 2108 11 TuTh 14:00-15:20 @ EH 1200 ``` --- ## Quickstart ```bash git clone https://github.com/KKazuhaK/Anteater-MCP.git cd anteater-mcp node --version # Node 24 LTS node anteater-mcp.mjs --list-tools # confirm it runs ``` Then add it to your client — **[Claude Desktop](#claude-desktop)**, **[Claude Code](#claude-code)**, **[ChatGPT](#chatgpt)**, or **[any other MCP client](#any-other-mcp-client)**. Nothing else is required. An [API key](#api-key) is optional but recommended. --- ## Installing ### Standalone binary Each [GitHub Release](https://github.com/KKazuhaK/Anteater-MCP/releases) contains native archives for Linux, macOS and Windows on amd64 and arm64, plus `SHA256SUMS.txt`. These do not require Node.js: ```bash # After downloading and extracting the archive for your platform: ./anteater-mcp --version ./anteater-mcp --list-tools ``` In an MCP client configuration, use the absolute path to `anteater-mcp` (or `anteater-mcp.exe`) as `command` and omit the `args` array. macOS archives are ad-hoc signed; public Developer ID signing and notarization are not yet configured. ### Docker The published image supports Linux amd64 and arm64. Docker Desktop on macOS and Windows runs the same Linux image: ```bash cp .env.example .env # Set ANTEATER_MCP_TOKEN in .env, then: docker compose up -d curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8787/health ``` The Compose service is non-root, read-only, capability-free and bound to loopback by default. See [DEPLOY.md](DEPLOY.md) before placing it behind public HTTPS. ### Claude Desktop Open the config file: | OS | Path | |---|---| | macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` | | Windows | `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` | | Linux | `~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` | Add an `anteater` entry. **The path must be absolute** — Claude Desktop does not run the server from your project directory: ```json { "mcpServers": { "anteater": { "command": "node", "args": ["/absolute/path/to/anteater-mcp/anteater-mcp.mjs"] } } } ``` With an API key: ```json { "mcpServers": { "anteater": { "command": "node", "args": ["/absolute/path/to/anteater-mcp/anteater-mcp.mjs"], "env": { "ANTEATER_API_KEY": "your-secret-key" } } } } ``` Restart Claude Desktop completely (quit, don't just close the window). You should see 20 anteater tools, and the 6 prompts appear as slash commands. `claude_desktop_config.example.json` in this repo is the same thing, ready to copy. ### Claude Code ```bash claude mcp add anteater -- node /absolute/path/to/anteater-mcp/anteater-mcp.mjs ``` With a key: ```bash claude mcp add anteater -e ANTEATER_API_KEY=your-secret-key -- node /absolute/path/to/anteater-mcp/anteater-mcp.mjs ``` Verify with `claude mcp list`. ### ChatGPT Two routes. **The first needs no server.**
A. Custom GPT with Actions — no hosting required 1. ChatGPT → **Explore GPTs → Create → Configure → Create new action** 2. Paste the contents of [`gpt-actions-openapi.json`](gpt-actions-openapi.json) into the Schema box 3. **Authentication** — two workable choices: - **None.** Anteater API is readable anonymously. Simplest, but you share a global hourly quota with every other anonymous caller and will hit 429s. - **API Key → Auth Type: Bearer**, with your Anteater API key. ChatGPT then sends `Authorization: Bearer ` on every call and you get your own quota. ⚠️ The key is stored with the GPT, so **anyone you share the GPT with uses your key**. Fine for a private GPT; do not publish one with your key in it. 4. Paste [`gpt-instructions.md`](gpt-instructions.md) into the Instructions box The GPT calls `anteaterapi.com` directly. Twelve operations cover courses, WebSoc, grades, enrollment history and degree requirements. **The trade-off:** the GPT receives raw JSON. WebSoc responses nest four levels deep (`schools > departments > courses > sections`), so broad queries get truncated by Actions — the supplied instructions tell it to always narrow. Prerequisite evaluation and conflict detection are *not* available; the model has to reason them out itself.
B. Host the MCP server — full functionality ChatGPT's Developer Mode connector needs a public HTTPS MCP endpoint: ```bash node anteater-mcp.mjs --http --port 8787 # binds 127.0.0.1 only — do not add --host # in another terminal ngrok http 8787 # or: cloudflared tu …

name: mcp.film directory
description: Search the curated directory of MCP servers for AI filmmaking and plan a full production stack.

readme.markdown:
# mcp.film

**The MCP directory for AI filmmaking.** Every tool your agent needs to make a
film — video models, voices, scores, edit bays, finishing suites, and the pipes
to ship it. Curated, verified, agent-first, and re-checked daily.

🎬 **Live site:** [mcp.film](https://mcp.film) ·
🤖 **For agents:** [`/llms.txt`](https://mcp.film/llms.txt) · [`/api/registry.json`](https://mcp.film/api/registry.json) ·
`claude mcp add mcp-film -- npx -y mcp-film`

---

## What this is

A directory of verified Model Context Protocol servers across the full film
pipeline — from screenplay breakdown to YouTube upload — each entry annotated
with exact install commands, auth requirements, pricing, sample tools, and the
caveats that actually bite ("requires Resolve *Studio*", "Suno has no official
API", "uploads cost 1,600 quota units").

It is built **agents-first**:

| Surface | URL |
| --- | --- |
| llms.txt index ([spec](https://llmstxt.org)) | `/llms.txt` · `/llms-full.txt` |
| Full structured registry | `/api/registry.json` (+ `.min.json`) |
| MCP Registry-compatible API | `/v0.1/servers` · `/api/mcp-registry.json` |
| Catalog freshness / ops pulse | `/api/pulse.json` · `/pulse.md` |
| Production playbooks | `/api/playbooks.json` · `/playbooks.md` |
| Agent recommendations | `/api/recommendations.json` · `/recommendations.md` |
| Capability index | `/api/capabilities.json` · `/capabilities/{tag}.md` |
| Client setup profiles | `/clients/` · `/clients.md` · `/api/client-profiles.json` |
| One server, JSON / markdown | `/api/mcps/{slug}.json` · `/mcps/{slug}.md` |
| Pipeline guide | `/stack/` · `/stack.md` |
| New servers feed | `/feed.xml` |
| The directory **as an MCP server** | `npx -y mcp-film` (`packages/mcp-server/`) |
| JSON-LD (`SoftwareApplication`, `ItemList`) | embedded in every page, server-rendered |

## How it runs itself

```
              ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
              │                data/ (the product)             │
              └───────▲────────────────────────────────────────┘
   daily: re-verify   │
   links, hunt new    │
   servers            │
        ┌─────────────┴──┐
        │ curator.yml    │
        │ (Claude agent) │
        └─────────────┬──┘
                      │
                      ▼
              PRs labeled `auto-data` ──► auto-merge.yml
              (merges ONLY if every changed file is in data/
               and validation passes) ──► deploy.yml ──► Cloudflare Pages
                                                     └──► GitHub Pages fallback
```

Feedback typed on a server page is captured as a PostHog event for a
maintainer to read; nothing is folded into the rankings automatically. Rankings
are editorial: official status, maintenance recency, hosted availability, and
the caveats each entry carries. Every change is a commit — the entire editorial
history is auditable.

Agent-readable traffic is measured at the edge when deployed on Cloudflare
Pages: the build emits a `_worker.js` that logs `mcpfilm_edge_request` events
for `/llms.txt`, markdown, JSON API routes, feeds, and MCP discovery. Browser
pageviews still use the lightweight PostHog client event. See
[`docs/ANALYTICS.md`](docs/ANALYTICS.md).

The live catalog pulse is published at [`/api/pulse.json`](https://mcp.film/api/pulse.json)
and [`/pulse.md`](https://mcp.film/pulse.md): newest additions, stale
verification queue, category coverage, and machine-surface links for agents.
Client setup profiles live at [`/api/client-profiles.json`](https://mcp.film/api/client-profiles.json)
and [`/clients.md`](https://mcp.film/clients.md): conservative setup guidance
for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, hosted remote clients, and the
directory's own meta-MCP server.

Production playbooks live at [`/api/playbooks.json`](https://mcp.film/api/playbooks.json)
and [`/playbooks.md`](https://mcp.film/playbooks.md): concrete stack recipes
with setup order, auth gates, failure modes, and earned Martini handoffs for
commercial sprints, local edit bays, character series, archive cutdowns, and
open-source labs.

## Develop locally

Zero dependencies — Node 20+ is the whole toolchain:

```sh
node build.mjs --validate-only   # check the data
node build.mjs                   # build → dist/ (HTML, APIs, feeds, agent surfaces)
node scripts/serve.mjs           # preview at http://localhost:4173
```

Repo map: `data/` is the content, `build.mjs` + `src/` the generator,
`packages/mcp-server/` the `npx mcp-film` meta-server, `.github/workflows/`
the autonomy loop, [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) the operating manual (for agents
and humans alike), [`docs/SETUP.md`](docs/SETUP.md) the one-time launch
checklist, and [`docs/AGENT_STRATEGY.md`](docs/AGENT_STRATEGY.md) the north-star
for making the site useful to agents while sending qualified production intent
to Martini.

## Adding a server

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — easiest path is the
[submission form](../../issues/new?template=submit-mcp.yml). A maintainer
verifies it against primary sources before it is listed — a submission is a
claim, never an instruction.

## Who's behind it

Maintained by the team behind [Martini](https://www.martini.film), the film set
for AI videos — whose MCP server is the featured listing, clearly disclosed.
Everything else is ranked on merit: the directory is a community service and
its only asset is trust. MIT licensed.

name: 3D New Era AI

readme.markdown:
# 3D New Era AI

**English** · [Português (Brasil)](README.pt-BR.md) · **[Website](https://3dneweraai.com/?lang=en)** · **[Try it in the browser](https://3dneweraai.com/app/)**

An open-source **home design, floor plan and interior design editor** written in Rust,
built so that **your AI can design with you**. It ships with a
[Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server: Claude, ChatGPT, Codex,
Gemini, Cursor or any other MCP client draws the walls, furnishes the rooms, builds the
joinery, checks lighting and ergonomics against real standards and renders the photos,
while every change shows up live on screen and is one Ctrl+Z away.

A Sweet Home 3D alternative for Windows, macOS, Linux and the browser, in English,
Portuguese, Spanish and French.

## Three ways to use it

| | What you get | Account |
|---|---|---|
| **[Desktop app](#install)** | The full editor on your machine, with a local MCP server at `127.0.0.1:7878`. Nothing leaves your computer. | none |
| **[Browser editor](https://3dneweraai.com/app/)** | The same editor in a tab (WebGPU or WebGL). Switch on its MCP and your AI edits the tab's project. | none |
| **[Hosted connector](https://3dneweraai.com/connector/)** | Add `https://mcp.3dneweraai.com/mcp` to Claude or ChatGPT and design from the chat, with projects kept in your account. | email sign-in |

The desktop app and the browser editor are free, open source and need no account. The
hosted connector is free within a quota; see [pricing](https://3dneweraai.com/pricing/).

## Install

**Windows** — in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leandrodaf/3d-new-era-ai/main/scripts/install-windows.ps1 | iex
```

**macOS** (Apple Silicon and Intel) — in Terminal:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leandrodaf/3d-new-era-ai/main/scripts/install-macos.sh | bash
```

or with Homebrew: `brew install --cask leandrodaf/tap/3d-new-era-ai`.

The installers work for your user only, with no administrator password: the app appears
in the Start menu or Launchpad, `newera` goes on your `PATH`, the MCP server is registered
in Claude Code and Codex if you have them, and running the same command again updates it.
Uninstall with `install-macos.sh --uninstall`, or from *Settings → Apps* on Windows.

Prefer a plain download?

| [Windows (x64)](https://github.com/leandrodaf/3d-new-era-ai/releases/latest/download/newera-windows-x64.zip) | [macOS Apple Silicon](https://github.com/leandrodaf/3d-new-era-ai/releases/latest/download/newera-macos-apple-silicon.zip) | [macOS Intel](https://github.com/leandrodaf/3d-new-era-ai/releases/latest/download/newera-macos-intel.zip) | [Linux (x64)](https://github.com/leandrodaf/3d-new-era-ai/releases/latest/download/newera-linux-x64.tar.gz) |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|

<details>
<summary>First launch of a plain download</summary>

The builds are not signed with a paid Apple or Microsoft certificate, so the system asks
once:

- **Windows:** unzip and open `newera-gui.exe`; if SmartScreen appears, click
  *More info* → *Run anyway*.
- **macOS:** unzip and move *3D New Era AI* to Applications, then right-click it →
  *Open* → *Open*. On macOS 15 and later, open it once, then go to *System Settings* →
  *Privacy & Security* → *Open Anyway*, or run
  `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/3D New Era AI.app"`.
- **Linux:** `tar xzf newera-linux-x64.tar.gz && ./newera/newera`. Run
  `./newera/install-desktop.sh` to add the menu entry, the icon and the `.newera` file
  type (`--uninstall` undoes it).

The one-line installers skip these prompts.
</details>

## Connect your AI

**Hosted, nothing to install.** In Claude or ChatGPT, add a custom connector with the
address `https://mcp.3dneweraai.com/mcp` and sign in with your email. Step by step:
<https://3dneweraai.com/connector/>.

**With the desktop app.** The editor serves MCP at `http://127.0.0.1:7878/mcp` while it is
open (or run `newera serve` for no window). The **AI** menu, or the MCP chip in the status
bar, shows the snippet for your client, can register it for you, and lists the tools the
agent calls as it calls them.

**From a browser tab.** Open <https://3dneweraai.com/app/> and switch the MCP on in the
**AI** panel (Ctrl+Shift+M). The tab gets an address your AI can reach through a small
relay, because a tab cannot listen on a port. The relay passes messages and stores
nothing; the project stays in the tab, and the address stops answering when you switch it
off or close the tab. Treat that address like a password. Video rendering is not offered
there, since it would hold the tab for minutes.

Then just ask, for example: *"Draw a 4 × 5 m bedroom with a door and a window, furnish it
and render a photo."*

### Client setup

One click, with the app installed:

**Claude Desktop:** download `newera-mcp.mcpb` from the
[latest release](https://github.com/leandrodaf/3d-new-era-ai/releases/latest) and open it.

**Plugins with skills:**

| Client | Command |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `/plugin marketplace add leandrodaf/3d-new-era-ai`, then `/plugin install 3d-new-era-ai-desktop@3d-new-era-ai` (the app on your screen) or `/plugin install 3d-new-era-ai@3d-new-era-ai` (hosted) |
| Codex | `codex plugin marketplace add leandrodaf/3d-new-era-ai` |
| Gemini CLI | `gemini extensions install https://github.com/leandrodaf/3d-new-era-ai` |

<details>
<summary>Manual setup for each client</summary>

**Claude Code** (already set up inside a clone of this repository by `.mcp.json`)

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http newera http://127.0.0.1:7878/mcp
```

**Codex CLI**

```sh
codex mcp add newera --url http://127.0.0.1:7878/mcp
```

**Gemini CLI**

```sh
gemini mcp add --transport http newera http://127.0.0.1:7878/mcp
```

**VS Code (Copilot agent mode)**

```sh
code --add-mcp '{"name":"newera","type":"http","url":"http://127.0.0.1:7878/mcp"}'
```

**Cursor** — `~/.cursor/mcp.json`

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "newera": { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:7878/mcp" } } }
```

*

…

name: Fyreflock
description: Talk to a real, verified person and play 25 games together, right inside your AI chat.

readme.markdown:
Fyreflock for Claude, ChatGPT and Claude Code Ask your assistant to find you someone. A real, verified person texts back in the same window, and you can play Connect 4, Battleship or 23 other games together without leaving the chat. Your assistant only carries the words, exactly as you typed them. No bots, ever. Early access: everything is free, filters included, and every month four early users win an award. Every AI chat is a room with one person in it. Fyreflock puts a second person in that room: a real one, who passed a camera check, picked at random, there for the same reason you are. You stay in Claude or ChatGPT. They might be in a browser, in ChatGPT, or in their own Claude. Your assistant is the courier, and it is held to that. Real box, two real accounts, real time. From "find me someone" to a won game of Connect 4 in about fifteen seconds. ## Try it in sixty seconds 1. **Add Fyreflock to your assistant.** The connector URL is `https://fyreflock.com/mcp`. Host-by-host steps are [just below](#set-it-up). 2. **Sign in once and press Allow.** A browser tab opens, you sign in or sign up, and you are sent straight back. New here? The same page signs you up, camera check and all. 3. **Say "find me someone to talk to".** The Fyreflock box opens right there in the conversation. Say "next" for somebody else, "leave" to stop. > [!TIP] > Nobody around yet? Press **Play** while you wait and take on the computer. The search keeps its place, and the box switches to the conversation the moment somebody arrives. ## Set it up
Claude (claude.ai and Claude Desktop) 1. Settings → **Connectors** → **Add custom connector**. 2. Paste `https://fyreflock.com/mcp` and save. 3. The first time you ask for someone, Claude opens fyreflock.com: sign in, press **Allow**, done. The chat box appears inline in the conversation. It survives you switching to other chats; your lines wait, and the box picks them up when you come back. It follows your assistant's theme.
ChatGPT 1. Settings → **Plugins** → **Add custom MCP server**. 2. Server URL `https://fyreflock.com/mcp`, authentication **OAuth**. 3. Ask for someone; sign in and press **Allow** when the page opens.
Claude Code (this repo is the plugin) ``` /plugin marketplace add FuloxDev/fyreflock-claude /plugin install fyreflock@fyreflock ``` Restart Claude Code and say **find me someone**. The first time, Claude Code opens fyreflock.com in your browser: sign in or sign up, press **Allow**, and you are back in the terminal, connected. No token to copy. It is a plugin rather than a bare `claude mcp add` line for one reason: **the hooks**. They turn "your assistant sends your words unchanged" from a request into something that is actually checked, every message. Do not also run `claude mcp add` for Fyreflock: two registrations means two servers, duplicate tools, and hooks that only cover one of them. Details in [How it stays honest](#how-it-stays-honest) and [The pane](#the-pane-talk-without-the-model-in-the-path).
VS Code (Copilot agent mode) Or add it by hand to `mcp.json`: ```json { "servers": { "fyreflock": { "type": "http", "url": "https://fyreflock.com/mcp" } } } ``` Sign-in happens in your browser on first use.
Any other MCP client Remote server, Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, client metadata documents and dynamic registration both accepted: ``` https://fyreflock.com/mcp ``` If your client cannot sign in by itself, create a token under **Settings** on fyreflock.com and send it as `Authorization: Bearer `.
## What you can do from your assistant | | | |---|---| | 💬 **Talk to a stranger** | One real person at a time, matched on region and the interests you share. "next" moves on, "leave" ends it. | | 🎮 **Play while you talk** | 25 games right inside the box: Connect 4, Battleship, Liar's Dice, Checkers, Reversi, Would You Rather and more. The server referees, so neither player, and neither assistant, can peek at a hidden board or hand. Nobody around? Play the computer while you wait. | | 🪺 **Roosts** | Your own circle, invite link only. Read and post in Roosts that let assistants in. | | 📹 **Take it to video** | Invite the person you are texting to a video call; it opens in your browser, no token, no new account. | | 🧭 **Filters and interests** | Set what you are into and who you want to meet. During early access every filter is free too. | | 🏆 **Monthly awards** | Every month four early users win an award badge and six months of premium for when paid features launch. [See the awards](https://fyreflock.com/awards). | | 🛡️ **The door that opens** | Block, report with the evidence attached, add to your Nest if you both want to talk again. Every exit works the first time. | ## How it stays honest - **Every match is a real person.** Every account passed a camera check in a browser before it could meet anyone. There is no bot in the queue and never will be. 18+ only. - **They know.** The other person's card says you are talking from inside an assistant, so nobody is fooled about where the words came from. - **Your words, verbatim.** The assistant is instructed to send your message exactly as typed. In Claude Code the plugin's hooks refuse any send that is not the line you wrote this turn. Rewording, shortening, "fixing" and inventing are all blocked. - **You can check.** The companion tab at [fyreflock.com/app/live](https://fyreflock.com/app/live) shows what was actually sent and received, with no model involved. - **It survives you looking away.** Switch to another chat, close the window, come back: your search keeps its place in line, your conversation keeps its lines …
